lam rim gyi chos skor/

d.b: Part 1: The Stages of the Path

f.d: @#/ /lam rim nyams mgur bzhugs so//(lam rim bsdus don/)

b.i: Essential Points of the Stages of the Path

f.d: rje tsong kha pa chen po/
Tsongkhapa Losang Drakpa
@#/ /phun tshogs dge legs bye bas bskrun pa'i sku/ / mtha' yas 'gro ba'i re ba skong ba'i gsung / / ma lus shes bya ji bzhin gzigs pa'i thugs/ / shAkya'i gtso bo de la mgos phyag 'tshal//[1]

1 Your body is created from a billion perfect factors of goodness, your speech fulfills the yearnings of countless sentient beings, your mind perceives all objects of knowledge exactly as they are. O chief of Śākya clan, I bow my head to you.
zla med ston pa de yi sras kyi mchog / rgyal ba'i mdzad pa kun gyi khur bsnams nas/ / grangs med zhing du sprul pas rnam rol pa/ / mi pham 'jam pa'i dbyangs la phyag 'tshal lo//[2]

2 You’re the most excellent sons of such a peerless teacher, you carry the burden of the enlightened activities of all conquerors, and in countless realms you engage in ecstatic display of emanations. O Maitreya and Mañjuśrī, I pay homage to you.
shin tu dpag par dka' ba rgyal ba'i yum/ / ji bzhin dgongs pa 'grel mdzad 'dzam gling rgyan/ / klu sgrub thogs med ces ni sa gsum na/ / yongs su grags pa'i zhabs la bdag phyag 'tshal//[3]

3 So difficult to fathom is the Mother of Conquerors;[131] you who unravel its content as it is are the jewels of the world, hailed with renown throughout the three realms. O Nāgārjuna and Asaṅga, I pay homage to you.

d.div: [131] The Mother of Conquerors is the Perfection of Wisdom sutras, scriptures key to the Mahayana teaching on emptiness.

f.d: shing rta chen po gnyis nas legs brgyud pa'i/ / zab mo lta ba rgya chen spyod pa'i lam/ / ma nor yongs su rdzogs pa'i gnad bsdus pa'i/ / gdams pa'i mdzod 'dzin mar me mdzad la 'dud//[4]

4 Excellently stemming from these two great trailblazers are the two paths of profound view and vast practice. The custodian of this treasury of instructions, preserving all key points of these paths without error, O Dīpaṃkara [Atiśa], I pay homage to you.
rab 'byams gsung rab kun la lta ba'i mig / skal bzang thar par bgrod pa'i 'jug ngogs mchog / brtse bas bskyod pa'i thabs mkhas mdzad pa yi/ / gsal mdzad bshes gnyen rnams gus phyag 'tshal//[5]

5 You are the eyes for seeing the myriad collections of scripture, you are the supreme gateway for fortunate ones voyaging to liberation, stirred by compassion you illuminate the most skillful approaches. O spiritual teachers, respectfully, I pay homage to you.
'dzam gling mkhas pa yongs kyi gtsug gi rgyan/ / snyan pa'i ba dan 'gro na lhang nge ba/ / klu sgrub thogs med gnyis las rim bzhin du/ / legs brgyud byang chub lam gyi rim pa ni//[6]

6 This [instruction on the] stages of the path to enlightenment flowed excellently in succession from Nāgārjuna and Asaṅga, crown jewels of all the learned ones of this world. Your banners of fame flutter vibrantly among sentient beings.
skye dgu'i 'dod don ma lus skong bas na/ / gdams pa rin chen dbang gi rgyal po ste/ / gzhung bzang stong gi chu bo 'du ba'i phyir/ / dpal ldan legs par bshad pa'i rgya mtsho'ang yin//[7]

7 Among instructions, it is the most precious of all gems, fulfilling all the wishes of beings without exception. It is also the ocean of the most glorious well-uttered insights, the confluence of a thousand rivers of excellent treatises.
bstan pa thams cad 'gal med rtogs pa dang / / gsung rab ma lus gdams par 'char ba dang / / rgyal ba'i dgongs pa bde blag rnyed pa dang / / nyes spyod chen po'i g.yang sa las kyang bsrungs/[1] /[8]

8 It helps you see all teachings as free of contradiction, it helps all scriptures dawn on you as personal instructions, it helps you easily discover the enlightened intention of the conquerors, and it helps protect you from the abyss of grave negative deeds.

d.div: [1] bsrung / zhol/

f.d: de phyir rgya bod mkhas pa'i skye bo ni/ / skal ldan du mas bsten pa'i gdams pa mchog / skyes bu gsum gyi lam gyi rim pa yis/ / yid rab mi 'phrog dpyod ldan su zhig yod//[9]

9 Therefore this most excellent instruction, relied upon by countless fortunate ones like the learned ones of India and Tibet, this teaching on the stages of the path of persons of three capacities: [4] what intelligent person would not be captivated by it?
gsung rab kun gyi snying po bsdu bsdu ba/ / tshul 'di thun re ston dang nyan pas kyang / / dam chos 'chad dang thos pa'i phan yon tshogs/ / rlabs chen sdud par nges pas de don bsam//[10]

10 This concise instruction that distills the essence of all scriptures — through reciting it or listening to it for even a single session, you will definitely receive powerful waves of merit of teaching and hearing the Dharma; so contemplate its meaning.

de nas 'di phyi'i legs tshogs ji snyed pa'i/ / rten 'brel legs par 'grig pa'i rtsa ba ni/ / lam ston bshes gnyen dam pa 'bad pa yis/ / bsam dang sbyor bas tshul bzhin bsten pa ru/ /[11] mthong nas srog gi phyir yang mi gtong bar/ / bka' bzhin bsgrub pa'i mchod pas mnyes par byed/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo/ /[12]

11–12 The root of creating well the auspicious conditions for all the good things of this and future lives is to rely properly, with effort in both thought and action, on the sublime spiritual teacher who reveals the path. Seeing this, never forsake him, even at the cost of your life, and please him with the offering of following his advice. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.[132]

d.div: [132] The last two lines of this pair of verses appear as a refrain at the end of every key topic in the stages of the path instruction. I have rendered this refrain as it appears in Tsongkhapa’s original. The tradition among Geluk practitioners, especially when chanting this text, is to modify the refrain as “The exalted lama practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.”

f.d: dal ba'i rten 'di yid bzhin nor las lhag/ / 'di 'dra rnyed pa da res tsam zhig yin/ / rnyed dka' 'jig sla nam mkha'i glog dang 'dra/ / tshul 'di bsams nas 'jig rten bya ba kun/ /[13] sbun pa 'phyar ba bzhin du rtogs 'gyur nas/ / nyin mtshan kun tu snying po len pa dgos/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo/ /[14]

13–14 This life of leisure is far more precious than a wish-granting jewel; finding such an existence happens just once. Hard to find, and yet, like a flash of lightning, it easily vanishes. Contemplating this, you must see all mundane pursuits like empty grain husks floating on the wind, and you must extract the essence of your human life. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

shi nas ngan 'gror mi skye'i gdengs med cing / / de yi 'jigs skyob dkon mchog gsum du nges/ / de phyir skyabs 'gro shin tu brtan pa dang / / de yi bslab bya nyams pa med par bya/ /[15] de yang dkar nag las 'bras legs bsams nas/ / blang dor tshul bzhin bsgrub la rag las so/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo/ /[16]

15–16 There is no certainty you will elude birth in the lower realms after death; protection from such terror lies in the Three Jewels alone. Make firm therefore the practice of going for refuge, and ensure that its precepts are never eroded. This depends in turn on fully contemplating white and black karma and their effects and on perfectly observing the ethical ideal. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

lam mchog sgrub la mtshan nyid tshang ba'i rten/ / ma rnyed bar du sa chod [2]mi 'ong bas/ / de yi ma tshang med pa'i rgyu la bslab/ / sgo gsum sdig ltung dri mas sbags pa 'di/ /[17] lhag par las sgrib sbyong ba gnad che bas/ / rgyun du stobs bzhi tshang bar bsten pa gces/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo/ /[18]

17–18 Until you’ve obtained the form best suited to the excellent path, you’ll fail to make great strides in your journey. Strive therefore to create all the causes for such a form. Your three doors, so sullied with negative karma and transgressions — it is especially vital to purify your karmic obscurations, so prioritize constant application of the four powers.[133] I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise. [5]

d.div: [2] sa phyod/ zhol/

[133] The four powers are (1) the power of reliance on the support, (2) the power of repudiation, (3) the power of the remedy, which is engaging the antidotes, and (4) the power of resolve to turn away from the fault henceforth. Together these four constitute an effective method for purifying negative karma. For a detailed explanation of these powers, see pages 91 and 396.

f.d: sdug bden nyes dmigs bsam la ma 'bad na/ / thar pa don gnyer ji bzhin mi skye zhing / / kun 'byung 'khor ba'i 'jug rim ma bsams na/ / 'khor ba'i rtsa ba gcod tshul mi shes pas//[19] srid las nges 'byung skyo shas brtan [3] pa dang / / 'khor ba gang gis bcings pa shes pa gces// rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[ 20]

19–20 Without striving to contemplate the ailment, the truth of suffering, a genuine aspiration for liberation does not arise; without contemplating the causal process of suffering’s origin, the way to uproot cyclic existence is not understood. Thus it’s vital to prioritize seeking renunciation through disenchantment with cyclic existence and to recognize the links that chain you to samsara. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

d.div: [3] brten/ sku 'bum/

f.d: sems bskyed theg mchog lam gyi gzhung shing ste/ / rlabs chen spyod pa rnams kyi gzhi dang rten// tshogs gnyis kun la gser 'gyur rtsi lta bu/ / rab 'byams dge tshogs sdud pa'i bsod nams gter//[21] de ltar shes nas rgyal sras dpa' bo rnams/ / rin chen sems mchog thugs dam mthil du 'dzin// rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[22]

d.div: [134] The two accumulations (saṃbhāradvaya) are the accumulation of merit (puṇya) and the accumulation of wisdom (prajñā), both of which must be cultivated in tandem to advance along the path to enlightenment. These are often correlated to the six perfections of a bodhisattva that are outlined in what follows, where the perfections of generosity, ethics, forbearance, diligence, and meditative absorption are said to complete the accumulation of merit, and the perfection of wisdom is said to complete the accumulation of wisdom.

f.d: sbyin pa 'gro ba'i re skong yid bzhin nor/ / ser sna'i mdud pa gcod pa'i mtshon cha mchog / ma zhum snying stobs bskyed pa'i rgyal sras spyod/ / snyan pa'i grags pa phyogs bcur sgrog pa'i gzhi//[23] de ltar shes nas lus dang longs spyod dge / yongs su gtong ba'i lam bzang mkhas pas bsten/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[24]

tshul khrims nyes spyod dri ma 'khrud pa'i chu/ / nyon mongs tsha gdung sel ba'i zla ba'i 'od/ / skye dgu'i dbus na lhun po lta bur brjid/ / stobs kyis bsdigs pa med par 'gro kun 'dud//[25] de ltar shes nas yang dag blangs pa'i khrims/ / dam pa rnams kyis mig bzhin bsrung bar mdzad/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[26]

25–26 Morality is the water that cleanses the stains of ill deeds, the cooling moonlight soothing the burning agony of the afflictions. It dignifies you amid people like the majestic Mount Meru; it draws all beings to you with no display of power. Knowing this, sublime ones guard, as they would their own eyes, the perfect discipline they have adopted. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

bzod pa stobs ldan rnams la rgyan gyi mchog/ / nyon mongs gdung ba'i dka' thub kun gyi phul/ / zhe sdang lag 'gro'i dgra la nam mkha' lding / / tshig rtsub mtshon la sra ba'i go cha yin//[27] de ltar shes nas bzod mchog go cha la/ / rnam pa sna tshogs tshul gyis goms par mdzad/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[28]

mi bzlog brtan pa'i brtson 'grus go bgos na/ / lung rtogs yon tan yar ngo'i zla bzhin 'phel/ / spyod lam thams cad don dang ldan par 'gyur/ / gang brtsams las kyi mtha' rnams yid bzhin 'grub//[29] de ltar shes nas le lo kun sel ba'i/ / rlabs chen brtson 'grus rgyal sras rnams kyi brtsams/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[30]

29–30 When you don the armor of dauntless diligence, knowledge of scripture and realization increases like the waxing moon. [6] Your conduct comes to be imbued with noble purpose, and whatever initiative you undertake succeeds. Knowing this, bodhisattvas expend great waves of effort, which helps to dispel all forms of laziness. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

bsam gtan sems la dbang bsgyur rgyal po ste/ / bzhag na g.yo med ri yi dbang po bzhin/ / btang na dge ba'i dmigs pa kun la 'jug / lus sems las su rung ba'i bde chen 'dren//[31] de ltar shes nas rnal 'byor dbang po rnams/ / rnam g.yeng dgra 'joms ting 'dzin rgyun du bsten/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[32]

31–32 Meditative absorption is the king that reigns over the mind. When at rest, it stands unwavering as the king of mountains; when engaged it takes up all objects of virtue. It induces the great bliss of a serviceable body and mind. Knowing this, great accomplished yogis ceaselessly apply concentrations, destroying the enemy distraction. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

shes rab zab mo'i de nyid lta ba'i mig/ / srid pa'i rtsa ba drungs nas 'byin pa'i lam/ / gsung rab kun las bsngags pa'i yon tan gter/ / gti mug mun sel sgron me mchog tu grags//[33] de ltar shes nas thar 'dod mkhas pa yi/ / lam 'di 'bad pa du mas bskyed par mdzad/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[34]

33–34 Wisdom is the eye that sees profound suchness, the path destroying cyclic existence at its root. It’s a treasury of higher qualities praised in all scriptures, hailed as the supreme lamp for dispelling the darkness of delusion. Knowing this, those who aspire to liberation strive with myriad endeavors to cultivate this path of the wise. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

rtse gcig bsam gtan tsam la 'khor ba yi/ / rtsa ba gcod pa'i nus pa ma mthong zhing / / zhi gnas lam dang bral ba'i shes rab kyis/ / ji tsam dpyad kyang nyon mongs mi ldog pas//[35] yin lugs phu thag chod pa'i shes rab de/ / g.yo med zhi gnas rta la bskyon nas ni/ / mtha' bral dbu ma'i rigs pa'i mtshon rnon gyis/ / mthar 'dzin dmigs gtad thams cad 'jig byed pa'i//[36] tshul bzhin dpyod pa'i yangs pa'i shes rab kyis/ / de nyid rtogs pa'i blo gros rgyas par mdzad/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[37]

35–37 The power to cut the root of cyclic existence is not found in one-pointed meditative absorption alone, and no amount of probing with wisdom divorced from the path of tranquil abiding will stop the afflictions. So saddling this wisdom decisively penetrating the true mode of being astride the horse of unwavering tranquil abiding, and with the sharp weapon of reasoning of the Middle Way free of extremes, tear down all sites of objectification of the mind grasping at extremes. With such expansive wisdom probing with precision, enhance your intellect so it realizes true suchness. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

rtse gcig goms pas ting 'dzin 'grub pa ni/ / smos par ci 'tshal tshul bzhin dpyod pa yi/ / so sor rtog pa yis kyang yin lugs la/ / g.yo med shin tu brtan par gnas pa yi//[38] ting 'dzin bskyed par mthong nas zhi lhag gnyis/ / zung 'brel sgrub la brtson rnams ya mtshan no/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[39]

38–39 What need is there to say that concentration is attained through one-pointedness? But discriminative awareness probing with precision can engender concentration too, abiding utterly stable and unwavering in the true mode of being. Wondrous are those who see this and strive to unite tranquil abiding and insight. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

mnyam bzhag nam mkha' lta bu'i stong nyid dang / / rjes thob sgyu ma lta bu'i stong pa gnyis/ / bsgoms nas thabs shes zung du 'brel ba yis/ / rgyal sras spyod pa'i pha rol 'gro ba bsngags//[40] de ltar rtogs nas phyogs re'i lam gyis ni/ / tshim pa med pa skal bzang rnams kyi lugs/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[41]

40–41 The space-like emptiness of meditative equipoise and the illusion-like emptiness of subsequent realization — praised are those who cultivate method and wisdom by binding them together, journeying beyond the bodhisattva deeds. Realizing this and not content with partial paths — this is indeed the way of the fortunate ones. [7] I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

de ltar rgyu dang 'bras bu'i theg chen gyi/ / lam mchog gnyis kar dgos pa'i thun mong lam/ / ji bzhin bskyed nas mkhas pa'i ded dpon gyi/ / mgon la brten nas rgyud sde rgya mtsho cher//[42] zhugs nas yongs rdzogs man ngag brten [4] pa des/ / dal 'byor thob pa don dang ldan par byas/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo//[43]

42–43 Having thus correctly cultivated the shared paths essential for the supreme paths of causal and resultant vehicles, enter the great ocean of tantras by relying on the counsel of learned guides. Through applying their quintessential instructions, make this human life you have obtained meaningful. I, a yogi, practiced in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should do likewise.

d.div: [4] bsten/ zhol/

f.d: rang gi yid la goms par bya phyir dang / / skal bzang gzhan la'ang phan par bya ba'i phyir/ / rgyal ba dgyes pa'i yongs su rdzogs pa'i lam/ / go sla'i ngag gis bshad pa'i dge ba des//[44] 'gro ba kun kyang rnam dag lam bzang dang / / 'bral med gyur cig ces ni smon lam 'debs/ / rnal 'byor ngas kyang smon lam de ltar btab/ / thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin 'debs 'tshal lo//[45]

44–45 To cultivate familiarity in my own mind and to also benefit fortunate others, I’ve explained here in words easily understood the complete path that pleases the conquerors. Thus I pray: “Through this virtue may all beings never be parted from the perfectly pure and excellent path.” I, a yogi, prayed in this manner; you who aspire to liberation should pray likewise.

zhes byang chub lam gyi rim pa'i nyams len gyi rnam gzhag mdor bsdus te brjed byang du byas pa 'di ni/ mang du thos pa'i dge slong spong ba pa blo bzang grags pa'i dpal gyis/ 'brog ri bo che dge ldan rnam par rgyal ba'i gling du sbyar ba'o// //

This brief presentation of the practices of the stages of the path to enlightenment, written in the form of a memorandum, was composed by the well-read monk the renunciant Losang Drakpai Pal at the great mountain retreat of Geden Nampar Gyalwai Ling. [8]
@#/ /lam gyi gtso bo rnam gsum bzhugs so//

d.b: 2. Three Principal Elements of the Path

f.d: rje tsong kha pa chen po/
Tsongkhapa Losang Drakpa
@#/ /rje btsun bla ma rnams la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to the most venerable gurus!
rgyal ba'i gsung rab kun gyi snying po'i don/ / rgyal sras dam pa rnams kyi bsngags pa'i lam/ / skal ldan thar 'dod rnams kyi 'jug ngogs de/ / ji ltar nus bzhin bdag gis bshad par bya//[ 1]

1 I shall explain here to the best of my ability the essential points of all the scriptures of the Conqueror, the path acclaimed by all excellent bodhisattvas, the gateway for fortunate ones aspiring to liberation.
gang dag srid pa'i bde la ma chags shing / / dal 'byor don yod bya phyir brtson pa yis/ / rgyal ba dgyes pa'i lam la yid rton pa'i/ / skal ldan de dag dang ba'i yid kyis nyon//[2]

2 You who are not attached to the joys of cyclic existence, who strive to make meaningful this life of leisure and opportunity, and who place your trust in the path that pleases the conquerors — O fortunate ones, open your hearts and listen.
rnam dag nges 'byung med par srid mtsho yi/ / bde 'bras don gnyer zhi ba'i thabs med la/ / srid la brkam pa yis kyang lus can rnams/ / kun nas 'ching phyir thog mar nges 'byung btsal//[3]

3 Without perfect renunciation you cannot pacify your yearning for the pleasures and fruits of samsara’s ocean. And the craving for existence keeps you thoroughly enchained, so you should first seek true renunciation.
dal 'byor rnyed dka' tshe la long med pa/ / yid la goms pas tshe 'di'i snang shas ldog / las 'bras mi slu 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal rnams/ / yang yang bsams na phyi ma'i snang shas ldog /[4]

4 By contemplating often that such a human life is rarely found and that you have no time to spare, preoccupation with this life will cease. By contemplating over and over the truth of karma and samsaric suffering, preoccupation with the next life will cease.
de ltar goms pas 'khor ba'i phun tshogs la/ / yid smon skad cig tsam yang mi skye zhing / / nyin mtshan kun tu thar pa don gnyer blo/ / byung na de tshe nges 'byung skyes pa lags//[5]

5 Having familiarized yourself in this way, when not even an instant of admiration arises for the treasures of cyclic existence, and when the thought that aspires to liberation arises both night and day, at this point true renunciation has arisen.
nges 'byung de yang rnam dag sems bskyed kyis/ / zin pa med na bla med byang chub kyi/ / phun tshogs bde ba'i rgyu ru mi 'gyur bas/ / blo ldan rnams kyis byang chub sems mchog bskyed//[6]

6 Furthermore, if such renunciation is not sustained by the perfect awakening mind, it will not become a condition for the perfect bliss of unsurpassed enlightenment. Therefore, intelligent ones, generate the supreme awakening mind.

shugs drag chu bo bzhi yi rgyun gyis khyer/ / bzlog dka' las kyi 'ching ba dam pos bsdams/ / bdag 'dzin lcags kyi dra ba'i sbubs su tshud/ / ma rig mun pa'i smag chen kun nas 'thibs//[7] mu med srid par skye zhing skye ba ru/ / sdug bsngal gsum gyis rgyun chad med par mnar/ / gnas skabs 'di 'drar gyur pa'i ma rnams kyi/ / ngang tshul bsams nas sems mchog bskyed par mdzod//[8]

7–8 Swept ever away by four powerful rivers, bound tightly with fetters of karma most secure, trapped in the iron mesh of self-grasping, enveloped by the thick mists of ignorance: they endlessly take birth within cyclic existence, ceaselessly tormented by the three kinds of suffering. Contemplating this condition of all your mothers, you must generate the supreme awakening mind.
gnas lugs rtogs pa'i shes rab mi ldan na/ / nges 'byung byang chub sems la goms byas kyang / / srid pa'i rtsa ba gcad [1] par mi nus pas/ / de phyir rten 'brel rtogs pa'i thabs la 'bad//[9]

9 Without the wisdom realizing the ultimate nature, though you gain familiarity with renunciation and the awakening mind, [10] you will be unable to cut the root of cyclic existence. So strive in the methods for realizing dependent origination.

d.div: [1] gcod/ zhol/

f.d: gang zhig 'khor 'das chos rnams thams cad kyi/ / rgyu 'bras nam yang slu ba med mthong zhing / / dmigs pa'i gtad so gang yin kun zhig pa/ / de ni sangs rgyas dgyes pa'i lam la zhugs//[10]

10 When, with respect to all phenomena of samsara and nirvana, you see that the laws of cause and effect never deceive, and when you have dismantled every basis of objectification, then you have entered the path that pleases the buddhas.
snang ba rten 'brel bslu ba med pa dang / / stong pa khas len bral ba'i go ba gnyis/ / ji srid so sor snang ba de srid du/ / da dung thub pa'i dgongs pa rtogs pa med//[11]

11 As long as the two understandings — of appearance, undeceiving dependent origination, and of emptiness, the absence of all positions — remain separate, then you have not realized the intent of the Sage.
nam zhig res 'jog med par cig car du/ / rten 'brel mi slur mthong ba tsam nyid nas/ / nges shes yul gyi 'dzin stangs kun 'jig na/ / de tshe lta ba'i dpyad pa rdzogs pa lags//[ 12]

12 However, if at some point, not in alternation but at once, the instant you see that dependent origination is undeceiving, this dismantles the entirety of the object of grasping at certitude,[135] then your analysis of the view is complete.

d.div: [135] This reading is based on Panchen Losang Yeshé’s Essence of Eloquence (55a4), where he interprets the Tibetan word nges shes in this line not as “ascertainment” but as “grasping at certitude.” Many other commentators, including the Fifth Dalai Lama and Tendar Lharam, read nges shes as “ascertainment,” thus making this line read as if this ascertainment dismantles entirely any grasping at the object.

f.d: gzhan yang snang bas yod mtha' sel ba dang / / stong pas med mtha' sel zhing stong pa nyid/ / rgyu dang 'bras bur 'char ba'i tshul shes na/ / mthar 'dzin lta bas 'phrog par mi 'gyur ro//[13]

13 Furthermore, when appearance dispels the extreme of existence and when emptiness dispels the extreme of nonexistence, and you understand how emptiness arises as cause and effect, you will never be swayed by views grasping at extremes.
de ltar lam gyi gtso bo rnam gsum gyi/ / gnad rnams rang gis ji bzhin rtogs pa'i tshe/ / dben pa bsten te brtson 'grus stobs bskyed nas/ / gtan gyi mdun [2] ma myur du sgrubs shig bu//[14]

14 Once you have thus understood as they are the key points of the three principal elements of the path, O child, seek solitude and, enhancing your power of diligence, swiftly accomplish your ultimate aim.

d.div: [2] 'dun/ sku 'bum/

f.d: zhes pa 'di ni mang du thos pa'i dge slong blo bzang grags pa'i dpal gyis/ tsha kho dbon po ngag dbang grags pa la gdams pa'o// //
This advice was given by the monk Losang Drakpai Pal to Ngawang Drakpa, a member of the ruling family of the Tsakho region.[136] [13]

d.div: [136] As this brief colophon says, this short text in verse was composed as advice to Tsakho Ngawang Drakpa. This figure was one of Tsongkhapa’s earliest disciples and served as the master’s attendant. The Tibetan word dbon po, which I have rendered here as “a member of the ruling family,” has multiple meanings. It can refer broadly to male members of a family on the father’s side, to a younger brother or nephew of a prominent person such as a local ruler, or to a male member of a ruling family.

f.d: lam rim legs gsungs nying khu/ @#/ /byang chub lam gyi rim pa nas 'byung ba'i nyams len gyi sgo rnam par nges pa legs gsungs kun gyi nying khu zhes bya ba bzhugs so//[1]

b.i: Well Ascertaining the Way to Practice Taught in the Stages of the Path to Enlightenment

d.div: [1] dwags po mkhan chen gyi lam rim legs gsungs nying khu 'di bzhin gzhung rang nyid kyi mtshan byang las gsal ba bzhin gtso bo rje tsong kha pa chen po'i byang chub lam rim chen mo'i nang nyams len gyi rim pa shin tu rgyas par gsungs pa rnams sdom gyi tshul du tshigs bcad du bsdebs pa'i legs bshad rmad du byung ba zhig tu snang ba ma zad/ nyams len pa rnams kyi'ang rgyun du ngag 'don du khyer chog pa'i lam rim khrid yig gal che ba zhig yin pas dge ldan pa'i mkhas grub rnams 'di lam rim khrid chen brgyad du grags pa'i nang brtsi'o/ / rje blo gros brtan pa'i sras kyi thu bo mkhan chen ngag dbang grags pa ni spyi lo dus rabs bco lnga'i stod du 'khrungs la/ ser byes grwa tshang du gzhung chen mor sbyangs pa mthar son par mdzad cing / rgyud smad grwa tshang gi khrir phebs pa ma tshad dwags po grwa tshang gi khri thog gnyis pa mdzad/ gsung rtsom la lam rim 'di dang «dri ba lhag bsam rab dkar» gyi lan sogs pod bzhi bzhugs/
[137] The work is customarily referred to as the Gomchen Lamrim.

f.d: dwags po sgom chen ngag dbang grags pa/
Translated by Rosemary Patton with Venerable Dagpo Rinpoché
@#/ /bla ma dam pa rnams la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to the perfect gurus![138]

d.div: [138] The author’s principal guru was Jé Lodrö Tenpa (1404–78), the founder of Dakpo Shedrup Ling Monastery and the sixth successor to Jé Tsongkhapa on the throne of Ganden.
bslab gsum lung rtogs mdzad pa'i khyad par gyis/ / rgyal ba'i dgongs pa ji bzhin 'dzin nus pa'i/ / slob dpon chen po de yi rjes zhugs nas/ / mdo sngags lam gyi rim pa nyams su blang //[1]

1 His excellent practice of the three trainings — [the teaching] both as scripture and realization — has given him the capacity to uphold the Buddha’s thought unerringly. Relying on this great spiritual teacher, I will practice the stages of the paths of sutra and tantra.

f.d: 'dir byang chub lam gyi rim pa'i khrid la bzhi/ mdzad pa po'i che ba dang / chos kyi che ba dang / chos la nyan bshad ji ltar bya ba dang / gdams pa dngos kyis slob ma ji ltar bkri ba'i rim pa'o/ /

This explanation of the stages of the path to enlightenment has four sections:[139] the greatness of the author, the greatness of the [lamrim] teaching, how to listen to and explain the teaching, and how students are progressively guided by the actual teaching.

d.div: [139] Gomchen’s original work is entirely in verse. The outline was added when it was first printed near the turn of the nineteenth century by Döndrup Wangyal of Dakpo Shedrup Ling, the author’s monastery. The outline is drawn from Jé Tsongkhapa’s Middle-Length Treatise on the Stages of the Path. Verse numbers were added to the 2005 Tibetan edition by the Institute of Tibetan Classics, and the numbering has been revised slightly in this translation.

f.d: [mdzad pa po'i che ba ]
1. [the greatness of the author]
dang po ni gzhan du shes par bya'o/ /
For the first, refer to other works.
gnyis pa chos kyi che ba
2. The Greatness of the [Lamrim] Teaching
['di ]la bzhi las/
This has four parts.
dang po bstan pa thams cad 'gal med du rtogs pa'i che ba ni/
2.1. The greatness of allowing you to realize that all the Teachings are free of contradictions

d.div: theg pa gsum gyi spangs rtogs rigs mtha' dag / lam gyi gtso bo yan lag ci rigs par/ / 'dir gcig 'tshang rgya'i lam du go ba ni/ / bstan pa thams cad 'gal med rtogs pa'o//[2]

2 Understanding that everything taught in the three vehicles about what is to be rejected and realized is a method for any given individual to achieve buddhahood, either as a primary path or an auxiliary one, is realizing that all the teachings are free of contradictions.

f.d: gnyis pa gsung rab thams cad gdams ngag tu 'char ba'i che ba ni/
2.2. The greatness of allowing you to recognize all discourses as practical instructions

d.div: dam pa'i man ngag la brten gsung rab ni/ / mtha' dag don la nges pa rnyed byas te/ / dpyad dang 'jog sgom nyams len rim pa [2] mkhas/ / chos spong drungs 'byin gsung rab gdams par 'char//[3]

3 By relying on precious personal instructions, once you have ascertained the content of all the Buddha’s discourses and become skilled in knowing which practices require analytical meditation and which require placement meditation, you cease to reject the teaching, and the discourses dawn as practical instructions.
[2] rim par/ rda sa shes dpar/

f.d: gsum pa rgyal ba'i dgongs pa bde blag tu rnyed pa'i che ba ni/
2.3. The greatness of allowing you to easily master the Buddha’s principles

d.div: gzhung lugs che rnams gdams pa'i mchog yin kyang / / ma sbyangs blo yis dgongs pa rnyed dka' zhing / / rnyed kyang yun ring tshegs che la ltos tshe/ / 'di las rgyal ba'i dgongs pa bde blag rtogs//[4]

4 Although the great treatises are the finest instructions, it is difficult for an untrained mind relying on them to master the Buddha’s intent, or doing it requires much time and great effort, while with this instruction you can easily realize it. [14]

f.d: bzhi pa nyes spyod chen po rang 'gags su 'gro ba'i che ba ni/
2.4. The greatness of automatically avoiding very serious misdeeds

d.div: de phyir rgyal ba'i bka' la 'tshang rgya ba'i/ / gegs dang thabs kyi rim pa gnyis brtags nas/ / legs gsungs 'dor ba gdams pa 'dis spong bas/ / nyes spyod chen po rang 'gags nyid du 'gyur//[5]

5 Thus, thanks to this instruction, you cease to forsake the excellent discourses — imagining some of the Buddha’s words to be obstacles to attaining buddhahood and others to be methods conducive to it — and thereby automatically avoid grave misdeeds.

f.d: gsum pa chos la nyan bshad ji ltar bya ba
3. How to listen to and explain the teaching
['di ]la gsum/ nyan pa'i tshul/ bshad pa'i tshul/ mjug tu thun mong du bya ba'i tshul lo/ /
This has three parts: how to listen to the teaching, how to explain the teaching, and the way to conclude common to both [teacher and student].
dang po nyan pa'i tshul
3.1. How to listen to the teaching
['di ]la gsum/ chos thos pa'i phan yon bsam pa/ chos dang chos smra ba la rim gro bskyed pa/ nyan tshul dngos so/ /
This has three parts: contemplating the benefits of listening to the teaching, serving and honoring the teaching and spiritual teachers, and how to actually listen.
dang po chos thos pa'i phan yon bsam pa ni/
3.1.1. Contemplating the benefits of listening to the teaching

d.div: gang zhig 'di thos yid ni dad gyur nas/ / legs par dga' la brtan pa nyid du 'gyur/ / shes rab skye zhing gti mug med 'gyur bas/ / rang gi shas kyang 'di ni nyo ba'i rigs//[3] [6]

6 “The mind of all those who hear it is filled with faith. You delight [in spiritual practice] and are constant in it. Your wisdom grows and your ignorance ceases. Thus it is worth buying even with your own flesh.”[140]
[3] sde dge_4150_bstan/ skyes rabs/ hu'aphags pa dpa' bo/ skyes pa'i rabs kyi rgyud/ skyes rabs so gnyis pa/ shog_121_ba7_rang gis shes kyang de nyid nyo par rigs//
[140] Āryaśūra, Garland of Birth Stories (Jātakamālā), chap. 32, Toh 4150 Tengyur, skyes rab, hu, 121b7.

f.d: gnyis pa chos dang chos smra ba la rim gro bskyed pa ni/
3.1.2. Serving and honoring the teaching and spiritual teachers

d.div: gcig tu dad cing gus pas chos nyan gyis/ / khengs dang chos dang chos smra khyad gsod bral/ / rim gro bskyed sogs gus par bya ba ni/ / sangs rgyas 'dra bar de la 'du shes bskyed//[4] [7]

7 “Listen to the teaching with complete faith and reverence, free of pride and scorn for the teaching and the teachers; cultivate respect for them — serving and honoring them and so on — and consider the spiritual teachers as you do the Buddha.”[141]
[4] sde dge_239_bka'/ mdo sde/ zha_sa'i snying po 'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 7_shog_223_na5
[141] Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sutra, (Daśacakrakṣitigarbhasūtra), chap. 7, Toh 239 Kangyur, mdo sde, zha, 223a5.

f.d: gsum pa nyan tshul dngos
3.1.3. How to actually listen
['di ]la gnyis/ 'du shes drug bsten pa dang / snod kyi skyon gsum spang ba'o/ /
This has two parts: cultivating the six recognitions and removing three faults like a vessel’s.
dang po 'du shes drug bsten pa ni/
3.1.3.1. Cultivating the six recognitions

d.div: rang la nad pa chos smra la sman pa/ / chos la sman dang nan tan la nad 'tsho/ / de bzhin gshegs la skyes bu dam pa dang / / chos tshul ring du gnas pa'i 'du shes bskyed//[8]

8 Generate the recognitions: yourself as a patient, the spiritual teachers as physicians, the Dharma as medicine, its steady practice as a treatment, the tathāgatas as superior beings, and [the wish for] the teaching to remain a long time.

f.d: gnyis pa snod kyi skyon gsum spang ba ni/
3.1.3.2. Removing three faults like a vessel’s

d.div: kha bub zhabs rdol dri ma'i skyon spangs te/ / legs par rab tu nyon la yid la 'dzin/ / mdor na sangs rgyas 'grub pa'i rgyu tshogs dang / / thos pa'i phan yon dran te spro bas nyan//[9]

9 Dispel the faults like a vessel that is overturned, pierced, or soiled. Listen very well, and remember what you hear. In brief, while mindful of all the causes of buddhahood’s attainment and the benefits of hearing, take delight in listening.

f.d: gnyis pa chos bshad pa'i tshul
3.2. How to explain the teaching
['di ]la bzhi/ chos bshad pa'i phan yon bsam pa/ ston pa dang chos la rim gro bskyed pa/ bsam pa dang sbyor ba ji lta bus bshad pa/ yul gang la bshad pa dang mi bshad pa'i khyad par ro/ /

This has four parts: contemplating the benefits of explaining the teaching, serving and honoring the Teacher and the teaching, [15] the attitude and behavior with which to teach, and differentiating whom to teach from whom not to teach.
dang po chos bshad pa'i phan yon bsam pa ni/
3.2.1. Contemplating the benefits of explaining the teaching

d.div: rnyed bkur blta sogs nyon mongs can sems dang / / log bshad spangs te mdo sogs ji bzhin ston/ / lhag bsam bskul dang [5] drag shul can zhus las/[6] / phan yon dpag med gsungs pa 'di yis 'dzin//[10]

10 While rejecting consideration for gain, honor, and the like, as well as afflictive thoughts[142] and incorrect explanations, teach [as the Buddha] taught the sutras and so on, and you will gain the countless benefits disclosed in Invoking the Altruistic Resolve and Questions of the Householder Ugra.[143]
[5] sde dge_69_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca_lhag bsam bskul ba'i mdo/ bam po+o/ 1_shog_135_ba1
[6] sde dge_63_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga_drag shul can gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 3_shog_279_na7
[142] This refers to thoughts affected by afflictions (Skt. kleśa) such as aversion, attachment, or ignorance.
[143] Respectively, Adhyāśayasañcodana, Toh 69 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ca, 135b1, and Gṛhapati-ugraparipṛcchā, Toh 63 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ca, 279a7.

f.d: gnyis pa ston pa dang chos la rim gro bskyed pa ni/
3.2.2. Serving and honoring the teacher and the teaching

d.div: rgyal yum gsungs tshe ston pas nyid gdan bshams/ / chos ni sangs rgyas rnams kyis bkur ba yi/ / zhing yin de phyir chos dang ston pa yi/ / yon tan bka' drin dran te gus pa bskyed//[11]

11 When he taught the Mother of Conquerors, the Teacher prepared his own seat, since for the buddhas the teaching is to be cherished.[144] Recall therefore the good qualities and the kindness of the teaching and the Teacher and generate reverence for them.
[144] Before teaching the Perfection of Wisdom, the Buddha set up a throne and circumambulated it three times to honor not himself but the teaching he was about to give.

f.d: gsum pa bsam pa dang sbyor ba ji lta bus bshad pa
3.2.3. The attitude and behavior with which to teach
['di ]la gnyis/ bsam pa dang sbyor ba'o/ /
This has two parts: attitude and behavior.
dang po bsam pa ni/
3.2.3.1. Attitude

d.div: dpe mkhyud bdag nyid sgrog dang 'chad pas ngal/ / gzhan skyon gleng dang phyi bshol phrag dog spang / / 'khor la byams bsgoms 'du shes lngas zin pas/ / tshul bzhin bstan dge [7] bde ba'i yo byad bsam//[12]

12 Abstain from withholding information, bragging, weariness with teaching, criticizing others, procrastination, and jealousy. Cultivate love for your followers and maintain the five recognitions.[145] See the virtue of teaching correctly as the means for your happiness.
[7] bstan dag_rda sa shes dpar/

[145] Tsongkhapa, citing the Questions of Sāgaramati, lists these five recognitions in his Middle-Length Treatise (trans., 27): viewing yourself as a physician, the Dharma as the medicine, listeners as patients, and tathāgatas as superior beings, along with wishing for the teaching to remain for a long time.

f.d: gnyis pa sbyor ba ni/
3.2.3.2. Behavior

d.div: khrus sogs gtsang sbra sngon 'gro bzang po yi/ / khri stan la 'dug zab mo'i gzungs bzlas te/ / bzhin gyi mdangs gsal dpe don rnam nges pas/ / lung dang gtan tshigs du mas dam chos ston//[13]

13 Once you have prepared yourself well, washed, and so on, sit on a throne and pronounce the profound dhāraṇī. With a friendly demeanor, confident of the meanings and illustrations, expound the excellent teaching using ample citations and reasoning.

f.d: bzhi pa yul gang la bshad pa dang mi bshad pa'i khyad par ni/
3.2.4. Differentiating whom to teach from whom not to teach

d.div: nyan pa'i kun spyod 'dul ba ji bzhin dang / / gsol nas 'chad cing snod ldan du shes na/ / ma gsol bar yang 'chad pa'i dmigs bsal gsungs//

14 Having been so requested, teach those whose behavior, when they listen, accords with the Vinaya; when you know that they are worthy recipients, it is taught that exceptionally you may teach when unsolicited.

f.d: gsum pa mjug tu thun mong du bya ba'i tshul ni/
3.3. The way to conclude common to both [teacher and student]

d.div: de nas bshad nyan dge ba rdzogs byang bsngo//[14]

de lta'i tshul gyis thun re'i bshad nyan la'ang / / phan yon dpag med gsungs rnams ji bzhin 'byung / / bshad nyan lam du gtong ba'i gnad 'di ni/ / sngon 'gro'i gdams pa mchog yin gces par bzung //[15]
Next, dedicate the virtue of teaching and listening to consummate enlightenment.

15 In this way, every time you teach or listen, you will gain the innumerable benefits that are taught. Cherish this important advice that ensures successful teaching and listening, for it is the foremost instruction on the preliminaries. [16]

f.d: lam gyi rtsa ba bshes gnyen bsten pa'i tshul/
bzhi pa gdams pa dngos kyis slob ma ji ltar bkri ba'i rim pa
4. How students are progressively guided by the actual teaching
['di ]la gnyis/ lam gyi rtsa ba bshes gnyen bsten pa'i tshul dang / bsten nas blo ji ltar sbyang ba'i rim pa'o/ /
This has two parts: how to rely on spiritual teachers, the root of the path, and while relying on them, how to progressively train your mind.
dang po lam gyi rtsa ba bshes gnyen bsten pa'i tshul
4.1. How to rely on spiritual teachers, the root of the path
['di ]la gnyis/ nges pa bskyed tshul spros te bshad pa/ skyong tshul mdor bstan pa'o/ /
This has two parts: a detailed explanation to ascertain [the topic] and a brief explanation for meditational purposes.
dang po nges pa bskyed tshul spros te bshad pa
4.1.1. A detailed explanation to ascertain [the topic]

['di ]la drug /bsten bya dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi mtshan nyid/ bsten byed slob ma'i mtshan nyid/ des de ji ltar bsten pa'i tshul/ bsten pa'i phan yon/ ma bsten pa'i nyes dmigs/ de dag gi don bsdu ba'o/ /

This has six parts: the defining characteristics of the spiritual teachers on whom to rely, the defining characteristics of the students who rely on them, the way to rely on them, the benefits of relying on them, the disadvantages of not relying on them, and a summary of the above.
dang po bsten bya dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi mtshan nyid ni/
4.1.1.1. The defining characteristics of the spiritual teachers on whom to rely

d.div: de nas gdams pa dngos kyi nyams len la/ / slob ma'i rgyud kyi yon tan sna gcig kyang / / dam pa'i bshes gnyen mnyes la rag las pas/ / thog mar de yi bsten tshul gnad du che//[16]
gang zhig tshul khrims bslab pas sems rta thul/ / dran shes thag pas ting 'dzin las su rung / / shes rab mig gis zab mo'i de nyid gzigs/ / mang thos slob ma dag las yon tan lhag/[17]

lung rigs tsam gyis de nyid rtogs pa'ang bzung / / bkri ba'i rim pa mkhas pas smra mkhas dang / / snying rjes kun bslab [8] ston pas brtse bdag nyid/ / spro brtan brtson bcas 'chad pas skyo ba spangs//[18]
bslab gsum de nyid rtogs dang brtse ba lnga/ / gtso bo yin mod dus kyis rnyed dka' na/ / skyon yon gnyis las yon tan lhag pa bzung / / 'di rnams tshang bya slob mas kyang 'di bsten//[19]

16 Next, since practice of the actual teaching and every single good quality in a student’s mind depend on pleasing the excellent spiritual teachers, knowing how to rely upon them is crucial from the start.

17 [Rely on those who] have broken in the mount of their mind by training in ethical discipline; on those who through meditative concentration have made it serviceable with the reins of mindfulness and meta-awareness;[146] on those who perceive profound suchness with the eye of wisdom, have studied much, and whose good qualities surpass their students’.

18 Understanding suchness by citations and reasonings alone is also acceptable. [Rely on those] who are proficient teachers skilled in guiding others in steps, on those who have loving natures because their teachings are inspired by compassion, and on those who have surmounted discouragement by teaching with diligence[147] and constant delight.

19 Although the five — the three trainings, understanding suchness, and compassion — are key qualities, if they are difficult to find [in others] given the times, follow those whose good qualities exceed their bad qualities. Students are to rely on those possessing all these good qualities.
[8] kun bslang / rda sa shes dpar/

[146] A factor that, along with mindfulness (smṛti), plays an important role in the cultivation of tranquil abiding (śamatha) by monitoring the mind focusing on its object. Alternate translations commonly found are “vigilance” and “introspection.”

[147] In the two works I have translated in this volume, I have rendered brtson ’grus (Skt. vīrya) as “diligence” to match the rest of the book. Merriam-Webster defines diligence as “steady, earnest, and energetic effort,” but this does not capture the connotation that Asaṅga glosses as “mental delight” and Śāntideva as “delighting in virtue.” Given these, I elsewhere translate this as “enthusiasm.” Another downside to “diligence” is that it makes presenting the “four possible combinations” (mu bzhi) between brtson ’grus and rtsol ba (“effort”) problematic, for you can delight in virtue (practice enthusiasm) without making the slightest effort.

f.d: gnyis pa bsten byed slob ma'i mtshan nyid ni/
4.1.1.2. The defining characteristics of the students who rely on them

d.div: phyogs lhung spangs shing don gnyer shugs drag pa/ / lam dang lam min 'byed pa'i blo gros can/ / nyan tshe chos la legs par yid gtod pa/ / 'di dag tshang bya slob ma'i mtshan nyid do//[20]

f.d: 20 Rejecting bias, possessing intense aspiration, having the intelligence to distinguish a path that is spiritual from one that is not, paying close attention when listening to the teaching — ensure that you have these, for they are what characterize a [good] student. [17]
gsum pa des de ji ltar bsten pa'i tshul
4.1.1.3. The way to rely on them
['di ]la gnyis/ bsam pas bsten pa'i tshul/ sbyor bas bsten pa'i tshul lo/ /
This has two parts: how to rely on them in thought and how to rely on them in deed.
dang po bsam pas bsten pa'i tshul
4.1.1.3.1. How to rely on them in thought
['di ]la gnyis/ rtsa ba dad pa sbyang ba/ bka' drin rjes su dran te gus par bya ba'o/ /

4.1.1.3.1.1. Cultivating faith, the root

d.div: lhag par dad pas slob dpon yon tan bzung / / de la skyon rtog skad cig kyang mi bya/ / dngos grub 'grub byed gegs byed 'gyur phyir ro/ / gal te bag med skyon rtog 'phral du bshags//[21]

21 With great faith, focus on the spiritual teachers’ good qualities. Do not consider their faults for even an instant, for it will hinder your achievement of spiritual realizations. If, out of carelessness, you do impute faults to them, confess it immediately.

d.div: 'dir ni bka' drin rjes su dran byas te/ / chos bcu pa dang [9] sdong po bkod pa'i mdor/[10] / ji ltar gsungs bzhin dbyangs su brjod cing bsam/ / de ni bsam pas bshes gnyen bsten tshul lo//[22]

23 Please them [by offering them] your life, children, spouse, wealth, and retinue, by bathing, massaging, wiping, and nursing them, by never disobeying them, whatever they instruct you to do, and most importantly by offering them your practice.

4.1.1.4. The benefits of relying on them

d.div: de yi phan yon rgyal dgyes dge bshes nye/ / ngan 'gror mi ltung las nyon gyis mi thub/ / yon tan je mthor 'gyur bas gnas skabs dang / / mthar thug don grub sangs rgyas yon zil gnon//[24]

24 The benefits are pleasing the buddhas, being close to spiritual teachers, not falling into unfortunate realms, becoming immune to karma and afflictions, and by enhancing your good qualities, achieving your temporary and ultimate goals, and as such, they surpass those of making offerings to buddhas.

f.d: lnga pa ma bsten pa'i nyes dmigs ni/
4.1.1.5. The disadvantages of not relying on them

d.div: gal te 'di yi bsten tshul log gyur na/ / rmongs bzhin 'chi ba'i dus byas mnar med sreg/ / yon tan mi skye skyes pa'ang nyams 'gyur zhing / / sdig grogs mi dge'i bshes kyi'ang skyon 'di 'byin//[25]

25 If through ignorance you commit a breach of reliance on your spiritual teacher, you will roast in the Relentless hell[149] after death. Good qualities will not arise in you, and those you have will decline. [Meeting] bad companions and false teachers also incurs these disadvantages.
[149] Skt. avīci, the eighth hot hell.

f.d: drug pa de dag gi don bsdu ba ni/
4.1.1.6. A summary of the above

d.div: mdor na snying nas chos zhig byed 'dod na/ / ma nor 'khrid pa'i bshes gnyen rgyun ring bsten/ / de tshe phan yon nyes dmigs rig pa'i blos/ / bla ma'i dam tshig srog las gces par bzung //[26]

26 In sum, if you sincerely wish to practice the Dharma, rely long on teachers who guide you infallibly. By understanding the benefits and disadvantages as you do so, value your commitment to the gurus more than you do your life. [18]

f.d: gnyis pa skyong tshul mdor bstan pa
4.1.2. A brief explanation for meditational purposes
['di ]la gnyis/ skyong tshul dngos/ skyong tshul gnyis kyis bskyang dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan no/ /
This has two parts: how to actually meditate and why it is necessary to meditate using both meditative approaches.
dang po skyong tshul dngos
4.1.2.1. How to actually meditate
['di ]la gnyis/ thun gyi ngo bo la ji ltar bya ba dang / thun mtshams su ji ltar bya ba'o/ /
This has two parts: what to do in the actual meditation sessions and what to do between meditation sessions.
dang po thun gyi ngo bo la ji ltar bya ba
4.1.2.1.1. What to do in the actual meditation sessions
['di ]la gsum/ sbyor ba/ dngos gzhi/ mjug tu ji ltar bya ba'o/ /
This has three parts: the preliminary practices, the actual meditation, and the concluding practice.
dang po sbyor ba ni/
4.1.2.1.1.1. The preliminary practices

d.div: de nas gnas gtsang sku gsung thugs rten dgram/ / mchod pa g.yo med bkod pa mdzes par bsham/ / stan la lus bsrang skyil krung spyod lam gyis/ / skyabs 'gro sems bskyed rgyud dang 'dres nges bya//[27]

bla ma gtsor gyur tshogs zhing gsal btab la/ / bsag sbyang gnad bsdus yan lag bdun pa bya/ / phyag mchod bskul ba gsol gdab [11] yi rang lngas/ / tshogs bsags bshags pas sgrib sbyong dga' bas spel//[28]
bsngo bas bsag sbyang spel ba'i dge ba rnams/ / nam yang mi zad byed phyir don bsdu na/ / bsag sbyang spel zhing mi zad byed pa gsum/ / maN+Dal sngon 'gros 'dod don gsol ba gdab//[29]
bshes gnyen gus sogs phyin ci ma log blo/ / mtha' dag rgyud la skye dang phyi nang gi / bar chad zhi sogs 'dun pa shugs drag gis/ / yang yang gsol ba gdab pa nges par bya//[30]

27 Next, in a clean place set up symbols of [the buddhas’] body, speech, and mind. Arrange faultless offerings in an attractive way. On a seat in the posture with crossed legs and straight back, take refuge and generate the awakening mind, taking care to be sincere.

28 Visualize the merit field, with the guru as the main figure. Perform the seven-limb practice that includes the key elements for accumulation and purification. Of these, by five — homage, offerings, request, supplication, and rejoicing — you gather the accumulations; confession purifies obscurations; and joy increases [virtue].

29 Dedication ensures that the virtues of accumulation, purification, and increase are never depleted. To summarize, there are three — accumulation, purification, and increase — along with rendering [virtue] inexhaustible [by dedication]. Then, after a mandala [offering], make requests for your desired goals:

30 that all kinds of unmistaken thoughts — reverence for the spiritual teachers and so on — may arise in your mind, that external and internal obstacles may ease, and so on.[150] With intense aspiration, be sure to supplicate again and again.
[11] gsol btab/ rda sa shes dpar/

[150] The three main objectives for which supplication is made are the two indicated here as well as the cessation of all mistaken thoughts, from irreverence toward your spiritual teachers up to grasping at the two types of self.

f.d: gnyis pa dngos gzhi
4.1.2.1.1.2. The actual meditation
['di ]la gnyis/ spyi'i skyong tshul/ skabs 'di'i skyong tshul lo/ /
This has two parts: how to meditate in general and how to meditate in the present context.
dang po spyi'i skyong tshul ni/
4.1.2.1.1.2.1. How to meditate in general

d.div: rang rgyud dge la bkol rung bsgrub 'dod pas/ / bskyang rgyu'i dmigs pa'i grangs dang go rim ni/ / nges byas lhag chad med par dran shes sgrim/ / gzhan du hril po'i dge sbyor skyon can 'gyur//[31]

31 To make your mind receptive to virtue, be certain of the order and number of meditation topics, and with neither excess nor want, be intent upon them while applying mindfulness and meta-awareness; otherwise, the virtuous practices of a lifetime will be flawed.

f.d: gnyis pa skabs 'di'i skyong tshul ni/
4.1.2.1.1.2.2. How to meditate in the present context

d.div: skabs 'dir bshes gnyen bsten pa'i phan yon dang / / ma bsten nyes dmigs bsams te skyon rtog bsdam/ / yon tan 'ba' zhig sems pa'i dad pa yi/ / drin bsam snying nas gus pa skyes te sgom//[32]

32 In this context, reflect on the advantages of relying on spiritual teachers and on the disadvantages of not relying on them, and refrain from considering faults. With faith that is conscious only of their good qualities, generate and sustain heartfelt reverence by reflecting on their kindness.

f.d: gsum pa mjug tu ji ltar bya ba ni/
4.1.2.1.1.3. The concluding practice

d.div: de rjes dge ba bsngo zhing rim pa 'dis/ / nyin zhag gcig la thun bzhir bcad de 'bad/ / re zhig thun chung grangs mang bzang gyes bslab/ / drod [12] tshad rnyed nas ji ltar rigs par bskyang //[33]

33 At the end dedicate the virtue. Following this routine, divide the day and night into four sessions and expend every effort. Initially, do many short sessions, ending them on a good note. [19] Once you have mastered these, you may meditate as you see fit.
[12] brod tshad/ rda sa shes dpar/

f.d: [thun mtshams su ji ltar bya ba ]
4.1.2.1.2. [What to do between meditation sessions]

d.div: thun mtshams su yang bskyang rgyu'i dmigs pa rnams/ / rgya yan mi gtang [13] yang yang dran byas te/ / de nyid ched du tshogs gsog sgrib sbyong dang / / gzhan yang dbang po'i sgo sdom zas tshod rig/[34]

ma [14] nyal rnal 'byor brtson dang nyal ba'i tshe/ / lus kyi kun spyod dran shes bsten tshul sogs/ / sbyor dngos rjes dang thun mtshams nyams len rnams/ / lhag mthong bar 'dra dngos gzhi'i dmigs bsal yod//[35]

34 Between sessions, do not put the topics you are meditating out of your mind but recall them again and again. For their sake accumulate merit and purify your obscurations.[151] Furthermore, restrain the doors of your senses and eat with moderation.

35 Strive in the yoga of no-sleep,[152] and when you do sleep, apply proper posture, mindfulness, meta-awareness, and the like. The practice of the preliminaries, actual meditation, conclusion, and between sessions is the same up to insight with the exception of the actual meditations.
[13] mi btang / rda sa shes dpar/
[14] mi nyal/ rda sa shes dpar/
[151] Creating merit and purifying wrongdoing is the groundwork that ensures that meditation on whatever topic leads to realization and insight.
[152] The instruction is to avoid sleeping at the beginning and end of the night and during the day.

f.d: gnyis pa skyong tshul gnyis kyis skyong dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan ni/
4.1.2.2. Why it is necessary to meditate using both meditative approaches

d.div: ji ltar rin chen bsreg bkrus las rung 'gyur/ / de bzhin gnag dang dkar po'i las 'bras la/ / skyo dang dang bar 'gyur ba'i yid byed ni/ / 'dzin stangs shugs drag rgyun ring dpyad sgom gyis//[36]
zhi lhag gang 'dod bsgrub la las rung 'gyur/ / de phyir mi rtog bsgrub la dpyad sgom mchog / gang zhig zhi gnas bsgrub pa lta bu'i tshe/ / ha cang dpyad na mi bzang 'jog sgom dgos//[37]
de phyir mkhas dang ku su lu gnyis kas/ / zhi gnas bshes gnyen dad sogs nges sgrub phyir/ / dpyad dang 'jog pa'i skyong tshul gnyis kas bskyang / / gzhan yang bying rgod sems gnas gegs yin pas//[38]
dngas [15] bshu gas drag bying ba sel ba'i mchog / skyo ba shugs drag rgod pa sel byed du/ / tshad ldan gzhung mchog du ma las gsungs phyir/ / 'gal rkyen sel byed skyon du ma blta zhig/[39]

36 Just as gold becomes malleable when heated and washed, the practice of focusing on disgust and delight [respectively, for example] for black and white karmas and their effects with firm apprehension of the object and prolonged analytical meditation,

37 also renders feasible tranquil abiding[153] and insight, whichever you desire. Accordingly, to realize nonconceptual cognition,[154] analytical meditation is best. When working to achieve tranquil abiding, excessive analysis is inappropriate and placement meditation required.

38 Consequently, both scholars and meditators — to ensure achieving tranquil abiding, faith in teachers, and so on — should train using both analytical and placement meditations. Moreover, as laxity and excitation hinder mental stability,

39 vigorous clarity is ideal for dispelling laxity and vigorous disgust for dispelling excitation, as taught in numerous excellent and authoritative treatises. Since they remove adverse conditions, do not think it wrong to apply them.
[15] dang ba/ rda sa shes dpar/

[153] Zhi gnas, Skt. śamatha. Other common translations are “meditative serenity” and “calm abiding.” Zhi or zhi ba (“peace”) refers to that fact that all distraction away from the focal object has been “pacified” or quelled; gnas refers to the stability aspect. A third important component of zhi gnas is mental and physical pliancy (shin sbyang).
[154] In this context “nonconceptual cognition” refers to a direct understanding of selflessness.

f.d: dal ba'i rten la snying po blang ba'i phyir du bskul ba/

b.i: Human Existence with Leisure and Opportunity

f.d: gnyis pa bsten nas blo ji ltar sbyang ba'i rim pa
4.2. While relying on [spiritual teachers], how to progressively train your mind
['di ]la gnyis/ dal ba'i rten la snying po blang ba'i phyir du bskul ba dang / snying po ji ltar len pa'i tshul lo/ /
This has two parts: urging to take full advantage of a [human] rebirth with leisure and the way to take full advantage of one.
dang po dal ba'i rten la snying po blang ba'i phyir du bskul ba
4.2.1. Urging to take full advantage of a [human] rebirth with leisure
['di ]la gsum/ dal 'byor ngos bzung ba dang / don che ba bsam pa dang / rnyed dka' ba bsam pa'o/ /
This has three parts: identifying leisure and opportunity, contemplating their great potential, and contemplating how difficult they are to attain.
dang po dal 'byor ngos bzung ba
4.2.1.1. Identifying leisure and opportunity
['di ]la gnyis/ dal ba dang / 'byor ba'o/ /
This has two parts: leisure and opportunity.
dang po dal ba ni/
4.2.1.1.1. Leisure

d.div: mtha' 'khob dbang po ma tshang log lta can/ / rgyal ba'i bka' med mi yi mi khom bzhi/ / tshe ring lha dang ngan song gsum ste brgyad/ / de dang bral ba dal ba yin par gsungs//[40]

40 Being born in a remote land, with incomplete senses, wrong views, [20] and in a place where the Buddha’s teaching is not found are the four human non-liberties. Adding [rebirth as] a long-life god or in the three unfortunate realms, there are eight. It is taught that averting these constitutes “leisure.”

f.d: gnyis pa 'byor ba
4.2.1.1.2. Opportunity
['di ]la gnyis/ rang gi 'byor ba dang / gzhan gyi 'byor pa'o/ /
This has two parts: personal opportunities and general opportunities.
dang po rang gi 'byor ba ni/
4.2.1.1.2.1. Personal opportunities

d.div: mi nyid dbus skyes dbang po tshang ba dang / / mtshams med ma byas sde snod gsum la dad//

f.d: gnyis pa gzhan gyi 'byor pa ni/
4.2.1.1.2.2. General opportunities

d.div: sangs rgyas byon nas chos bstan bstan pa gnas/ / de rjes 'jug dang gzhan phyir snying brtse ba'o//[41]
These are that a buddha has appeared, he has taught the Dharma, his teaching remains, there are those who follow it, and there are those with compassion for others.

f.d: gnyis pa dal 'byor don che bar bsam pa ni/
4.2.1.2. Contemplating the great potential of leisure and opportunity

d.div: 'byor ba bcu ldan rten ni rnyed gyur nas/ / tshe 'di lhur len dud 'gro'i kun spyod yin/ / gling gsum skyes pa bud med ma gtogs pa/ / sgra mi snyan pa sdom pa'i rten ma [16] rung //[42]
khams gong lha dang 'dod lha phal cher gyi/ / rten des 'phags lam gsar du thob mi srid/ / sems kyi stobs chen mi nyid rnyed gyur nas/ / don med spyod na rig sngags kyis rmongs 'dra//[43]
bde gshegs lam rten 'di dgos ma zad kyi/ / mngon mtho'i lus dang 'khor dang longs spyod rgyu/ / sbyin sogs rten 'dis 'grub 'dra gzhan gyis min/ / de phyir rgyun du 'di nyid don che bsam//[44]

42 Once you have attained a life with the ten opportunities, to strive after this life’s concerns is to behave like an animal. Only a rebirth as a man or woman on three continents is a suitable basis for taking vows, not one in Uttarakuru.[155]

43 In most rebirths as a god of the higher realms or the desire realm, it is not possible to achieve an ārya path for the first time.[156] Having attained a human life with a powerful mind, if you use it meaninglessly, you are like someone stupefied by magic.

44 Not only is it the basis needed to travel the Tathāgata’s path, it is also the basis for creating the causes of a fortunate rebirth, and those of wealth and entourage caused by generosity and so forth, and not any other. For these reasons persistently contemplate its great potential.
[16] mi rung / rda sa shes dpar/

[155] Uttarakuru (sgra mi snyan) is the northern continent in Buddhist cosmology, where, given the excessive hedonism of that existence, beings there are said to be unsuitable vessels for Dharma practice.

[156] Here “the higher realms” are the form and formless realms, and “achieving an ārya path” is attaining the path of seeing, which according to Prāsaṅgika tenets, requires realizing emptiness directly, no matter which vehicle one is on.

f.d: gsum pa rnyed dka' ba bsam pa ni/
4.2.1.3. Contemplating how difficult they are to attain

d.div: mi dge'i phyogs yongs 'dzin pa ngan 'gro'i sgo/ / rang rgyud dge ba khong khro'i chom pos 'phrog / sngar nyes mi sbyong phyin chad mi sdom pa/ / sos dal 'dis ni 'gro ba cir 'gyur soms//[45]
bde thob chos rag las phyir chos sgrub dgos/ / bshes gnyen dal 'byor tshang phyir chos sgrub nus/ / 'dir ma bsgrubs na dal 'byor phyis rnyed dka'/ / nam 'chi'i dus btab med pas deng nas sgrub//[46]
ngan 'gro'i tshod na bde 'gro srid mtha' tsam/ / bde 'gro tsam yang dkon na dal 'byor soms/ / mdor na dal 'byor ngo bo ngos bzung la/ / de nyid rgyu 'bras sgo nas rnyed dka' bsam//[47]

45 Tending entirely to nonvirtue is the door to unfortunate realms. Anger is the thief who plunders your virtue. You who fail to purify past misdeeds and refrain from future ones yet take your ease, think what kind of life awaits you!

46 Since achieving happiness depends on the Dharma, you must practice it. Because you have spiritual teachers as well as leisure and opportunity, you can practice it. If you do not do it now, it will be difficult to find leisure and opportunity in the future. As your time of death is not set, practice it from this day forward.

47 Compared to an unfortunate birth, a fortunate one is nearly impossible to attain. If ordinary fortunate rebirths are rare, consider how exceptional leisure and opportunity are. In brief, identify the nature of leisure and opportunity, and contemplate the difficulty of attaining them from the perspective of karma and its effects. [21]

f.d: gnyis pa snying po ji ltar len pa'i tshul
4.2.2. The way to take full advantage of leisure and opportunity
['di ]la gnyis/ lam spyi'i rnam gzhag la nges pa bskyed pa/ de la snying po len tshul dngos so/ /
This has two parts: ascertaining the system of the spiritual path in general, and actually taking full advantage of them.
dang po lam spyi'i rnam gzhag la nges pa bskyed pa
4.2.2.1. Ascertaining the system of the spiritual path in general
['di ]la gnyis/ skyes bu gsum gyi lam du gsung rab thams cad 'du ba'i tshul/ skyes bu gsum gyi sgo nas rim pa bzhin du 'khrid pa'i rgyu mtshan bstan pa'o//
This has two parts: the way all discourses are included in the paths of persons of three capacities, and the reason you are guided in steps along the paths of persons of three capacities.
dang po skyes bu gsum gyi lam du gsung rab thams cad 'du ba'i tshul ni/
4.2.2.1.1. The way all discourses are included in the paths of persons of three capacities

d.div: gsung rab kun gyi brjod bya'i lam mtha' dag/ / skyes bu gsum gyi lam du nges 'du ste/ / mngon mtho nges legs sgrub pa las brtsams te/ / gsungs pa las gzhan gsung rab yod min phyir//[48]
mngon mtho'i dpal dang nges legs gnyis phye ba/ / rim bzhin gsum sgrub gtso phyir khyab 'brel yod//

48 Every spiritual path — the topic of all the [Buddha’s] discourses — is without doubt included in the paths of persons of three capacities, for no discourse was ever given for any reason other than to ensure the achievement of fortunate rebirths and definite goodness.
49 As the [three] stages lead respectively to the three: excellent fortunate rebirths and definite goodness, the latter being twofold [and the second of which is] foremost, they are exhaustive.[157]

[157] “Definite goodness” is twofold in that it indicates both personal liberation from samsara and buddhahood. Of the two, buddhahood is the ultimate goal sought by those practicing the lamrim. The stages of the persons of the three capacities are exhaustive in that, since all Buddha’s discourses were necessarily given as means to achieve either a high rebirth or definite goodness in its two forms, and the three stages of the path produce these results, the lamrim necessarily includes all the essential elements of the Buddha’s discourses.

f.d: gnyis pa skyes bu gsum gyi sgo nas rim pa bzhin du 'khrid pa'i rgyu mtshan bstan pa
4.2.2.1.2. The reason you are guided in steps along the paths of persons of three capacities
['di ]la gnyis/ skyes bu gsum gyi lam gyi sgo nas 'khrid pa'i don gang yin pa/ rim pa de ltar 'khrid pa'i rgyu mtshan bstan pa'o/ /
This has two parts: what it means to be guided along the paths of persons of three capacities, and the reasons why you are to be guided like this in that order.
dang po skyes bu gsum gyi lam gyi sgo nas 'khrid pa'i don gang yin pa ni/
4.2.2.1.2.1. What it means to be guided along the paths of persons of three capacities

d.div: 'khrid tshul chung 'bring skabs kyi thun mong lam/ / 'ga' zhig sngon 'gror byas nas chen por 'khrid//[49]
As for how to be guided, with some paths shared with persons of lesser and intermediate capacity as preparations, you are led to the path of persons of great capacity.

f.d: gnyis pa rim pa de ltar 'khrid pa'i rgyu mtshan
4.2.2.1.2.2. The reasons why you are to be guided like this in that order
['di ]la gnyis/ dngos dang / dgos pa'o/ /
This has two parts: the actual reasons and the purpose.
dang po dngos ni/
4.2.2.1.2.2.1. The actual reasons

d.div: sems bskyed theg chen lam gyi gzhung shing ste/ / tshogs gnyis rdzogs la gser 'gyur rtsi lta bu/ / gnas skabs mthar thug 'dod don ma lus pa/ / sems mchog 'di yis 'grub par gdon mi za//[50]

50 “The awakening mind is the central beam of the supreme vehicle. For completing the two accumulations, it is like a philosopher’s stone.”[158] All temporary and ultimate objectives without exception are undoubtedly achieved by this supreme aspiration.
[158] These two lines are drawn from Jé Tsongkhapa’s Song of Spiritual Experience, verse 21. See page 46.
phan yon can gyi sems de 'byung ba la/ / phan yon de la spro ba shugs drag dgos/ / chung 'bring thun mong bsam pas 'di sgrub phyir/ / de nas nges par sems de bsgrub par 'gyur//[51]

51 To realize the state of mind that carries such advantages, you need to take profound delight in its benefits. Since it is achieved by reflecting on the paths shared with persons of lesser and intermediate capacity, be sure you contemplate them, and your achievement will be assured.
de yang sgrub byed rtsa ba byams snying rje/ / gang zhig rang nyid bde phongs sdug bsngal gyis/ / mnar tshul bsams tshe nyam nga mi 'byung na/ / gzhan sdug bsngal la mi bzod ga la skye//[52]

52 Its prime causes are love and compassion. If, when you reflect on the way you are personally deprived of happiness and tormented by suffering, you are not horrified, how could you possibly find the suffering of others unbearable?
de phyir ngan song gnod pa 'bab tshul dang / / mtho ris na yang bde bas phongs pa'i tshul/ / chung 'bring skabs su rang nyams sbyar bsams na/ / gnyen gyur 'gro la byams dang snying rje skye//[53]

53 Thus you should reflect on how you are subjected to the unfortunate realms’ miseries and deprived of happiness even in fortunate births, relating it to yourself personally according to the teachings for persons of lesser and intermediate capacity, and love and compassion will emerge for sentient beings, your friends.

gzhan yang chung 'bring skabs kyi bsag sbyang rnams/ / sems bskyed sngon 'gro'i rgyud sbyong thabs 'gyur phyir/ / chung 'bring chos skor chen po'i yan lag tu/ / 'gro tshul 'di dag bsam nas nyams len gces//[54]

54 Furthermore, as the accumulations and purifications of persons of lesser and intermediate capacity are the means to prepare your mind for the awakening mind, contemplate how the topics of persons of lesser and intermediate capacity [22] are prerequisites to the path of persons of great capacity, and treasure their practice.
de ltar sbyangs pas sems bskyed de brtan phyir/ / smon sems cho gas gzung ste bslab bya mnyan/ / de nas rgyal sras spyod pa khur bzod na/ / 'jug sdom blang zhing rtsa ltung srog bsdos bsrung //[55]

55 Having trained in this way, stabilize the awakening mind by performing the aspirational bodhicitta ceremony and studying the precepts. Then, when you feel you can bear the load of bodhisattva practice, take the vow of engaging bodhicitta and guard yourself against root transgressions even at the cost of your life.

56 Refrain from lesser and intermediate transgressions, and restore [your vow] if it declines. Train in the six perfections in general and in tranquil abiding in particular to attain clairvoyance and special insight. Once you have a decisive understanding of suchness, engage in tantra.

87 From general virtuous and nonvirtuous karmas arise general happiness and suffering; specific instances of happiness and suffering arise from subtle specific instances of each kind of karma.

d.div: dge sdig chung ngus bde sdug cher bskyed dang //
88 Minor virtues and sins produce [respectively] great happiness and suffering.

d.div: dge sdig ma bsags bde sdug myong mi srid//
Without accomplishing virtue and sin, it is impossible to experience happiness and suffering.

4.2.2.2.1.1.2.2.1.1.4. Karma once accomplished does not dissipate

d.div: rang gi las byas chud zar mi 'byung zhing / / ma byas phrad med byin len ltar mi 'pho//[88]
Karma you have accomplished does not dissipate; you do not experience effects of what you have not accomplished; and karma is not exchanged like the giving and receiving [of gifts].[164]
[164] You cannot give the karma you produce to others nor receive others’ karma, as you do gifts.

4.2.2.2.1.1.2.2.1.2.1. Explaining the importance of the ten paths

d.div: sgo gsum las rnams 'di bcur ma 'dus kyang / / che long bsdus nas las lam bcur gsungs so/[37] / tshul khrims la sogs dge ba sna re yang / / byed pa'i [38] khur med theg chen khas 'che ba//[89]
rgyal ba'i spyan sngar 'jig rten bslu bar gsungs/ / de phyir ngag bsrungs yid ni rab bsdams te/ / lus kyis mi dge ba dag mi byed pa/ / de dag drang song chen po'i lam la brtson//[90]

89 Although all actions of the three doors are not included in the ten, classifying them broadly as ten karmic paths has been taught.[165] If you do not adopt so much as a single virtuous practice such as ethical discipline and yet portray yourself a Mahayanist,

90 it is taught that in the eyes of the buddhas you are deceiving the whole world. Thus those who guard their speech, control their minds well, and abstain from committing physical nonvirtues are those who are endeavoring to follow the Great Sage’s path. [28]
