f.d:
de bzhin du rga ba'i sdug bsngal yang rgya che rol pa las/
rga bas gzugs sdug gzugs mi sdug par byed/ / rga bas gzi brjid 'phrog cing mthu stobs 'phrog / rga bas bde ba 'phrog cing brnyas par byed/ / rga bas 'chi byed rga bas mdangs kyang 'phrog[105] / ces skra dkar zhing lus gug pa/ dpral ba gnyer mas khebs pa sogs lus kyi mthu nyams pa'i tshul la mtshon na/ sngar na tshod dar bab kyi dus lus drang zhing skra'i mdog gnag pa pags [106] pa la gnyer ma sogs med pa'i gzhon sha can de da lta lus ma 'phos kyang 'phos pa dang khyad par med pa 'di bzhin du song 'dug/ / slar yang lo zla zhag mang song rim gyis zla ba mar gyi ngo bzhin rnam par 'gribs nas 'chi bdag gi khar chud par 'dug snyam du skyo shas kyi myong ba drag po ma thon gyi bar du bsam/

With respect to the suffering of aging, the Play in Full Sutra says:
Age renders your attractive body ugly. Age steals your charisma and robs you of your strength. Age ravishes your happiness and makes you an object of contempt. Age kills you and deprives you of your radiance.[465] Think: My hair has gone white, my body is stooped, and my brow is covered in wrinkles. If I look at the decline of my physical strength, for example, and compare myself to how I was in my prime — with my straight body, black hair, wrinkle-free skin, and so on — although I have not yet changed bodies, I may as well have. This is what I have now become. Many days, months, and years have passed. The time I have left to live is decreasing steadily, like waning of the moon, and I will end up in the jaws of death. Reflect on this until a feeling of intense distaste arises in you.

d.div: [105] sde dge_95_bka'/ mdo sde/ kha_rgya cher rol pa'i mdo/ shog_88_ba4
[106] lpags pa/ rme ru phun tshogs gling gi dpar ma/
[465] Lalitavistarasūtra, Toh 95 Kangyur, mdo sde, kha, 88b4.

f.d: de bzhin du lus kyi mthu nyams pas ldang 'dug tshul bzhin du mi 'ong / 'gro ba'i tshe gom pa 'khyor/ ngag ldab ldib du smra bas mtshon te dbang po nyams pas mig rna sogs kyis sngar lta bu'i mthong thos sogs ji bzhin mi 'byung zhing dran pa mi gsal bas brjed ngas can du 'gyur/ bza' btung yang sngar za ba'i tshod tsam du zos na nad sna tshogs skyed par byed pa'i tshul rnams gong bzhin bsgom/ nyams len byed pa po na tshod gzhon nu zhig yin na mgo bo dkar ba sogs bshad ma thag pa'i skyon phal cher rang nyams la dpags te gzhal rgyu med mod/ na tshod rgan po zhig la phar bltas nas 'di yang ma'i mngal nas btsa' ba'i dus rgas shing 'khogs pa 'di ga min pa thag chod/ bdag lta bu'i gzhon nu zhig gnas skabs 'di 'drar gyur 'dug go bsam pa'i tshul gyis bsgom gsung /

In this way, as your strength fails, you cannot rise and sit down properly; you totter as you walk; when you talk, your speech is slurred, and so on. As your senses decline, you cannot see or hear as you did before; your memory fails you, and you become forgetful. As for food and drink, eating the same amounts as before causes various sicknesses. Contemplate how these occur in the way described above. Young practitioners still in their prime will be unable to relate to most of the above-mentioned flaws, like white hair. They should therefore contemplate someone old and think, “When this person was delivered from his mother’s womb, he certainly was not old and feeble like this; someone young like me will inevitably end up just like him!” [My guru] said to meditate in this way.

na ba'i sdug bsngal ni sngar rang nyid nad drag pos 'debs myong ba'am min na nad pa gzhan dag la rjes su dpags te yun ring po nas 'du ba 'khrugs pa'i nad dam/ glo bur du gdon dang mtshon la sogs pas gtses pa'i tshul ni/ rgya che rol pa las/
dper na dgun smad rlung dang kha ba che/ / rtswa shing gel pa nags sman mdangs kyang 'phrog/ / de ltar nad 'dis 'gro ba'i mdangs 'phrog cing / / dbang po zungs dang stobs ni nyams par byed/[107] / ces tsha grang shes che chung gi gzugs gzer sogs gdung ba sna tshogs kyis nyam thag pas lus kyi sha lpags bskams shing sgul skyod dka'/ yid du 'ong ba'i zas skom rnams nad la gnod kyi dogs nas sman pa sogs kyis zar mi ster/ yid du mi 'ong ba'i zas dang sman sna tshogs gtar sreg rnams mi 'dod bzhin du bsten dgos tshul bsam mo//

Regarding the suffering of illness, you may have fallen seriously ill at some point. If not, then contemplate illness from others’ sicknesses stemming from a protracted unbalanced physical constitution, sudden harm by an evil spirit or a weapon, and so on. Concerning this, the Play in Full Sutra states:
Just as late winter winds and snowstorms rob trees, grasses, bushes, and herbs of their luster, so does illness rob beings of their bloom and drain their senses, vital substance, and strength.[466] Reflect on how you are debilitated by various torments like the pain occasioned by changes in temperature, and on how as a result your skin dries up, you lose weight, and your movement becomes difficult. [184] Doctors and others refuse to give you rich food and beverages in fear that they will aggravate your illness. Against your will you are forced to take various nasty foods and medicines and undergo bloodletting and moxibustion.

d.div: [107] sde dge_95_bka'/ mdo sde/ kha_rgya cher rol pa'i mdo/ shog_88_ba6

f.d:
'chi ba'i sdug bsngal ni/ rgya cher rol pa las/
'chi dang 'pho dang 'chi 'pho dus byed pa/ / phongs shing sdug pa'i skye bo rtag tu 'bral/ / phyir mi 'ong zhing 'phrad par 'gyur ma yin/ / shing las lo 'brul 'dra zhing klung rgyun mtshungs/[108] / zhes nad las thar ba zhig byung na dka' ba de tsam spyod ring chog na'ang phal cher ni thabs sna tshogs byas pas kyang nad je cher song ste sman pas bor/ mo bon gyis bslus/ gnyen bshes rnams kyis mtha' bskor nas smre sngags 'don/ shi dge dang dur 'debs kyi gshom ra 'ding / rang nyid kyang bkrag mdangs nyams/ kha bskams/ mchu brdzes/ sna zhom/ mig kong mor song / dbugs brtsegs/ sngar byas kyi sdig pa la 'gyod/ gnyen bshes 'khor g.yog rdzas nor phun tshogs kun dang bral/ gces par bskyangs pa'i lus kyang mal du bzhag ste chags zhen drag po'i dbang gis 'jig rten pha rol du 'gro dgos tshul gyi sdug bsngal drag pos mnar ba rnams bsam mo//

On the suffering of dying, the Play in Full Sutra states:
When the time comes to die, move on, and die again, you are definitively separated from those that you cherish. Like leaves fallen from trees and water in the current of a stream, there is no turning back and no encountering them again.[467] If you manage to recover from an illness, all the trials endured will have been worthwhile. However, illnesses more frequently grow worse, despite the various medical treatments undertaken. Doctors then give up on you, diviners deceive you, friends and relatives surround you and lament, and preparations are made for postmortem practices of virtue and for the disposal of your corpse. As for you, your complexion pales, your mouth dries up, your upper lip curls, your nostrils become pinched, your eyes recede in their sockets, and your breathing becomes labored. You regret your past sins. You are soon to be separated from everything good you ever had — friends and relatives, entourage and servants, wealth and property. You also have to leave behind you in the bed the very body that you cared for so dearly and move on to the next world under the sway of strong attachment. Reflect on how you are afflicted by these great torments.

d.div: [108] sde dge_95_bka'/ mdo sde/ kha_rgya cher rol pa'i mdo/ shog_88_ba7

f.d: dgra la brten pa'i sdug bsngal ni/ mi sdug pa'i dgra zhig gis lus srog gtam don la gnod pa byas dogs pa'i sdug bsngal lta ci smos/ dgra dngos sam mi mdza' ba zhig dang gnas khang gcig tu 'tshog dgos byung na'ang yid mi bde ba nag yor re ba lta bu'i snang ba 'char/ de phyogs gzhan zhig tu song na nam langs pa lta bu'i spro ba 'byung tshul la brten nas dgra sdang ba dang phrad kyi dogs pa'i sdug bsngal bsam/

As for suffering caused by enemies, it goes without saying that suspecting that a dire enemy will harm you bodily, take your life, or damage your reputation distresses you. Furthermore, just having to be in the same house with a true enemy or adversary oppresses you to the point that you feel as though darkness has enveloped you, and when they leave and go elsewhere, you are delighted and feel as if the sun has just come up. In this manner you are to reflect on the angst caused by suspecting you might encounter a reviled enemy.

gnyen la brten pa'i sdug bsngal ni/ gnyen bshes dang / de'i nang nas kyang shin tu mdza' ba zhig yul gzhan du song ba la de dag gi yon tan dang phun tshogs rnams dran te sgo gsum sdug bsngal drag po dang / de las go log na dga' ba chen po 'byung ba'i tshul gyi gnyen sdug pa dang bral gyi dogs pa'i sdug bsngal bsam/

As for the suffering entailed by friendships, when friends and relatives depart, especially the dearest of them, think how you ruminate on their good qualities and strengths and deeply suffer physically, verbally, and mentally. Recall how delighted you are when they return as well. In this way contemplate the sorrow occasioned by fear of separation from your loved ones.

'dod pa la brten pa'i sdug bsngal ni/ tshong pa dang zhing las pa sogs kyis 'bad pas bsgrubs kyang tshong zog stor ba dang lo tog ser bas bcom pa/ dbu gtso dang zhang blon rnams kyis dgra ma thul zhing gnyen ma 'khyongs pa/ rab tu byung ba la la gnyen po zhan pas tshul khrims kyi 'go mi thon pa/ shes rab dman pas thos bsam gyi bya ba ma 'grub pa sogs 'dod pa btsal gyis mi rnyed pa'i sdug bsngal/ gzhan yang kha drag po zhan por song ba/ phyug po sprang por song ba/ mi mang po gcig pur song bas mtshon te rgyal khams la brtags na sngar gyi sa na mi 'dug pa sogs mdor na bkres skom tsha grang mi 'dod pa sna tshogs pas mi+i'i lus rten 'di nyid kyang sdug bsngal gyi rang bzhin can yin par myong ba snying thag pa nas ma skyes kyi bar du bsgom mo/ / byang chub lam rim du sdug bsngal brgyad bsam pa dang drug bsam pa sogs spyi ldog tu gsungs na'ang / 'khrid kyi skabs 'jug pa bde ba'i dbang du mdzad de sdug bsngal bdun po gtso cher mi la sbyar nas de'i mjug tu bde 'gro gzhan gnyis kyi sdug bsngal dang sdug bsngal brgyad pa dang / gsum dang drug bsam pa rnams spyir mdzad pa yin no//

As for the suffering that ambition causes, businessmen, farmers, and so on work hard to achieve their goals only to see their merchandise lost and their crops destroyed by hail. [185] Political leaders and their ministers fail to defeat their foes and protect their friends. Monastics are unsuccessful in observing their ethical discipline due to their weak antidotes. They fail to become proficient in learning and reflection owing to poor intelligence and so forth. Such is the suffering of the unsuccessful pursuit of ambitions. Furthermore, there are the sufferings of the powerful becoming powerless — for example, the rich being reduced to poverty, the gregarious finding themselves alone — and these are comparable to returning to your homeland to find nothing as it was before. In brief, meditate until you have gained a deep understanding that owing to various unwelcome situations like hunger and thirst, or heat and cold, the human condition is also characterized by suffering. Although in general the [Great and Middle-Length Treatises on the] Stages of the Path to Enlightenment prescribe the contemplation of eight sufferings, six sufferings, and so on, to simplify in teachings given to small groups, most often seven sufferings are explained mainly in relation to humankind. Following this you are taught to reflect on the sufferings of the other two kinds of fortunate rebirths as well as on the eight, three, and six kinds.
gnyis pa
2.2.2.1.1.1.2. The sufferings of the gods and demigods

bde 'gro gzhan gnyis kyi sdug bsngal bsam pa ni/ bshes spring las/
lus kyi kha dog mi sdug 'gyur ba dang / / stan la mi dga' me tog 'phreng brnyings dang / / gos la dri ma chags dang lus la ni/ / sngon chad med pa'i rdul 'byung zhes bgyi ba/ / mtho ris 'chi 'pho sbron byed 'chi ltas lnga/[109] / zhes 'dod pa'i lha rnams la mi lta bu'i skye rga sogs kyi sdug bsngal med na'ang / 'chi bar nye ba'i tshe glo bur du lus kyi bkrag mdangs nyams shing bde ba'i stan la 'dug snying mi 'dod pa/ me tog gi 'phreng ba brnyings pa/ gos la dri ma nag nog chags pa/ sngon med pa'i lus la rdul 'byung ba rnams 'chi ltas lnga/ lus kyi 'od chung du song ba/ khrus chu lus la chags pa/ gos rgyan las sgra mi snyan pa 'byung ba/ mig gi rdzi ma 'khrab pa/ yul gcig la chags pa lnga po nye ba'i 'chi ltas te bcu po de rnams 'chi ltas su rig nas sdug bsngal zhing / khyad par skabs gsum pa zhes bya ba gang du skye 'gyur gyi gnas kyang brtags na shes pa yin pas/ de ma thag dmyal bar skye nges lta bu yin na dmyal bar skyes zin pa dang khyad par med pa'i sdug bsngal drag po mi bzad pa yod pas mi lta bu la ngan song du skyes dogs pa tsam las rtag brtan ther zug de 'dra med pas lha'i sdug bsngal lhag par che ba yin gsung / gzhan yang bsod nams chen po'i lha rnams mthong ba'i tshe chung ba rnams spa bkong ba dang / stobs che bas chung ba gnas gzhan du bskrod pa dang / lha ma yin dang 'thab pa'i tshe phan tshun gcig gis gcig gsod cing lus dang yan lag gtubs cing gcod pa'i sdug bsngal sna tshogs pa/ gzugs gzugs med kyi lha rnams ni mngon gyur gyi sdug bsngal de dag dang mi ldan na'ang rgya mtsho'i gzings kyi phug ron slar yang gzings la 'khor ba ltar ting nge 'dzin gyi 'phen pa zad de shi ba'i rjes su slar yang 'dod khams kyi sdug bsngal mngon gyur spyod dgos tshul legs par bsgom mo//

Regarding the sufferings of the other two kinds of fortunate rebirths, the Friendly Letter says:
It is said that your complexion becomes unattractive, your seat loses its appeal, your flower garlands wilt, and your clothes start to smell; as for your body, it perspires for the first time. These five signs portending death from the higher states appear to gods residing in the divine realms.[468] Desire-realm gods are not subjected to sufferings like the birth and aging of humans, but when death approaches, their physical splendor suddenly fades, they no longer want to sit on their comfortable seats, their flower garlands wilt, their clothes acquire an unpleasant smell, and they perspire, which they never did before. These are the five signs of death’s approach. The signs that death is imminent are that their body’s radiance declines, ablution waters stick to their body, their clothing and ornaments make unpleasant sounds, their eyes blink, and they feel attached to specific objects. As they become conscious that the ten portend their death, they grow despondent. In particular, when those called [knowers of] three times[469] investigate the matter, they see where they will take rebirth. If they are certain to shortly be reborn in a hell, for example, they suffer horribly, exactly as if they had already been born there. [186] Humans can only surmise that they will be born in a hell and can never be absolutely certain of it, but it is different for gods, which is why their suffering is said to be far more devastating. Gods undergo other sufferings as well: those of lesser merit feel intimidated when they encounter gods of greater merit; more powerful gods banish the weaker; when battling demigods, gods kill others and are themselves killed — their bodies and limbs are cut and chopped to pieces. Gods of the form and formless realms do not experience manifest sufferings such as these. However, just as a ship’s pigeon eventually returns to its vessel, after the karma that projected such gods into a state of meditative concentration is depleted and they die, they must endure manifest suffering once more in the desire realm. Contemplate this well.

d.div: [109] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / shog_45_na6
[468] Nāgārjuna, Suhṛllekha, verses 99–100a, Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 45a6.
[469] The name given to certain desire-realm gods who are aware of their past life, their future life, and those of others.

f.d: gsum pa zhar byung rigs drug thun mong gi sdug bsngal bsam pa ni/
2.2.2.1.1.1.3. Sufferings shared by all six categories of life

gzhan yang 'khor ba las ma grol phyin chad bsod nams kyi mthus 'khor los sgyur ba'i rgyal po dang tshangs par gyur kyang slar bran du 'gyur ba lta bu ni 'grub pa'i sdug bsngal/ tshe 'di'i skye rga na 'chi'i sdug bsngal ni grub zin pa'i sdug bsngal/ 'bras tsha ba'i steng du tshwa chu btab pa'i 'gyur byed kyi reg pa dang 'phrad pas sdug bsngal cher song ba lta bu ni sdug bsngal gyi sdug bsngal/ phyin pas ngal ba na bsdad pas bde bar snang ba la nam zhig na yan lag dang sked pa na ba de 'gyur ba'i sdug bsngal/ 'khyags pa'i sbubs su chud pa zhig de las ma thar gyi bar du dro ba'i skabs med pa lta bu khyab pa 'du byed kyi sdug bsngal yin pas don hril gyi dril na zag bcas nyer len gyi phung po 'di blangs phyin chad da lta'i phung po la brten pa'i sdug bsngal myong zhing phyi ma'i sdug bsngal 'dren pa las 'os med/ nyer len gyi don 'dun pa dang 'dod chags yin pas dper na shing las byung ba'i me la shing gi me zer ba bzhin ma 'ongs pa'i lus thob 'dod dang da lta'i lus la chags pa'i dbang gis phung po 'grub pa rgyu la brten nas btags pa/ de bzhin du 'bras bu bskyed pa'i shing la 'bras bu'i shing du grags pa ltar grub pa'i phung po des 'dun pa dang 'dod chags bskyed pa 'bras bu'i sgo nas btags pa ste gcig las gcig byung bas 'khor bar 'khor ro//

As long as you are not free of samsara, you are exposed to future suffering. For example, you may become a universal sovereign or Brahmā by the power of your merit, but [once that is exhausted] you will again become a slave. Then there are present sufferings: those of birth, aging, illness, and death in this life. There is also manifest suffering, like pain made more acute when, say, salt water comes into contact with a festering boil. There is the suffering of change: when tired from walking, you experience a sense of well-being by resting, but after sitting for some time, your legs and back begin to hurt. The suffering of pervasive conditioning is analogous to the experience of being encased in ice — until you are free of it, you never know what it is to feel warm. To distill the significance of the above, once you have taken rebirth with impure appropriated aggregates, you are helplessly subjected to suffering because of your present aggregates, and they inevitably induce future suffering. Appropriated refers to aspiration and attachment. For example, just as a fire that issues from wood is called a wood fire, so too are the aggregates named after the causes that produce them: the desire for a future body and attachment to the present body. Similarly, just as a tree that bears fruit is known as a fruit tree, so too are the aggregates named after their results, for once they are produced, they give rise to aspiration and attachment. [187] As one leads to another, you turn in samsara.

bshad ma thag pa'i sdug bsngal der ma zad yid brtan du mi rung ba ni bshes spring las/
pha ni bu nyid ma ni chung ma nyid/ / skye bo dgrar gyur pa dag bshes nyid dang / / ldog pa nyid du mchis pas de slad du/ / 'khor ba dag na nges pa 'ga' ma mchis/[110] / zhes pha ma dang gnyen bshes dgra gnyen mang po go ldog pa skye ba rim brgyud la 'ong bar ma zad tshe 'dir yang tshe stod la shin tu mdza' ba dag tshe smad la dgrar 'gyur ba dang / lo sngon ma gcig gis gcig gsod du cha ba'i mi zhig lo rting ma gnyen gyi dwangs mar 'gro ba sogs mngon sum gyis grub pas dgra gnyen la nges gzung gi yid brtan mi thub pas nges pa med pa'i sdug bsngal bsam/

In addition to the aforementioned sufferings, there is that of uncertainty, regarding which the Friendly Letter says:
As fathers become sons, mothers become wives, those who were your enemies become your friends, and the contrary occurs as well, nothing is certain for beings in cyclic existence.[470] Relationships with parents, companions, friends, and enemies are often reversed not only over consecutive births but within single lives as well. Beloved ones of the first half of your life may very well become your enemies in the second half. Someone you thought to do away with last year, and who would have killed you as well, may by next year become a very dear friend and the like. This is all plain to see, which means you cannot rely on amiable and inimical relationships with any certainty. In these terms you contemplate the suffering of uncertainty.

d.div: [110] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / shog_43_ba6
[470] Nāgārjuna, Suhṛllekha, verse 66, Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 43b6.

f.d:
chog mi shes pa ni bshes sbring las/
ji ltar mdze can srin bus nyen pa ni/ / bde ba'i don du me la kun brten kyang / / zhi bar mi 'gyur de dang 'dra bar ni/ / 'dod pa rnams la chags pa'ang mkhyen par mdzod/[111] / ces sngon chad phun sum tshogs pa'i lha'i bdud rtsi/ bar ma ma'i nu zho/ tha ma mi gtsang ba'i khu ba dang khro chu khol ma btungs pa'ang rgya mtsho chen po grangs med pa las ches mang mod/ des kyang ngoms su med pa mdze can me la brten pa'i dpe ltar 'dod pa'i longs spyod la ngoms mi shes par bsam/

Regarding discontent with what you have, the Friendly Letter comments:
A leper infested with maggots, despite seeking relief by approaching a fire, is not appeased; know that it is the same for attachment to sense objects.[471] Although in the past you drank the choice nectar of the gods, then mother’s milk, and finally sewage and molten bronze in volumes far surpassing those of countless great oceans, still you feel dissatisfied. Contemplate your inability to ever feel fulfilled by experiencing objects of desire, like a leper who sits by a fire.

d.div: [111] sde dge_4183_bstan/ spring yig_nge mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / shog_42_na1
[471] Ibid., verse 26, 42a1.

f.d:
lus rten bgrang mi nus pa ni mya ngan gsal ba las/
phan tshun 'thab dang brtsod pa'i phyir/ / mgo bo bcad pa gang yin pa/ / spungs na de ltar mtho ba ni/ / tshangs pa'i 'jig rten las kyang thal/[112] / zhes nad sna tshogs kyi sgo nas lus dor ba gzhan rnams phar zhog /mtshon gyis gtubs te shi ba'i mgo bo rnams spungs na tshangs pa'i 'jig rten las mtho bar 'gyur bas/ da dung 'khor ba las ma thar na lus yang yang 'dor ba'i snang tshul de las ma 'das snyam du bsam/

On the impossibility of calculating the number of your bodies, Dispelling Sorrow explains:
If all the heads you had cut off in fights and quarrels with others were placed in a pile, its height would surpass that of the Brahmā realms.[472] Putting aside the bodies you lost to various illnesses, and so on, if you were to heap together just the heads you lost each time it was cut off by a blade, the pile would reach higher than the Brahmā realms. Think, “If I do not free myself from cyclic existence, the process of repeatedly giving up my body will never end.”

d.div: [112] sde dge_4177_bstan/ spring yig_nge _slob dpon rta dbyangs/ mya ngan bsal ba/ shog_34_na5
[472] Aśvaghoṣa, Śokavinodana, Toh 4177 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 34a5.

f.d:
mngal sgo grangs med 'grim pa ni/
ma yi thug mtha' rgya shug tshi gu tsam/ / ri lur bgrangs kyang sa yis lang mi 'gyur/[113] / zhes rang cag gi rtsa ba'i ma/ de'i ma/ de'i yang ma zhes bgrang ba'i ched du sa chen po 'di ril bu chung ngur dril nas bgrangs kyang 'dren mi thub pa thug mtha' zhes pa'i nus pas dngos su bstan nas/ don gyis rang gi ma yang bgrang bar mi nus pa'i phyir na sngar nying mtshams sbyar ba dang slad nas sbyor bar 'gyur ba la yid nges par 'byung bar bya'o//

With regard to passing through countless birth canals [the Friendly Letter] says:
If you were to count back to your original mother using pellets of earth the size of juniper berries, there would never be enough soil.[473] If you were to try to tally your personal mother, her mother, and again her mother, and so on using small pellets of earth made of this vast planet’s soil, it would be impossible [for lack of sufficient soil]. [188] This is the explicit meaning of the expression “original [mother],” but the actual meaning is that you cannot count how many mothers you have had [over past lives]. Based on this, you generate renunciation in relation to your past and future conceptions.

d.div: [113] sde dge_4177_bstan/ spring yig_nge _slob dpon rta dbyangs/ mya ngan bsal ba/ shog_43_ba7
[473] Nāgārjuna, Suhṛllekha, verse 68, Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 43b7.

f.d:
mtho dma' ma nges pa ni/
brgya byin 'jig rten mchod 'os gyur nas ni/ / las kyi dbang gis phyir yang sa steng lhung / / 'khor los sgyur ba nyid du gyur nas kyang / / 'khor ba dag tu yang bran nyid du 'gyur/[114] / zhes lha rnams kyi bdag po brgya byin dang 'khor los sgyur ba'i rgyal po'i go 'phang thob kyang sngar byas kyi mi dge ba'i las ma zad pa'i mthus de la gsos 'debs pa po byung na yang bran dang ngan song sogs dman pa'i gnas su skye bar 'gyur zhing rang 'od kyis 'jig rten snang bar byed pa'i nyi zla yang mun pa'i smag rum du skye ba dang / stobs 'byor gyi dregs pas myos pa mang po'ang rgyal po'i chad las dang pha rol gyi dgra zlas bcom pas khas zhan la mnga' thang dang bral ba'i tshul rnams bsam/

On the uncertainty of high and low status it also says:
Although as Indra you might become worthy of the world’s honors, by the power of karma, you will fall again to the earth. Although you might become a universal sovereign, in samsara, you will revert to being the slave of a slave.[474] Reflect on the fact that though you become Indra, king of the gods, or a universal sovereign, if something occurs to activate a nonvirtuous karma produced in the past and not yet spent, you will later be reborn with inferior status as the slave of a slave, or in an unfortunate realm. Even if you are born as the sun and moon,[475] who illuminate the world with their light, you will later be reborn in dense gloom. Ponder how many people drunk with pride in their own power and wealth are punished by kings or destroyed by their adversaries and end up powerless and wretched.

d.div: [114] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / shog_43_ba7
[474] Ibid., verse 69, 43b7.
[475] In Indian culture the sun and moon are regarded as sentient beings.

f.d:
thams cad shul du lus 'gro ba ni spyod 'jug las/
lus 'di gcig pu byung ba yang / / lhan cig skyes pa'i sha rus dag/ / zhig ste so sor 'gyes 'gyur na/ / mdza' ba gzhan dag ci zhig smos/[115] / zhes 'chi ba'i dus su grogs med gcig pur 'gro ba'i tshul rnams la yid 'jigs zhum zhum pa ma byung gi bar du bsgom mo/ / bshad ma thag pa'i sdug bsngal de dag kyang rang re rnams kyis sngon chad myong zin pa dang / da lta'i spyod tshul la dpags na slar thog tu 'bab pa las 'os med de/ po to ba'i zhal nas/
rigs drug gang du skyes phan chad na tsha dang 'chi ba la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal 'byung ba ni na rgyu cig na ba yin/ 'chi rgyu cig 'chi ba yin gyi de la mi 'os pa cig glo bur du byung ba min/ 'khor ba'i mtshan nyid dam rang bzhin yin/ 'khor bar gnas ring la de las ma 'das/ rang cag de la yid 'byung na skye ba spong dgos/ de la rgyu spong dgos zhes gsungs pas kyang shes so// //

As for having to leave everything behind, the Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Although a body arises whole, if the flesh and bones that come with it disintegrate and scatter, what is to be said of other companions?[476] Contemplate this until you shrink in fear at how when you die, you have to go on alone, friendless. In the past you have already experienced the sufferings just explained, and given your present behavior, it is only fitting that they should befall you again. Potowa says:
Regarding the sufferings of illness, death and so on, once you have been born in one of the six classes, you fall sick because you must fall sick and die because you must die. It is not as if these events occur unexpectedly and unjustly, for they define and characterize cyclic existence. As long as you remain in samsara, they are unavoidable. If you are fed up with them, the Buddha taught that you must give up taking birth, and for this you must abandon its causes.[477] This is easy to understand.

d.div: [115] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 8_sh+loka_32_shog_24_ba3
