f.d:
phar phyin bsdus pa las/
slong ba mngon du 'ongs nas rgyal sras des/ / rdzogs pa'i byang chub tshogs ni spel ba'i phyir/ / des gzhan 'du shes bdag la bzhag byas shing / / dge ba'i bshes gnyen 'du shes de la bskyed/[157] / ces 'di la brten nas sbyin pa'i phar phyin rdzogs par bya'o snyam pa dgos pa la dmigs pa dang / dang po nas bdag gi chos dang gzhan skyob pa'i nus pa dang bdog pa thams cad gzhan la btang zin pa yin pas bcol ba'i rdzas len pa dang mtshungs pa yin snyam du dngos po la dmigs pa dang / 'di rnams bdag gi sbyin pa'i phar phyin rdzogs par byed pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen yin no snyam pa'i zhing la dmigs pa ste bsam pa khyad par gsum ldan gyi sgo nas ji ltar gtong na/ chos zab pa sbas nas mi zab pa ston pa dang / 'jigs pa thams cad sel nus bzhin du phyogs re tsam skyob pa dang / dngos po ngan pa dang grangs nyung ba dang gzhan gyi lag nas phrogs te ster ba sogs kha na ma tho ba'i nyes pas ma gos shing / bzhin mdangs gsal zhing 'dzum pa/ ngag snyan par smra ba/ gzhan la 'tshe ba med cing rang gi dka' spyad khur du bzod pa'i sgo nas sbyin bya'i yul dgra gnyen bar ma yon tan can skyon can mtho dma' mnyam gsum skyid pa dang sdug pa ste bcur bshad pa'i dgos pa dgra la byams pa yon tan can la dang ba sogs so sor ngos zin pa'i ched de don dril na der sems can thams cad 'dus pas skabs dang bstun nas

The Condensed Presentation of the Perfections says:
When directly approached by a person requesting something, bodhisattvas, to increase their collections for complete enlightenment, identify their [possessions] as belonging to others and regard the person as their spiritual teacher.[533] The way to view the purpose is to think, “In this way may I complete the perfection of generosity.” The way to view your things is to think, “Since from the start I gave all my Dharma, ability to protect others, and belongings to others, now it is like borrowing the things I have entrusted to others [to give them again].” [220] The way to view the recipients is to think, “These people are like spiritual teachers; thanks to them I will complete my perfection of generosity.” These are the three specific thoughts to have when being generous. As to how to give, giving should not be sullied by untoward faults such as concealing profound teachings and giving easier ones; giving only partial protection when you can protect from all fears; giving things of inferior quality, few things, or things you have taken from others by force. Give with an open and friendly expression, speak in a pleasant manner that is free of any hostility toward others, and accept the hardship involved. Ten kinds of recipients are taught: enemies, friends, neutral beings, those with good qualities, those with shortcomings, superiors, inferiors, equals, the happy, and the wretched. In sum, as the list includes all beings, the point is to identify them individually and to adapt your attitude to each — to love your enemies, admire those with many good qualities, and so on.

d.div: [157] sde dge_3944_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_slob dpon dpa' bo/ pha rol tu phyin pa bsdus pa/ sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i le'u/ shog_221_na7
[533] Āryaśūra, Pāramitāsamāsa, Toh 3944, dbu ma, khi, 221a7.

f.d: chos kyi sbyin pa ni theg pa che chung gi dam pa'i chos gsung rab dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa dang / sgra tshad bzo gso la sogs pa thun mong ba'i rig gnas sogs lhag bsam dag pa'i sgo nas rang gis ji ltar shes pa bzhin ston cing bslab pa'i gzhi 'dzin du 'jug pa sogs nyan pa po'i blo dang sbyar nas 'di dag rnams kyis thos bsam sgom gsum byas nas rang gzhan gyi don rgya chen po 'grub par gyur cig snyam du bsam zhing ngag tu yang brjod dgos te/ chos bshad pa'i rjes su dge ba bsngo ba mtshan nyid dang ldan pa'i bshes gnyen rnams kyi phyag len du snang ngo // der ma zad rang nyid chos 'chad pa po'i ming du btags pa min yang grogs skye bo gzhan dag sdig pa mi dge ba la 'jug pa 'dug na gleng mo'i tshul gyis blang dor bstan te de las bzlog nas dge ba la sbyor ba sogs bsam pa khyad par gsum ldan gyi sgo nas chos sbyin la dngos su 'bad cing /

Giving the Dharma is teaching, according to your knowledge, the Buddha’s sacred words of both the Great and Lesser Vehicles, the commentaries, and the ordinary sciences — grammar, logic, technology, medicine, and so on — with a genuinely altruistic intention. It includes conferring vows and so on consistent with the capacity of those listening. You should also make the wish, “Once they have studied, reflected, and meditated on these, may they accomplish much for the sake of others and for their sake!” After teaching the Dharma, the tradition of authentic spiritual teachers is to dedicate the virtue created. Furthermore, you may not be known as a teacher, but if your friends or others are involved in wrongdoing or nonvirtue, you can point out their errors, explain to them what to adopt and what to reject, and have them stop it and accomplish virtue instead. In this way, with the three specific thoughts,[534] truly strive to give the Dharma.

d.div: [534] See above: the view of the purpose of giving, the view of the things to give, and the view of the recipient.

f.d: dngos su sbyin par bya ba'i yul ma rnyed na snying thag pa nas sems can thams cad la dam pa'i chos bstan par mos shing chos kyi sbyin pa de'i mthus phan pa rgya chen po byung bar bsam pa/ dper na chos kyi sgra thos pas dmyal ba pa rnams gnas ngan len sdug bsngal las thar bar mos pa sogs kyi sgo nas smon lam khyad par can gdab/ de bzhin du sems can rnams la rgyal po'i chad pas nag can khrims la sbyor ba/ gcan gzan dang dgra la sogs pas lus srog longs spyod la rgol ba/ me dang chu la sogs pa'i 'jigs pa rnams las dngos su rang stobs kyis nus na bskyab/ mi nus na de las thar pa'i thabs bstan/ 'jig rten gyi khams gzhan du sdug bsngal 'di dag gis mnar ba dpag tu med pa yod pas de dag rnams la mi 'jigs pa'i sbyin pa btang ba dang de'i mthus 'jigs pa las grol bar snying thag pa nas bsam/ rang byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i mthu ldan du gyur bar mos blos sprul te tsha ba'i dmyal bar char chen po phab nas me bsad pa sogs dmigs pa dang smon lam 'debs/ zang zing gi sbyin pa yang bza' btung gnas mal/ na ba'i gsos sman/ dar zab rin chen/ rta glang po/ sa mkhar yul zhing / mgo bo mig yan lag nying lag sogs lus longs spyod thams cad bsam pa khyad par gsum ldan gyi sgo nas sbyin zhing / rang nyid bkres shing phongs bas de ltar byar med tshe/ dper na zas g.yos su byas pa dang ma byas pa dpag tu med pa sprul nas yi dwags sogs bkres pas nyen pa'i 'gro ba rnams la sbyin pas sdug bsngal de las thar par bsam pa sogs yul dang rdzas skabs thob sbyar te rgya chen por spro ba ni byang sems shes rab can gyi sbyin pa yin pas bshad ma thag pa'i sbyin pa'i nyams len gsum po de yang 'di nas bzung ste chos tshigs bcad bzhi pa yan chad ston pa/ tsha bas gdungs ba la bsil ba'i gnas khang ston pa/ ngan slong la zas gos ster ba sogs nus pa rnams dngos su bya dgos kyi/ nus bzhin du dmigs pas byed pa ni rang mgo rang gis g.yogs par gsung / de ltar sngar bshad pa rnams nges par byas nas sbyin pa gtong ba'i dngos po la yid chags pa'i ser sna dang / bdag la longs spyod med pas ster mi nus snyam pa dang / dngos po yid du 'ong ba la dmigs bsal gyi chags sems gang 'dug pa de legs par brtag/ / bdag sngar yi dwags dang rnam thos kyi bu sogs mtho dma' bgrang gis mi lang bar skyes 'dug na'ang da lta'i snang tshul ni 'di ltar 'dug/ / dngos po 'di las lhag pa yid bzhin nor bu thob nas de dang bral ba bsam gyis mi khyab snyam yang yang bsams te mi mthun phyogs mgo gnon/ gtong sems mngon gyur skyes kyang lan dang rnam smin la re ba'i bsam pa shas che ba 'dug na/ sngar mchod sbyin grangs med pa zhig byas te brgya byin dang tshangs pa sogs kyi go 'phang thob kyang don med du song 'dug pas da res zas kham gcig sbyin par btang ba yan chad bla na med pa'i byang chub kyi rgyur bsngo snyam pa'i 'dun pa du re ba dang bcas thun dngos gzhi la yid kyis sprul te sbyin pa gsum po gtong ba'i dmigs pa nan tan dang / thun mtshams su dngos su gtong ba dang yid goms pa la 'bad par bya/

If you have no one to whom to be generous in this manner, imagine that you are teaching the perfect Dharma to all sentient beings and that they thereby benefit greatly from this gift. You can visualize, for example, that hearing the teaching frees hell beings of suffering and its causes, and you can make excellent prayers on their behalf. [221] [Giving protection from fears:] Similarly, if you have the power to do so directly, you should protect sentient beings from the fears of being sentenced to death by a political leader, the fears of having their body, belongings, and their very life harmed by wild animals or enemies, and from the fears of fire, floods, and the like. If you lack that ability, you can explain to others how to overcome these. Since there are countless beings in other realms undergoing such sufferings, think from the depths of your heart that you provide them with the gift of protection and that thanks to this their terrors cease. Imagine that, empowered by generating the aspiration to enlightenment, you mentally emanate heavy rains that fall on the hot hells and extinguish its fires, or you wish for it to happen. As for giving material gifts, with the three specific thoughts in mind, you give food, beverages, beds, medicine for the sick, fine silks and gems, horses and elephants, land, buildings, domains, fields, your eyes, head, major and secondary limbs — in other words, your entire body — and all your belongings. When you are hungry and poor yourself and cannot manage this, imagine that you emanate large quantities of food, both raw and cooked, and give it to hungry ghosts and other beings suffering from starvation, thanks to which their deprivation ends. You are to adapt what you give to the recipients. Wise bodhisattvas practice generosity by emanating these extensively. From now on, as much as you are able, try to actually accomplish the three practices of generosity just explained — teaching the Dharma starting from as little as four lines, showing those suffering from the heat where they can find shelter, giving food and clothes to the poor, and the like. It is taught that if you are capable of these but you content yourself with just doing visualizations, you are deceiving yourself. Having ascertained what I explained above, carefully check whether you are stingy due to attachment to the things to be given, whether you tend to think, “Since I do not have many belongings myself, I cannot give any away,” or whether you are particularly attached to beautiful things. To curb these inappropriate attitudes, reflect repeatedly as follows: Although in the past I was born countless times in high states as the child of Vaiśravaṇa and the like and in low states as a hungry ghost and so on, this is the state I am in now. [222] While I often acquired things, like wish-granting gems, that were far superior to what I own now, I have lost them all. If you have a real intention to give but it is most often in the hope of receiving something in return or with expectations regarding the maturation effect, continuously inspire yourself thinking: Although in the past I made offerings and was generous countless times and, as a result, attained the states of Īśvara, Brahmā, and so on, it was all in vain. Now when I give so much as a morsel of food, I will dedicate it in such a way that it becomes a cause of supreme enlightenment. During meditation sessions, be sure to visualize giving in the three ways by emanating gifts mentally. Between sessions endeavor to actually give, and familiarize yourself with the idea of giving.

des na sbyin pa gsum po de bya nus tshad nyams su blang bar bya'am snyam na/ mtha' gcig tu ma nges te/ spyod 'jug las/
snying rje'i bsam pa ma dag par/ / lus ni btang bar mi bya ste/ / ci nas 'di dang gzhan du yang / / don chen 'grub pa'i rgyur btang ngo /[158] / zhes snying rje chen pos lus kyi sha gcod pa sogs kyi dka' spyad bsgribs te yid mi 'byung ba ma rnyed kyi bar dang / dgos pa chung ngu'i ched dang / bdud rigs kyis mtho 'tshams pa dang smyon pa sogs kyis slong ba la lus kyi sbyin pa dus dang dgos pa dang sbyin yul gyi sgo nas ster du mi rung ba ni lus kyi dngos po gtong mi gtong gi khyad par dang / phyi'i dbang du byas na blo shin tu dman pa la theg pa chen po'i chos ston pa dang / rab tu byung ba la phyi dro'i kha zas dus kyi sgo nas ster du mi rung / sdom brtson la sha chang sgog btsong lhag ma mi gtsang bas sbags pa/ pha rol gyis gnod pa byed nges pa'i srog chags/ nad pa la mi 'phrod pa'i zas/ tshod bgam pa dang nor gyi 'du shes can la glegs bam lta bu yul gyi sgo nas ster du mi rung ba/ mi 'dod pas sdug bsngal bzhin du bran ster ba lta bu dngos po'i sgo nas sbyin du mi rung ba/ ma rung ba zhig rgyal po'i phyag sbal nas 'thon na 'gro ba grangs med pa sdug bsngal la sbyor ba btson ra'i 'jigs pa las skyob pa'i sbyin pa dang / gnod sems kyis slong ba la dug mtshon sogs sbyin pa ni dgos pa'i sgo nas sbyin du mi rung bas spyir btang dmigs bsal legs par phyed par byas nas bdag kyang myur du 'chi ba'i chos can yin pas/ btang bya'i dngos po 'di rnams kyis kyang bdag 'dor/ bdag gis kyang 'di rnams 'dor bas gang la yang snying po med snyam du snying thag pa nas gtong sems la goms par bya ba legs so// //

You may wonder whether you are to practice giving in the three ways to the maximum of your ability, but this is not necessarily the case. Guide to the Bodhisattva Way explains:
Without powerful compassion, do not give away your body, or if you do, give it to accomplish important goals for this and future lives.[535] From the perspective of time, purpose, and recipient, it is inappropriate to give away your body until your compassion is so great that it defuses the painful austerity of cutting off your flesh; nor is it right to give it for a limited purpose, to demons who intend to cause harm, or when someone like a madman begs you for it. This is how to determine whether to give away your body. Regarding external factors, it is unfitting from a temporal perspective to teach the Mahayana to those of very inferior capacity and to offer food to monastics in the evening. When it comes to the recipient, it is inappropriate to give meat, alcohol, garlic, onions, leftovers, and unclean food to those observing vows, to give animals to people who are very likely to harm them, to give harmful food to sick people, and to give books to those who see them only for their monetary value or to those who just want to test you. Regarding the objects given, it is not right to give servants away if it would make them unhappy by going against their wishes. Giving that is unsuitable in terms of purpose is, for example, providing criminals protection from the fear of incarceration by releasing them from prison, as it would make many people suffer, or giving poison, weapons, and so on when those seeking them have malevolent intentions. Once you have carefully studied the general principles and the particular cases, reflect as follows: “Since I am doomed to die soon, [223] the things I could give away will let me down, and I too will have to give them up; as such they are utterly futile.” In this way cultivate a heartfelt intention to give.

d.div: [158] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 5_sh+loka_87_shog_13_ba4
[535] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 5.87, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 13b4.

f.d:
smras pa/
yid gtong sems drag pos lus longs spyod/ / drin 'khor thabs med pa'i 'gro ba la/ / dus grangs med byin pas gtan bde'i nor/ / gter 'dzad med bang mdzod deng 'dir grub/ /
lar mi bzad dbul phongs sdug bsngal 'di/ / rang gcig pu'i thog tu bab min pa'i/ / ma 'gro ba kun gyi snang tshul te/ / 'di brtags na blo yis bzod thabs med/ /
sngar dkar min las mang bsags pa'i mthus/ / dus da lta'i snang tshul 'di ltar na/ / da sbyin pa'i phar phyin rdzogs byas nas/ / mtha' mi mngon sems can sgrol bar smon/ / zhes bya ba ni bar skabs kyi tshigs su bcad pa'o// //

d.div: By giving body and belongings, with an intense wish to give, to beings whose kindness cannot be repaid, I achieve over endless periods of time a store of inexhaustible wealth — the jewel of stable happiness.
Moreover, the endless suffering of poverty does not befall me alone. It is the lot of all mother sentient beings as well. Upon reflection, the thought of it is unbearable.
Having committed scores of dark deeds in the past, such is the situation I find myself in now. Once I have completed the perfection of generosity, I pray that I may liberate boundless beings.

f.d: gnyis pa tshul khrims kyi phar phyin ni
2.2.3.2.1.2. The perfection of ethical discipline

spyod 'jug las/
nya la sogs pa gang zhig tu/ / de dag gsod mi 'gyur bar bskrad/ / spong ba'i sems ni thob pa las/ / tshul khrims pha rol phyin par bshad/[159] / ces gzhan la gnod pa gzhi dang bcas pa las yid phyir log pa'i spong sems ni tshul khrims yin zhing / sems de la goms pa gong nas gong du yongs su rdzogs pas tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin par 'gyur ba yin pas sems can thams cad gnod 'tshe dang bral ma bral la bltos mi dgos so/ /

Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Where could fish and the like be sent to escape being killed? It is said that ethical discipline is perfected by achieving the intention to abstain.[536] Ethical discipline is the intention to abstain that is desisting from harming others and from the thought to harm others. The perfection of ethical discipline is gradual and increasing familiarization with this intention until it is complete. It does not depend on all sentient beings having been freed of harm.

d.div: [159] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 5_sh+loka_11_shog_10_ba3

f.d:
de yang nyes spyod sdom pa'i tshul khrims la lam sgron du/
so so thar pa rigs bdun gyi/ / rtag tu sdom gzhan ldan pa la/ / byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa yi/ / skal ba yod kyi gzhan du min/[160] / zhes pa'i tshig la 'khrul nas so sor thar pa'i tshul khrims dngos bstan la khas blangs tshe byang sems kyi bslab pa la slob pa'i rten can du gyur pa'i lha yod pas/ lam sgron 'grel par/ da ni tshul khrims kyi sdom pa'i rten khyad par can bstan par 'dod nas [161] zhes bshad pas khyad par can ma yin pa'i thun mong ba zhig bshad pa mi rigs mod/

On the [bodhisattva] ethical discipline of abstention from wrongdoing, Lamp on the Path to Enlightenment states:
Those who maintain [one of] the seven vows for individual liberation other than the [bodhisattva] vows have the good fortune to take bodhisattva vows, while others do not.[537] Some misinterpret this and say that it means one must have prātimokṣa vows [before taking the bodhisattva precepts]. However, there are gods [who lack prātimokṣa vows] who have a valid basis for training in bodhisattva precepts. [224] The Commentary on Lamp on the Path explains this saying, “Now I would like to describe the superior basis for [bodhisattva] vows of ethical discipline.”[538] It is therefore incorrect to assert that [the Lamp] is referring to a universal basis and not a superior one.

d.div: [160] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_jo bo rje dpal ldan a ti sha_byang chub lam gyi sgron ma/ shog_239_na4
[161] sde dge_3948_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_jo bo rje dpal ldan a ti sha_byang chub lam gyi sgron ma'i dka' 'grel/ shog_258_na5
[537] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 239a4.
[538] Atiśa, Bodhimārgapradīpapāñjikā, Toh 3948 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 258a5.

f.d:
'o na gang la ngos 'dzin snyam na so thar gyi sdom ldan byang sems kyi bslab pa la bslabs pa zhig yin na so thar gyi sdom pa dngos de dang thun mong ba'i spong sdom ni skabs 'di'i sdom pa'i tshul khrims la ngos 'dzin la/ so thar gyi sdom ldan min na so thar dang thun mong ba mi dge bcu spong ba'i spong sdom de la nyes spyod sdom pa'i tshul khrims su ngos 'dzin pa'i phyir na phar phyin bsdus pa las/
mtho ris thar pa'i bde lam gyur pa ste/ / las lam bcu po 'di las nyams mi bya/ / 'di la gnas pas 'gro la phan sems pa'i/ / bsam pa'i khyad par 'bras bu yod par 'gyur/[162] / zhes rab byung yin na mkhan slob kyi drung du khas blangs pa'i rtsa ba dang yan lag gi nyes pas gos ma gos dang / so thar gyi sdom pa dang mi ldan na sngar skyes bu chung ngu'i skabs su bshad pa'i mi dge ba bcu'i dbang du song ma song yang yang dran shes kyis brtag cing / bka' gdams gong ma rnams kyi phyag len ltar nyin re zhing dge sdig gang byas la rde'u dkar nag btang nas/ brtsis pas dkar po mang ba la spro ba dang nag po mang ba la 'gyod sems drag po'i sgo nas thun dngos gzhi la thog mar rde'u nag po'i grangs ji tsam byung gi sdig pa dran shes kyis zin pa rnams la phyir 'chos dang bshags sdom gnyen po stobs bzhi tshang ba'i sgo nas bya ba dang / bdag gi tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par gyur cig snyam du bsam pa dang ngag nas kyang brjod cing / chags sems kyi yul la chags pa drag po skyes pa kha rgyal du ma btang bar kha na ma tho ba'i nyes pa dang mi sdug pa dran pa'i sgo nas mgo gnon pa sogs nyon mongs gang che ba de la rnam smin sogs bsams nas gnyen po bsten te bsgoms pas tshul khrims dag pa zhig 'ong / mi dge ba bcu spong ba'i tshul de skyes bu gsum gar byung ba ngo bo 'dra yang bsam pa'i khyad par gyis dbye dgos so//

How is this category of ethical discipline to be identified? When those having prātimokṣa vows train in bodhisattva precepts, the vow of abstention concordant with their actual vow for personal liberation[539] in the present context is identified as the bodhisattva ethical discipline of abstention. For those who do not have a prātimokṣa vow, the vow of abstention that is avoidance of the ten nonvirtues and is concordant with the vows for personal liberation is identified as the [bodhisattva] ethical discipline of abstention from wrongdoing. The Condensed Presentation of the Perfections states:
Do not let the ten karmic paths decline, for they are the easy path to high rebirth and liberation. By sustaining them with the superior attitude that is the wish to benefit beings, you attain the result [bodhisattva vows].[540] If you are ordained, you must repeatedly check with mindfulness and meta-awareness whether you have been sullied by the primary and secondary transgressions you promised in the presence of your preceptor to abstain from. When you do not have a prātimokṣa vow, you are to verify whether you have committed any of the ten nonvirtues explained above in the path of persons of lesser capacity. According to the custom of past Kadam masters, you are to note daily the virtues and sins you accomplish using black and white stones. After calculation, you rejoice when you find more white stones than black and feel great remorse when there are more black than white. In sessions, first you confess the sins that mindfulness and meta-awareness catch, consistent with the number of black stones, and do restoration practice applying all four remedial powers. You are also to think and repeat, “May I complete the perfection of ethical discipline!” When strong feelings of attachment arise in relation to objects of desire, do not give them free rein but curb them by contemplating their unattractiveness and recalling the drawbacks of wrongdoing. Having reflected on the consequences of whichever affliction is strongest, apply its remedies. By these meditations, you will achieve pure ethical discipline. Although by nature the way to abstain from the ten nonvirtues is similar for each of the three kinds of persons,[541] the motivation specific to each differentiates them.

d.div: [162] sde dge_3944_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_slob dpon dpa' bo/ pha rol tu phyin pa bsdus pa/ tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i le'u/ shog_222_na2

[539] The vow for individual liberation (prātimokṣa) that is the vow to abstain from killing, for example, is concordant with the bodhisattva vow of abstention from killing but is not that latter vow because it taken for the duration of one’s present life alone while the bodhisattva vows are taken for all one’s lives. See Gomchen’s lamrim on page 116 above: “The vow of individual liberation within a bodhisattva’s mind / is the vow of ethical discipline, not the bodhisattva vow.”
[540] Āryaśūra, Pāramitāsamāsa, Toh 3944 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 222a2.
[541] Here, the three kinds of practitioners are persons of lesser, intermediate, and great capacity.

f.d: dge ba chos sdud kyi tshul khrims ni byang sems kyi tshul khrims dang ldan pas lus ngag gi dge ba byas pa rnams yin la/ de yang bslab pa gsum dang zhing khyad par can bla ma sogs la rim gro byed pa/ dkon mchog gsum la bsngags pa brjod cing gzhan gyi dge ba la yi rang ba'i tshig smra ba/ tshur gnod pa la sngon las su blta ba/ dge ba rnams bsngo smon gyi rgyas 'debs pa/ dkon mchog la mchod pa 'bul ba/ bag yod pas dge ba rgyun mi gcod pa/ dbang po'i sgo nyon mongs pa'i phyogs las srung ba/ zas kyi tshod rig pa/ nam gyi cha stod smad la rnal 'byor la brtson pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen nam ma rnyed na rang gis rang gi bshes gnyen byas te gnyen po bsten pa/ nyes pa rnams yul khyad par can la bshags pa rnams las/ ting nge 'dzin sgom pa lta bu thun dngos/ dkon mchog gi mchod pa'i sta gon sogs thun mtshams/ bag yod bsten pa dang shes bzhin gyi bya ra sogs ni gnyis ka la dgos shing bla ma la bsu ba dang stan bstab pa sogs ni dus kyi nges pa med mod/ da lta phyag len la thun dngos gzhi la bshad ma thag pa mtha' dag dpyad 'jog skabs dang sbyar te dmigs pa skyong ba lags/

The ethical discipline of collecting virtue consists of any physical or verbal virtue performed by those possessing the bodhisattva vows: cultivating the three trainings,[542] honoring any superior fields of action such as gurus, extolling the Three Jewels, expressing delight in others’ virtues, viewing harm done to you as the outcome of your past karma, dedicating virtue and making aspirational prayers, presenting offerings to the Three Jewels, practicing virtue conscientiously and continuously, guarding the doors of the senses from afflictions, eating in moderation, practicing diligently at the beginning and the end of the night, applying antidotes while relying on spiritual teachers or being your own guide if you have not found any, and confessing your transgressions to superior beings. [225] States of concentration are cultivated during meditation sessions, and preparations for making offerings to the Three Jewels and so on are done between sessions. In both contexts you must exercise conscientiousness, meta-awareness, and so on. The time for welcoming gurus, preparing their seats, and so on is indeterminate. According to the present tradition, in relation to all the above-mentioned practices, during sessions you engage in either analytical or placement meditations, whichever is appropriate.

d.div: [542] In the present context, “the three trainings” refers to cultivating the wisdoms of learning, reflection, and meditation.

f.d:
sems can don byed kyi tshul khrims ni byang chub sems dpa' sems can la phan 'dogs pa ste/ de la yang rnam pa bcu gcig tu bshad pa'i/ kha na ma tho ba med pa'i sgo nas longs spyod rkun pos mi 'khyer ba'i thabs bstan pa ni bya ba byed pa'i grogs kyi don byed pa dang / nad pa la sman dang rkang pa nyams pa la bzhon pas gnas su skyel ba lta bu ni sdug bsngal gyi grogs kyi don byed pa/ chos bstan nas nyes spyod las ldog pa'i thabs ston pa lta bu thabs la rmongs pa'i don byed pa/ bsnyen bkur sogs byed pa lta bu phan 'dogs pas don byed pa/ seng ge dang stag la sogs pa'i gnod pa las skyob pa lta bu 'jigs pas nyen pa'i don byed pa/ pha ma dang bral ba'am chom rkun gyis nor phrogs pa sogs mya ngan gyis zin pa la mi rtag pa'i gtam gyi sgo nas sel ba lta bu mya ngan gyis gzir ba'i don byed pa/ kha zas kyis dbul ba la yid du 'ong ba'i zas ster ba lta bu phongs pa'i don byed pa/ chos dang mthun pa'i gos ster ba dang 'dod chags can la mi sdug pa ston pa sogs gnas 'cha' bar 'dod pa'i don byed pa/ pha rol po dge ba la sbyor mi nus par mthong na mi 'dod pa'i lus ngag gi spyod lam spangs te _sems la phan par bya ba ni blo mthun par 'dod pa'i don byed pa/ tshul khrims sogs kyi yon tan la gzengs bstod pa ni yang dag par zhugs pa'i don byed pa/ sdig pa byas pa la chad pa gcod pa lta bu ni log par zhugs pa'i don byed pa/ dmyal ba sprul nas gzhan sdig pa las ldog ba lta bu dang cho 'phrul ya ma zung bstan nas gzhan 'dun par byed pa lta bu ni rdzu 'phrul gyi sgo nas gdul bya'i don byed pa ste bcu gcig po 'di dag la dngos su bya nus mi nus dang dus la nges mi nges sna tshogs kyang / thun dngos la dpyad sgom gyi tshul gyis nyams su len dgos pas tshig bshad tsam du ma song ba gnad du che/ de yang phar phyin bsdus pa las/
tshul khrims nyams pas rang don mi nus na/ / gzhan don tshul la mthu yod ga las 'ong / / de phyir gzhan don legs par brtson pa yis/ / 'di la rim gro glod par rigs ma yin/[163] / zhes don gnyis sgrub pa la tshul khrims 'di rtsa ba lta bur gsungs pas/ gzhan gnod gzhi bcas spong ba'i tshul khrims la goms pa gong nas gong du 'phel ba'i thabs bya 'tshal lo// //

The ethical discipline of helping sentient beings consists in bodhisattvas’ assistance to sentient beings. Eleven aspects are taught. (1a) In blameless ways, showing others how to prevent thieves stealing their belongings is helping those that need help in their activities. (1b) Providing the sick with medicine and the lame with transport to their destination are examples of helping those who are suffering. (2) Showing people how to reject wrongdoing by teaching the Dharma is an example of helping those who are unaware of the methods. (3) Providing hospitality and so on is helping those who have been helpful. (4) Protecting beings from harm by the likes of lions and tigers is helping those who are frightened. (5) Alleviating the distress of those who have lost their parents, had their belongings stolen by thieves and brigands, and so on by explaining about impermanence is helping those who are grieving. (6) Giving tasty food to those in want of it is an example of helping the poor. (7) Giving clothes adapted to a person’s religious status, explaining ugliness to people who have attachment, and so on is helping those wishing to live in a community. (8) When you encounter those who you fail to guide to virtue, refraining from physically or verbally indicating your disapproval and instead benefiting them [by adapting to them] is helping those who wish to befriend you. [226] (9) Praising good qualities such as ethical discipline is helping those who are practicing well. (10) Punishing the sinful, for example, is helping those engaged in wrongdoing. (11) Deterring others from sin by producing visions of hell realms, for example, or creating various magical displays to inspire others is helping disciples by means of supernormal powers. There are many variables; you may or may not be capable of all eleven, and it may or may not be the appropriate time for them. Nevertheless, you should practice them during sessions using analytical meditations. It is key to not content yourself with just enumerating them. The Condensed Presentation of the Perfections states:
If you cannot achieve personal goals because your ethics have declined, how will you ever be able to accomplish others’ aims? For that reason, while striving well for others’ sake, value [your ethics] and prevent their transgression.[543] It is taught that ethical discipline is the very root of achieving the two aims. As such, I ask you to apply the methods to increase your familiarization with the ethical discipline of rejecting ill will and harm toward others.

d.div: [163] sde dge_3944_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_slob dpon dpa' bo/ pha rol tu phyin pa bsdus pa/ tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i le'u/ shog_224_na1
[543] Āryaśūra, Pāramitāsamāsa, Toh 3944 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 224a1.

f.d:
smras pa/
phun tshogs dal 'byor rten gyi skyed tshal du/ / rnam gsum tshul khrims yongs 'du sa brtol la/ / myang 'das 'bras bu'i khur chen gyis dud par/ / phan bde'i ro brgya'i snying po ci yang 'dzag /
grangs med bskal par bsags pa'i sbyin pa yi/ / phung po gcig tu dkar ba'i longs spyod kyang / / lha mi'i rten la nyams su myong mi myong / / byed po tshul khrims kho nar rag lus na/ /
lan cig thob pa'i rten bzang shing rta 'di/ / bag med ltung ba'i 'dam du nyer bying ba/ / phyir bcos 'phrul gyis bde ba'i thang yangs por/ / mi 'don dal bar 'dug rnams gdon gyis brlams/ / zhes bya ba ni bar skabs kyi tshigs su bcad pa'o// //

d.div: In the garden of a life with excellent leisure and opportunity are wish-granting trees, the three kinds of ethical discipline, bowing under a great load of fruit, nirvana, that drips with luscious juices of happiness and benefit.

The numerous acts of generosity collected over countless eons are pure virtues for attaining wealth, but experiencing their results in a divine or human rebirth or failing to do so depends entirely on ethical discipline.

So when the cart, a good rebirth attained just this once, gets stuck through carelessness in the mire of transgressions, those who fail to drag it by restoration practice onto the broad expanse of happiness and instead remain idle must indeed be possessed by the devil [of ignorance].

f.d: gsum pa bzod pa'i phar phyin ni
2.2.3.2.1.3. The perfection of forbearance

spyod 'jug pas/
sems can mi srun nam mkha' bzhin/ / de dag gzhom gyis yongs mi lang / / khro ba'i sems 'di gcig bcom na/ / dgra de thams cad choms dang 'dra/ /
sa steng 'di dag kos g.yog tu/ / de snyed ko bas ga la lang / / lham mthil tsam gyi ko bas ni/ / sa steng thams cad g.yogs dang 'dra/ /
de bzhin phyi rol dngos po yang / / bdag gis phyir bzlog mi lang gi / bdag gi sems 'di phyir bzlog bya'i/ / gzhan rnams bzlog go ci zhig dgos/[164] / zhes rang gis 'gro ba rnams la khong khro ba la sogs pa 'gog pa'i sems kyi goms pa yongs su rdzogs pa de bzod pa'i phar phyin rdzogs pa yin gyi skye bu mtha' dag mi srun pa'i blo dang 'bral mi dgos pa yin pas/ zhi ba lhas/
bskal pa stong du bsags pa yi/ / sbyin dang bde gshegs mchod la sogs/ / legs spyad gang yin de kun kyang / / khong khro gcig gis 'joms par byed/[165] / ces yul dam pa la khong khro byas pas dge ba'i rtsa ba 'joms par thams cad yod smra ba'i gzhung las kyang byung zhing / dmigs bsal 'jug par/
gang phyir rgyal sras rnams la khros pa yis/ / sbyin dang khrims byung dge ba bskal pa brgyar/ / bsags pa skad cig gis 'joms de yi phyir/ / mi bzod las gzhan sdig pa yod ma yin/[166] / zhes byang sems stobs chung bas byang sems stobs che ba la khros par dge ba bskal brgyar bsags pa 'joms nus la byang sems min pa'i so skyes byang sems la khros na bskal pa stong gi dge ba'i 'bras bu mi 'byin pa sogs shin tu lci bar gsungs/

Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Unruly beings are [as infinite] as space, I cannot possibly overcome them all. If I could just overcome my anger, I will have overcome all my foes.
Where could I ever find enough leather to cover the entire surface of the earth? With just the leather of the soles of my shoes, I will have covered the surface of the earth.
Similarly, I cannot possibly control all external [harmful] elements, but once I have come to control my mind, what need is there to control anything else?[544] [227] The perfection of forbearance is accomplished once familiarization with the intention to halt anger and so on toward sentient beings is complete. It is not necessary that all beings be free of their unruly states of mind. Śāntideva states:
All the good deeds accomplished and collected over a thousand eons by acts of generosity, homage to the sugatas, and the like are destroyed by a moment’s anger.[545] Even the Sarvāstivādin texts state that anger toward a superior being destroys virtuous roots. Specifically, Entering the Middle Way states:
Since anger toward a bodhisattva destroys in an instant the virtue collected by giving and ethical discipline over a hundred eons, there is no greater sin than anger.[546] It is taught that if the anger of a less spiritually advanced bodhisattva toward a more advanced bodhisattva can destroy a hundred eons worth of virtues, then the anger of an ordinary being who is not a bodhisattva toward one is extremely grave: it renders a thousand eons’ worth of virtues unfruitful and so on.

[165] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 6_sh+loka_1_shog_14_ba3
[166] sde dge_3861_bstan/ dbu ma/ 'a_slob dpon zla ba grags pa/ dbu ma la 'jug pa/ sems bskyed/ 3_sh+loka_6_shog_203_na5
[544] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 4.12–14, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 10b4.
[546] Candrakīrti, Madhyamakāvatāra, 3.6, Toh 3861 Tengyur, dbu ma, ’a, 20a5.

f.d:
rang re rnams kyis khong khro ni rkyen chung ngu re la yang 'bad med du gsog /yul byang sems ni gang zag me dong thal bas g.yogs pa ltar gang na yod cha med pas sngar byas kyi dge ba ni gtan brlag lta bur song zin 'dug pas rgud pa kun gyi rtsa bar nges shing / zhi ba lhas/
gang zhig bsgrims te khro 'joms pa/ / de ni 'di dang gzhan du bde/[167] / zhes khro ba spangs na tshe 'dir lus sems mi mnar bar ma zad/ skye ba mtha' dag tu bde ba'i rgyur snang bas bzod pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa la bslab snyam pa'i yid du re ba dang bcas te/

Anger arises in us at the slightest provocation, without the least effort. As for the objects of anger, bodhisattvas are like coals covered in ash in that we cannot know for sure where they are, which is how we have obliterated our virtue in the past and why anger is definitely the root of all our troubles. Śāntideva continues:
Whoever strives then defeats anger finds happiness now and hereafter.[547] Renouncing anger not only delivers from short-term mental and physical suffering, it also brings happiness in all lives. Therefore, with determination, think, “I will train in the perfection of forbearance.”

d.div: [167] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 6_sh+loka_6_shog_14_ba6
[547] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 6.6, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 14b6.

f.d:
thog mar gnod byed kyis gnod pa byed bzhin pa yin na dang / min na sngar byas pa zhig bsal btab nas zhe sdang dmar lam pa skyes byung ba'i tshe de'i ngo bo la bltas nas/ spyod 'jug las/
gang tshe nyon mongs dbang gyur pas/ / bdag sdug nyid kyang gsod byed pa/ / de tshe de dag gzhanalu sa la/ / gnod mi byed par ji ltar 'gyur/[168] / zhes dper na la la gzhan la mi dga' ba'i nyon mongs drag po skyes pa na rang lceb pa dang mtshon 'debs pa g.yang la mchong ba sogs rang srog rang gis gcod pa mngon sum gyis grub bas bdag gces 'dzin gyis rang la rang gis gnod pa bya mi nus bzhin du nyon mongs pa'i gzhan dbang gis de ltar byed pa la khro ba'i go skabs med na/ 'gro ba gzhan nyon mongs pa'i shugs drag pos rang dbang dang bral te gnod pa byed pa la ci'i phyir khro snyam du bsam/

First visualize a malevolent person who is hurting you now, or if there isn’t one, someone who harmed you in the past. Once this has prompted red-hot anger in you, observe it and reflect: Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
If, under the sway of the afflictions, I can be led to take my own dear life, under the circumstances how could I avoid physically harming another person?[548] [228] Clearly a strong affliction like loathing for someone can make you commit suicide by stabbing yourself, jumping off a cliff, and so on. I cherish myself, and you would think that would make me incapable of hurting myself, but under the sway of an affliction, that is exactly what I can be led to do. In this situation, I would not get angry with myself, so when others cannot help but hurt me when they too are swayed by strong afflictions, why should I get angry with them?

d.div: [168] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 6_sh+loka_37_shog_16_na2

f.d: 'o na gnod byed des rang dbang yod pas kho rang gi gnyen sogs la gnod pa mi byed do snyam na/ gnyen la phan 'dogs pa de ga 'dod chags kyi gzhan dbang du song bar 'dug/ sems can rnams la rang dbang dang ldan na thams cad sdug bsngal mi 'dod pas sdug bsngal gyis mnar ba'i sems can med par thag chod snyam du bsgoms pas rgyal po lta bus dbang med du gnod pa byed par btang ba'i mi de la 'char ba'i snang ba lta bu zhig 'ong gsung /

I may object that these harmful people must be able to control themselves because, for example, they do not hurt their friends, but in fact it is out of attachment that they protect their friends. If beings were free, since they all want to avoid suffering, for sure there would be no one left who was tormented by it. By this reflection, it is said that you will come to see malicious people the same way you do someone impelled by a political leader to go and inflict harm on others.

gzhan yang 'gro ba kho rang gi rang bzhin la gnod pa de grub na me tsha zhing sreg pa dang 'dra la/ gal te glo bur du byung ba zhig yin na nyi ma sprin gyis bsgribs par nam mkha' la khro mi rigs pa lta bu/ de bzhin du dngos su nad bskyed pa ni dbyug pa lta bu'i mtshon dang / brgyud nas zhe sdang gis rbad pas gang zag des byas pa ci zhig yod/ gnod pa byed pa'i rtsa ba'i rgyu la khro na/ rang gis sngon chad gzhan la gnod pa 'di lta bu byas pa las byung ba'i tshul spyod 'jug las/
bdag gis sngon chad sems can la/ / 'di 'dra ba yi gnod pa byas/ / de bas sems can 'tshe byed pa/ / bdag la gnod pa 'di 'byung rigs/[169] / zhes so//

Moreover, if it is in a person’s nature to harm and he does so, it is like faulting fire for being hot and burning. If the harm is adventitious, then getting angry with the person is just as unreasonable as getting angry with the sky when its clouds obscure the sun. In fact, it is the weapon like a club that hurts you directly, and indirectly it is the anger that incites its use. So why blame the person? If you want to direct your anger to the root cause of your injury, then recall that the injury is the outcome of similar harm that you inflicted on others in the past. As Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
In the past I have inflicted similar injury on sentient beings; thus, as an abuser of others, it is only right that I am harmed now.[549]

d.div: [169] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u drug pa/ sh+loka_42_shog_16_na5

f.d: der ma zad bdag la gnod byed 'dis ngan smras dang rma phyung ba sogs gnod pa phra mo yang mi bzod pa 'di ltar na/ da lta ngan 'gro'i rgyu mang du bsgrubs pas dmyal bar skyes na sdug bsngal ji ltar bzod snyam du rang la zhe khrel yang yang 'debs/ gzhan yang chu thog tu char babs na gnyis ka rlan gsher yin pa las ma 'das pa ltar/ bdag lus dang mtshon cha gnyis ka sdug bsngal gyi rgyu yin pas zug rngu bskyed pa las 'os ci yod/ rang don sgrub pa'i nyan thos kyang khro bar mi byed na bdag sems can thams cad pha mar shes te gzhan phan sgrub bar sems bskyed nas 'di ltar bya ga la rigs snyam du bsgoms pas lus sems bde 'bol gyi 'gro ba yin gsung /

Moreover, think: If I cannot put up with even minor wrongs like being criticized or physically injured by harmful people, then since I have created so many causes for rebirth in unfortunate realms, how will I be able to stand the suffering once I am born in a hell? In this way, feel disgusted again and again with the faults you see in yourself. Reflect: When water falls in water, both can only be wet. Likewise, both my body and weapons are sources of suffering, so it is only natural that I feel pain. [229] If even śrāvakas, who pursue their own welfare, do not get angry, how could it be right for me to get angry — I who know that all beings are my parents and who have generated bodhicitta to achieve their welfare? It is taught that this meditation brings physical and mental comfort.

da dung gzhan gyis bstod pa byas pa la dga' bar 'dug na smad pa la mi dga' ba shugs kyis 'ong bas/ spyod 'jug las/
bstod dang grags pa'i rim gro ni/ / bsod nams mi 'gyur tsher mi 'gyur/ / bdag stobs mi 'gyur nad med min/ / lus bde bar yang mi 'gyur ro/[170] / zhes bstod pa dang snyan grags kyis phyi mar ma zad 'di'i bde ba yang 'phel bar mi byed pa'i steng du rang nyid don med kyi g.yeng bar 'jug pa dang / gzhan gyis phrag dog byed pa'i nyes pa du ma bskyed la/ snyan grags nyams pa'i rgyur song nas des gnas skabs gzhan rkyen gyi 'tshe ba dang mthar thug g.yeng ba med pas byang chub bsgrubs te bde ba mang po zhig 'phel bar 'dug pa de sangs rgyas kyi byin rlabs yin snyam du dga' ba sgom pa dang / mtshon lta bu phog na sems la ma gnod kyang lus la cung zad gnod mod ngan smras sogs kyis lus sems gang la yang mi gnod pa'i tshul bsam/

If you still relish others’ praise, implicitly you dislike their criticism. Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Praise and the honors of renown will not increase my merit or lengthen my life, they will not boost my strength or ensure my good health, nor will they secure my physical well-being.[550] Not only do praise and fame fail to increase happiness in future lives, they do not even do it in this life. They also lead to many problems: they cause pointless distraction and make others jealous. [On the other hand] by the decline of your reputation, others will not harm you in the short run, and in the long run, by avoiding distraction, you will achieve buddhahood. You should think therefore, “This [loss of reputation] will bring great happiness; it is the buddhas’ blessing,” and feel glad. Reflect that if you are struck by something like a sharp weapon, it may be painful physically, but it does not affect your mind; as for verbal abuse, it hurts you neither physically nor mentally.

d.div: [170] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 6_sh+loka_90_shog_18_na4

f.d:
de ltar bsgoms pas kyang rang la bstod smad byas pa mgo snyoms pa byung na'ang / da dung dgra la phun sum tshogs pa 'dug pa mi bzod pa'i blo thol gyi shar byung na/ spyod 'jug las/
gal te dgra zhig mi dga' na'ang / / de la khyod dgar ci zhig yod/ / khyod kyi yid smon tsam gyis ni/ / de la gnod pa'i rgyur mi 'gyur/ /
khyod kyi 'dod pas sdug bsngal de/ / grub na'ang khyod dgar ci zhig yod/ / gal te 'tshengs par 'gyur zhe na/ / de las phung pa'ang gzhan ci yod/ /
nyon mongs nya pas btab pa yi/ / mchil pa 'di ni mi bzad gze/ / des bzung sems dmyal bum par yang / / dmyal ba'i srung mas bdag 'tshed nges/[171] / zhes sems can kho rang gis rnyed pa'i bde ba la khro ba'i don med la khros kyang gnod par ci la 'gyur/ gal te gnod du zin kyang rang gzhan gnyis ka dmyal bar sreg pa'i las yin pa 'dug snyam du sdom sems drag po bya/

Although with these meditations you may succeed in remaining equanimous in the face of praise and scorn, you might still suddenly feel that you cannot bear the thought of your enemies’ advantages. Concerning this, Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Even if an enemy is unhappy, why should you be pleased? For your simple wishes do not suffice to cause him harm.
Even if your wish for his suffering were fulfilled, why should that please you? If your answer is, “It will gratify me,” what could be more despicable?
Once caught on the dreadful, sharp hook cast by fishermen — the afflictions — infernal guardians are sure to cook you in the cauldrons of hell.[551] Think the following to generate a strong wish to avoid anger: It is pointless for me to be annoyed because a person has found happiness, and how would my getting angry with him harm him? If it did, by the karma we both create, we will end up roasting in hell.

d.div: [171] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 6_sh+loka_87_nas _89_shog_18_na2

f.d: de ltar gnod pa byed pa po rnams la dmigs pa'i khong khro'i gnyen po bsten par nus na'ang / rang sdug bsngal thog tu babs pa 'di mi bzod par 'dug snyam na/ sdug bsngal de la bcos su med na mi dga' ba byas pas dgos nus med cing / bcos su yod na bcos pas chog pas mi dga' ba bya yang mi dgos la/ da lta mi 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal 'bab pa 'di tshe sngon ma mi dge ba byas pa'i 'bras bu yin pas tshe 'dir sdug bsngal gyi tshor ba 'di lta bu zhig ma myong na blang dor mi 'grub par 'khor ba'i 'khor lo 'khor ba kho nar zad/ da res sdug bsngal 'dis rkyen byas nas 'khor ba las yid 'byung ste thar pa mya ngan las 'das pa sgrub pa'i rtsa ba byas pas bka' drin che/ gtar sreg sogs dpyad rtsub mo'i sdug bsngal bsten pas nad kyi gdung ba zhi ba ltar phyi ma mnar med du skye dgos pa'i sdug bsngal gyi tshe ba la tshe 'dir nad kyis thebs pa la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal byung bas go bcad snyam du bsam/

Reflect: Although I may manage in this way to apply the antidotes to the anger that I feel toward those who harm me, I wonder, could I bear it if misfortune suddenly befell me? [230] In fact, if there is nothing to be done about a problem, getting angry is futile and ineffective. If something can be done about it, then it should be done, and there is no point in getting angry. So now when I am faced with unwanted suffering, I will see it as the result of my nonvirtuous deeds of past lives. In this life, if I did not experience painful feelings like these, I would never adopt and reject what I should, and I would just continue turning in the endless round of cyclic existence. Moreover, since suffering helps to generate disgust with samsara, which in turn is the basis for achieving liberation and nirvana, it is a real blessing. Just as undergoing painful and invasive medical treatments like surgery and cauterization eases a painful illness, experiencing sufferings in this life, like those you endure when you are struck with a sickness, can replace having to take rebirth later in the Relentless hell.

bshad ma thag pa de rnams thun dngos gzhi la myong ba thon par byas nas/ thun mtshams la gos phyag dar khrod pa sogs tshangs spyod 'phel ba'i gnas la brten pa'i sdug bsngal dang len/ bstod smad sogs 'jig rten gyi chos la brten pa'i sdug bsngal dang len/ stan la blo mi 'bebs pa'i spyod lam gyi sdug bsngal dang len/ dkon mchog mchod pa sogs chos yongs su 'dzin pa la brten pa'i sdug bsngal dang len/ gzugs mi sdug pa dang gos ngan pa sogs nyams su blang zhing glu gar sogs 'dod yon las ldog pa'i slong mos 'tsho ba la brten pa'i sdug bsngal dang len/ dge ba'i phyogs la mngon par brtson pas dub pa la brten pa'i sdug bsngal dang len/ gzhan gyi srog skyob pa sogs sems can don byed la brten pa'i sdug bsngal dang len/ tshong sogs spangs ba 'phral gyi bya ba la brten pa'i sdug bsngal rnams dngos su dang du len zhing mi nus pa rnams kyang dang du len pa la yid kyi goms pa nan tan du byas pas/ spyod 'jug las/
goms na sla bar mi 'gyur ba'i/ / dngos de gang yang yod ma yin/ / de bas gnod pa chung goms pa/ / gnod pa chen po'ang bzod par bya/[172] / zhes rim gyis goms na mthar gang la'ang ji mi snyam pa'i ba_zod pa'i phar phyin yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ba lags so// //

Having ensured that you gain a spiritual experience of the above during meditation sessions, between sessions accept the suffering involved in cultivating pure conduct, like wearing clothes made from rags from the refuse heap. Accept the suffering brought on by worldly concerns — praise and scorn and so on. Accept the suffering that conduct such as not lying down involves. Accept the suffering involved in thoroughly upholding the teaching, like making offerings to the Three Jewels. Accept the suffering involved in living by mendicancy — having an unattractive physical appearance, inferior clothing, and so on and giving up sense pleasures like singing and dancing. Accept the suffering of fatigue from diligently accomplishing virtue. Accept the suffering involved in helping sentient beings by protecting their lives and so on. Accept the suffering relative to concerns of this life, like giving up business and so on. Be sure to accustom yourself to the idea of accepting those you cannot as yet fully accept. Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
There is nothing at all that does not become easier through habit. Thus, through habituation to minor problems, you will come to bear great ones as well.[552] By progressive habituation, you will in the end be able to put up with anything and complete the perfection of forbearance.

d.div: [172] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 6_sh+loka_14_shog_15_na3

f.d:
smras pa/
skye bar bsags pa'i dge tshogs nags kyi klung / / khong khro'i me phung gcig gis rab bsregs nas/ / mi dge'i sdong dum srid pa'i rtser spungs pa'i/ / mi bzod dgra 'di sdug bsngal kun gyi gzhi/ /
dbang med las nyon ri gzar rtse mo nas/ / dkar min 'bras bu thur du rgyug ba'i rbab/ / 'khor ba'i gcong rong khrod du gnas pa rnams/ / bcom pa'i gshis lugs 'di la su zhig gshung / /
kun 'byung dpung tshogs bshams pa'i g.yul ngo na/ / bzod pa'i go cha btsan po legs bgos tshe/ / rdeg rdung tshig rtsub mtshon gyis 'bigs min pa'i/ / myang 'das gnas su bgrod par byed 'di mtshar/ / zhes bya ba ni bar skabs kyi tshigs su bcad pa'o// //

Stanzas between sections [231]
The forest of virtue produced over many lives is reduced to ashes by a single blaze of anger. The pile of charred tree trunks of nonvirtue it leaves reaches as high as the peak of existence. This enemy, anger, is the source of all suffering!
Irresistibly impelled by karma and afflictions, from the peak of a steep mountain, the results of nonvirtue plummet us downward. How can you dispute the fact that those residing in samsara’s abyss are overcome [by suffering]?[553]
When facing the aligned troops of suffering’s origins in battle, if you don the sturdy armor of forbearance, you will not be pierced when struck by the sharp weapons of harsh words. In this way you will travel to nirvana; its benefits are marvelous indeed!

d.div: [553] That is to say, this is the indisputable nature of samsaric existence.

f.d: bzhi pa brtson 'grus kyi phar phyin ni
2.2.3.2.1.4. The perfection of diligence

spyod 'jug las/ brtson gang dge la spro ba'o/[173] /zhes dge ba bsdu ba dang sems can gyi don bya ba'i phyir du sems mngon par spro ba phyin ci ma log pa gong nas gong du yongs su rdzogs pa mthar phyin pa de brtson 'grus kyi pha rol tu phyin pa yin la/

Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states, “What is diligence? It is delight in virtue.”[554] The perfection of diligence is the development of authentic delight in collecting virtue and working to benefit sentient beings until it is utterly complete.

d.div: [173] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 7_sh+loka_2_shog_20_na4

f.d:
de yang mdo sde rgyan las/
dge ba'i tshogs kyi nang na brtson 'grus mchog / 'di ltar de la brten nas de rjes 'thob/ / brtson 'grus kyis ni mod la bde gnas mchog / dngos grub 'jig rten 'das dang 'jig rten gtogs/ /
brtson 'grus kyis ni srid spyod 'dod pa 'thob/ / brtson 'grus kyis ni dag pa rab 'gyur ldan/ / brtson 'grus kyis ni 'jig tshogs 'das nas 'gro / brtson 'grus kyis ni byang chub mchog 'tshang rgya/[174] / zhes 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i phan bde thams cad kyi 'byung gnas ni brtson 'grus yin pas de nyams su len par byed pa la/ thog mar go cha'i brtson 'grus la/ bskal pa chen po stong phrag re la zhag gcig /de sum cu la zla ba/ de bcu gnyis la lor byas pa'i bskal pa chen po grangs med pa gsum bye ba phrag 'bum 'gyur gyi bar du sems can gcig gi sdug bsngal bsal ba'i ched du dmyal ba kho nar gnas pa la brten nas sangs rgyas sgrub dgos pa byung yang brtson 'grus mi gtong na de las thung ba lta ci smos snyam pa go cha'i brtson 'grus dang / 'khor ba thog ma med pa nas da lta yan chad la zhag gcig tu byas pa'i rim pa bzhin zla ba dang lor brtsis nas lo 'bum song ba na byang chub kyi sems gcig skye zhing sangs rgyas gcig mthong ba lta bu gang+gA'i klung gi bye ma snyed kyi grangs dang mnyam pa na sems can gcig gi sems dang spyod pa shes shing / de 'dra ba'i yul sems can re re bzhin nas byed dgos pa byung yang de dag la yun ring bar mi sems par spro bar byed pa ni gong na med pa'i brtson 'grus su bshad pas rang re rnams kyis sngar sbyin pa'i skabs kyang thog mar zan kham gcig las brtsams nas bsam sbyor gnyis kas sbyin pa la goms par byas pas mthar lus dang mgo bo gtong ba la yang zhum pa med par byung tshul bzhin 'dir yang thog mar bdag gis snga dro 'di'i yun gyi bar dge ba'i bya ba 'di tsam zhig byed snyam du bsam pa dang /

The Ornament of Mahayana Sutras states:
Among [the ways to] collect virtue, diligence is supreme. Based on it, all good qualities are attained. With diligence, you achieve excellent happiness in this life, and both mundane and supermundane attainments.
With diligence, you gain the enjoyments of this world that you desire. With diligence, you are endowed with excellent moral purity. With diligence, you transcend [the view of] the personal identity. With diligence, you achieve the supreme enlightenment of buddhahood.[555] Diligence is the source of all mundane and supermundane happiness and goodness. To practice it, to start there is armor-like diligence. Counting a thousand great eons as one day, thirty of these as a month, and twelve of those as a year, armor-like diligence is the thought “I will not give up diligence even when I realize that attaining buddhahood requires remaining in the hells alone for up to a trillion great eons made up of such years for the purpose of ending a single being’s suffering. [232] It goes without saying then that I will not do it for shorter periods.” Such is armor-like diligence. Counting the time from beginningless samsara until now as one day, and calculating months and years accordingly, even if it took a hundred thousand of such years to generate the awakening mind once and see a single buddha, and as many of such years as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River to know the mind and behavior of a single being, and you had to do the same for each being, the fact of not feeling that it was too long and delighting in it is said to be sublime [armor-like] diligence. You should think: As before in the context of generosity, just as getting used to being generous in thought and in deed, starting by giving single morsels of food, eventually enables us to give our head and body without hesitation, in the present context as well, I will start by practicing virtue for just one morning.

d.div: [174] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_rje btsun byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 17_sh+loka_66_shog_24_ba1
[555] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, 17.66–67, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 24b1.

f.d: bsams pa bzhin du sbyin sogs kyi dge ba gang yin pa de la brtson 'grus chen pos 'bad cing / rim gyis zhag grangs zla ba lo ji srid 'tsho'i bar lta bu'i dam bca' dang bcas te brtson 'grus brtsams kyang de la yun ring ba dang dka' ba'i snang ba mi 'char ba dang spro ba cher 'phel bas sngar bshad pa'i go cha'i brtson 'grus de dag kyang sgrub nus pa zhig 'ong ba yin la/ thun dngos gzhi'i skabs dkon mchog rjes su dran pas dug gsum gyi gnyen po bsten pa sogs ji ltar rigs pa'i dpyad 'jog gi dmigs pa thun de ma rdzogs kyi bar du gzhan gyis bar ma bcad par byed snyam pa'i 'phen pa btang zhing / snyom las dang dman pa'i bde ba la sred pa bkag nas brtson 'grus chen pos byas pas thun snga ma rnams la dka' se 'ong yang / rim gyis bsgom pa na dka' ba med cing spro ba cher 'phel ba yin gsung /

Following this intention, with great diligence you then earnestly cultivate virtues like generosity. You commit yourself to exercising diligence progressively over days, months, years, and in the end for your entire life. As a result, although you make every effort, you will not find the time long nor find it difficult. Your delight will grow, and you will succeed in achieving the aforementioned armor-like diligence. You are to initiate meditative sessions by recalling the Three Jewels, deciding to apply the antidotes to the three mental poisons, and being determined not to let anything interfere with your meditation — analytical or placement, whichever is appropriate — until the end of the session. For the first sessions, it might be somewhat difficult to curb your sloth and craving for inferior pleasures and exercise great diligence, but it is said that as you continue meditating, it will gradually become easier, and your delight will increase tremendously.

de yang da dung long yod snyam pa'i phyi bshol gyi le lo zhig blo la thol gyi shar byung ba na/ spyod 'jug las/
snyom las bde ba'i ro myang dang / / gnyid la brten pa'i sred pa yis/ / 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal mi skyo las/ / le lo nye bar skye bar 'gyur/[175] / zhes dge ba la zhag 'phul nyin 'phul gyi phyi bshol byed pa'i le lo'i rgyu gnyid rmugs sogs dman pa'i ro la chags pa las 'byung bar bshad pas/ lus kyi spyod lam rlung 'ong sa dang gos srab tu gtong ba khams gseng ba yang byed cing dmigs pa ni rgan gzhon med par shi ba mig gis mthong ba bzhin bdag kyang myur du 'chi/ shi ba'i 'og tu rten bzang 'di 'dra rnyed pa dka' snyam du bsam pas skom 'thung ba'i long yang med pa lta bu'i shes pa tsab ling nge ba zhig ma skyes bar bsgom/ da dung gnyen po mthar ma phyin pas bre mo'i gtam sogs dman pa'i bde ba la sred pa'i snang ba byung ba na/ spyod 'jug las/
dga' ba'i rgyu ni mtha' yas pa'i/ / dam chos dga' ba'i mchog spangs nas/ / sdug bsngal rgyu yi g.yeng ba dang / / rgod sogs la khyod ci phyir dga'/[176] / zhes gnas skabs kyi bde ba phra mo 'di dag la rnam par g.yengs bas dam pa'i chos kyi sgo 'gags te bdag ngan song du skye ba 'dug snyam du bsam/

If laziness in the form of procrastination suddenly occurs, and you find yourself thinking that you still have plenty of time, recall what Guide to the Bodhisattva Way says:
It is owing to craving idleness, experiences of pleasure, and sleep and to lacking revulsion toward samsaric suffering that laziness prevails.[556] It is taught that attachment to inferior pleasures like sleep, lethargy, and so on results in laziness in the form of procrastination — the postponement of virtue. [233] In this case the physical conduct to adopt is to sit in a well-ventilated place, wear thinner clothing, or get up and move around. Reflect, “As I can see with my own eyes, the time of death has nothing to do with how old or young you are, and I too will die soon. After death, it will be hard for me to find another good rebirth like this one,” and meditate until you feel so restless that you have no time even to quench your thirst. If these remedies are insufficient, and you still feel drawn to lesser pleasures like stories about bears, recall what Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Among the many causes of delight, why do you reject the boundless [practice of the] excellent Dharma, the supreme joy, and instead delight in the sources of misery: distractions, amusements, and the rest?[557] Think: By letting myself be distracted by these small short-lived pleasures, I am closing the door to the perfect teaching and will be reborn in an unfavorable realm.

d.div: [175] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 7_sh+loka_3_shog_20_na5
[176] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 7_sh+loka_15_shog_20_ba4
[556] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 7.3, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 20a5.

f.d:
de bzhin bsgoms pas bdag gis thob bya sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das 'di ni skyon kun zad yon tan kun ldan yin pas 'thob par dka' snyam pa'i blo zhum pa zhig 'byung bas de'i tshe 'di snyam du/ spyod 'jug las/
bdag gis byang chub ga la zhes/ / sgyid lug par ni mi bya ste/ / 'di ltar de bzhin gshegs pa ni/ / bden pa gsung pas bden 'di gsungs/ /
sbrang bu sha sbrang bung ba dang / / de bzhin srin bur gang gyur pa/ / des kyang brtson pa'i stobs bskyed na/ / byang chub 'thob dka' bla med 'thob/ /
bdag lta rigs kyi mir skyes la/ / phan dang gnod pa ngo shes pas/ / byang chub spyod pa ma btang na/ / bdag gis byang chub cis mi 'thob/[177] / ces yon tan khyad par can dang ldan pa'i bcom ldan 'das des sems can thams cad sangs rgyas 'thob par gsungs na bdag ci'i phyir sangs rgyas thob par mi 'gyur snyam gzengs bstod pa'i tshul gyis bsgom/ sangs rgyas thob par 'gyur snyam pa'i gzengs bstod kyang rkang lag la sogs pa'i lus gtong ba zhig mi nus so snyam na/ spyod 'jug las/
gso dpyad phal pa 'di 'dra ba/ / sman pa mchog gis ma mdzad de/ / cho ga shin tu 'jam po yis/ / nad chen dpag med gso bar mdzad/ /
tshod ma la sogs sbyin pa la'ang / / 'dren pas thog mar sbyor bar mdzad/ / de la goms nas phyi nas ni/ / rim gyis rang gi sha yang gtong / /
gang tshe rang gi lus la ni/ / tshod sogs lta bu'i blo skyes pa/ / de tshe sha la sogs gtong ba/ / de la dka' ba ci zhig yod/[178] / ces mgo dang mig la sogs pa gtong ba la tshod ma'i tsha ba 'dren pa tsam gyi blo skye ba'i tshe gtong ba yin pas dka' ba mi 'dug snyam pa'i spro ba chen po bsam/

When meditating in this way, if you feel discouraged and think, “Given that the goal I am pursuing — the condition of a blessed buddha — is endowed with all good qualities and free of all faults, it will be hard to achieve,” reflect on the following: Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Do not be discouraged, thinking, “How can I attain enlightenment?” For the Tathāgata, who is a truth-speaker, announced this truth:
“Even bees, flies, gnats, and worms, by generating powerful diligence, all achieve supreme enlightenment so difficult to attain.”
Why then should someone like me, who has been born a human and knows what is harmful and beneficial, not attain buddhahood, provided I do not abandon the bodhisattva deeds?[558] The Blessed One, who has such superior qualities, said that all types of sentient beings attain buddhahood, so why should not I? Contemplate this to raise your spirits. Although you pluck up your courage and think, “I shall attain buddhahood,” you might question your ability to give away your body, limbs, and so on, but Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Such ordinary medical therapies the Supreme Physician does not prescribe. With extremely gentle treatments he cures countless grave illnesses.
The Teacher first encourages giving vegetables and the like. Later, once schooled in these, slowly you can also give your own flesh.
When you have come to see your body as you see vegetables and the like, what difficulty will there be in giving away your flesh and the rest?[559] [234] With great delight, reflect that you will give your eyes, head, and so on once it has become as easy as giving dishes of vegetables, in which case it will involve no difficulty.

d.div: [177] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 7_sh+loka_70_nas _75_shog_21_ba6
[178] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 7_sh+loka_24_nas _26 shog_21_na3

f.d:
de ltar rgyal sras kyi spyod pa la slob pa'i tshe 'khor bar skye ba len pa mi bzod do snyam na/ spyod 'jug las/
sdig pa spangs phyir sdug bsngal med/ / mkhas pa'i phyir na mi dga' med/ / 'di ltar log par rtog pa dang / / sdig pas sems dang lus la gnod/ /
bsod nams kyis ni lus bde la/ / mkhas pa yis ni sems bde na/ / gzhan don 'khor bar gnas kyang ni/ / snying rje can dag ci ste skyo/[179] / zhes byang sems kyis sdig pa spangs pas rgyu med pa'i phyir na 'bras bu sdug bsngal mi 'byung ngo snyam du bsgom/

When training in bodhisattva practice in this manner, if you begin to feel that you can no longer bear being born in samsara, think about what Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Since they have rejected sin, [bodhisattvas] do not suffer. As they are wise, their minds are not troubled. Thus it is wrong thinking and sin that harm the mind and body.
As merit brings physical well-being and wisdom brings mental well-being, why should remaining in samsara for others’ sake dishearten the compassionate ones?[560] Contemplate this, and reflect that since bodhisattvas have given up sin, for lack of a cause, they do not experience suffering, its result.

d.div: [179] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 7_sh+loka_27_dang _28_shog_21_na4

f.d:
dge ba chos sdud ni dkon mchog mchod pa sogs la brtson pa dang / sems can don byed ni gzhan gyi nor rkun pos mi 'khyer ba'i thabs ston pa la brtson pa sogs tshul khrims kyi skabs ltar la mi 'dra ba'i khyad par skabs thob phye ste dmigs pa bskyang ngo / / bshad ma thag pa'i yon tan de dag kyang sna re tsam skyes pa la chog mi shes par rgyal sras kyi spyod pa la bslab pa dang ma bslabs pa'i phan yon dang nyes dmigs dran pa'i sgo nas mos pa'i stobs brtson 'grus rtsom pa la phyir mi ldog pa brtan pa'i stobs/ spro ba chen po dang bcas te 'phro mi gcod pa dga' ba'i stobs/ dub na ngal gso ba'i gnad shes pa dor ba'i stobs rnams kyi sgo nas/ spyod 'jug las/
'thab rnying dgra dang lhan cig tu/ / g.yul ngor ral kha lhags pa bzhin/ / nyon mongs mtshon las gzur bya zhing / / nyon mongs dgra rnams 'jebs par btab/[180] / ces dgra 'thab la mkhas pas phar dgra la mtshon bsnun pa dang tshur brdeg pa la zon byed pa ltar/ 'dir yang nyon mongs pa mngon gyur 'joms pa dang / bag la nyal gyi nyon mongs pas tshur sems la rma phyung ba la zon byed pa gnyis ka'i tshul gyis brtson 'grus bskyed cing nyams su len 'tshal lo// //

To collect virtue, strive to make offerings to the Three Jewels and so on. To help sentient beings, endeavor to show others how to avoid having their belongings stolen and so forth, as in the context of the ethical discipline [of helping others]. You are to meditate on this once you have identified the particulars of the present topic. Do not content yourself with achieving only a few of the good qualities just explained; cultivate the power of aspiration by recalling the benefits of training in bodhisattva practice and the drawbacks of not doing so. Develop the power of constancy for not abandoning your practice of diligence, the power of joy in continuity along with great delight, and the power of abandonment — conscious of the instruction to rest when tired.[561] As Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Like seasoned warriors, who battle their enemies with swords, you must avert the weapons that are the afflictions and pulverize your enemies, the afflictions.[562] Just as skillful people, when fighting an enemy, will strike their foes with weapons and avert their blows, here, in both defeating manifest afflictions and protecting the mind from latent ones, I urge you to cultivate and exercise diligence.

d.div: [180] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 7_sh+loka_67_shog_23_na1
[561] These four powers that enhance diligence are explained in the Bodhicaryāvatāra, 7.31–67, and expanded further in Tsongkhapa’s Great Treatise (trans.), 2:195–201.
[562] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 7.67, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 23a1.

f.d:
smras pa/
gti mug gnyid dang rmugs sogs bde ba'i ro/ / don med rnam par g.yeng ba'i rgod bag la/ / ji tsam spyad kyang ngoms pa med pa 'di/ / skom pas ba tshwa'i chu las 'thung ba bzhin/ /
zhe sdang dbang gis stobs ldan dgra bo la/ / mi nus bzhin du gzengs bstod mtho btsams na/ / nges par sgrub nus sangs rgyas go 'phang la/ / zhum par byed pa'i blo ngan 'di ko nor/ /
long med tshe 'di'i snang tshul shes bzhin du/ / gtan gyi bde ba sgrub pa'i dam chos la/ / zhag 'phul nyin 'phul med par brtson pa'i lcag / brabs na thar pa'i gling der bgrod par nges/ / zhes bya ba ni bar skabs kyi tshigs su bcad pa'o// //

Stanzas between sections [235]
The more you indulge in the pleasures of ignorant sleep, lethargy, and the rest, and in the excitation and carelessness of pointless distraction, the more you feel dissatisfied, like the thirsty person who drinks salt water.
If, driven by anger, you can summon the courage to attack a powerful enemy you are incapable of overcoming, then discouragement regarding buddhahood that is attainable is a poor misguided attitude.
Knowing that there is no time in this life, do not postpone the perfect Dharma that creates stable happiness. Goad yourself with the cane of diligence, and you are sure to travel to the isle of liberation.
lnga pa bsam gtan gyi phar phyin ni
2.2.3.2.1.5. The perfection of meditative absorption

spyod 'jug las/
de ltar brtson 'grus bskyed nas ni/ / yid ni ting nge 'dzin la bzhag[181] / ces sems dmigs pa las gzhan du mi g.yeng bar gnas pas sems rtse gcig pa la sgom pa mthar phyin pa na bsam gtan gyi pha rol tu phyin par 'gyur la/

Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
Having generated diligence in this way, place your mind in meditative concentration.[563] The perfection of meditative absorption is a fully accomplished meditation in which the mind is one-pointed, as it abides free of distraction toward other objects.

d.div: [181] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 8_sh+loka_1_shog_23_na7

f.d:
de yang lam rim che chung sogs gong ma rnams kyi gsung rab tu bsam gtan dang shes rab kyi skor la mdor bstan rgyas bshad kyi tshul du zhi lhag gnyis logs su mdzad na'ang / dngos don gcig gi nyams len snying por bsgril ba'i tshe zhi gnas kyi dmigs pa sa bcad lnga pa dang / lhag mthong gi dmigs pa sa bcad drug par mdzad nas mjug tu bsdu ba'i dngos po bzhis don bsdu ba lags pas de ltar na bsam gtan nam ting nge 'dzin gyi nyams len zhi gnas bsgom pa la/ dgongs 'grel las/
skye ba po yis lhag mthong dang / / zhi gnas bsgom par byas na ni/ / gnas ngan len gyi 'ching ba dang / / mtshan ma'i 'ching las rnam grol 'gyur/[182] / zhes gnas ngan len gyi 'ching ba myong ba sa bon dang bcas pa rtsa ba nas drungs phyung ba shes rab dang / mtshan ma'i 'ching ba myong ba mngon gyur mgo gnon pa bsam gtan yin pas de gnyis la zhi lhag gi ming du btags te theg pa gsum gyi ting nge 'dzin ming gi 'dogs phyogs rnam grangs mang ba mtha' dag don zhi lhag gnyis su ma 'dus pa med cing / zhi gnas ni dmigs pa gcig la dran shes rgyun chags su gtad pas sems dmigs pa la ngang gis gnas te lus sems shin sbyangs kyi dga' bde skyes pa na ting nge 'dzin khyad par can du 'gyur ba'i phyir na shes rab kyis mtshan 'dzin gyi 'ching ba gcod par byed pa la yang zla ba sgron me'i mdo las/
zhi gnas stobs kyis g.yo ba med par 'gyur/ / lhag mthong gis ni ri dang 'dra bar 'gyur/[183] / zhes dper na chu'i bya ba byed pa la chu de sdod pa'i snod gcig dgos pa bzhin du dmigs pa la 'jug par 'jug mkhan gyi sems mi g.yo ba dgos pas gnas lugs kyi don ri mo sna tshogs kyi bkod pa ma 'dres par so sor mthong bar byed pa la ma rig pa'i mun pas bsgribs na shes rab kyi mar me sbar te blta dgos par rnam g.yeng gi rlung gis bskyod de mi gsal bas na de nyid sgo dgag pa'i ting 'dzin ni med du mi rung ba ste/ zhi gnas la brten nas gzhan du mi g.yel ba ma byung na gnas lugs kyi don du ma zad las 'bras byams snying rje bzlas brjod sogs dge ba gzhan rnams kyang 'bras bu chung ba'i phyir/ spyod 'jug las/
sems ni rnam par g.yengs pa'i mi/ / nyon mongs mche ba'i phrag na gnas/[184] / zhes dang /
bzlas brjod dang ni dka' thub kun/ / yun ring dus su spyad byas kyang / / sems gzhan g.yeng bas byas pa ni/ / de nyid rig pas don med gsungs/[185] / zhes pa ltar ro//

Concerning absorption and wisdom, past masters, in works such as the Great and Middle-Length treatises, have composed separate sections on tranquil abiding and insight, some of which are brief expositions and others detailed. I will explain the meditation on tranquil abiding in relation to the fifth [perfection] and the meditation on insight in relation to the sixth by summarizing their essential content for the purpose of practice, and I will conclude with a brief explanation of the four means of gathering others. On the meditation on tranquil abiding (śamatha) — the practice of meditative absorption (dhyāna) or states of concentration (samādhi) — the Unraveling the Intent Sutra states:
When practitioners cultivate special insight and tranquil abiding, they free themselves of bondage to dysfunctional tendencies and bondage to signs.[564] Wisdom eradicates the experience of bondage to dysfunctional tendencies along with their seeds, and meditative absorption inhibits the experience of manifest bondage to signs.[565] They are called [respectively] special insight and tranquil abiding. Among the three vehicles, states of concentration go by many different names, but all without exception are included in tranquil abiding and insight. [236] Tranquil abiding is a superior state of concentration in which the mind naturally focuses on its object. It is attained once the bliss of mental and physical pliancy has arisen through the continual observation of a single object with mindfulness and meta-awareness. Wisdom cuts the bonds of grasping at signs.[566] The Moon Lamp Sutra explains:
By the power of tranquil abiding, the mind becomes immoveable. By special insight, it comes to resemble a mountain.[567] Just as water requires a container to fulfill its function, for a state of mind to penetrate its object, the awareness penetrating it must be immoveable. When it is obscured by the darkness of ignorance, you are to light the lamp of wisdom to observe each aspect of the complex pattern of existence without confusing any of its parts. If the draft of distraction makes its light flicker, it will shine less brightly, which is why a state of concentration that halts [the mind’s] movement is absolutely necessary. If you fail to overcome distraction by relying on tranquil abiding, not only will [your understanding] of the mode of existence be ineffectual, so will all other virtuous practices in relation to karma and its effects, love, compassion, mantra recitation, and so on. Guide to the Bodhisattva Way states:
A person whose mind is distracted remains in the jaws of the afflictions.[568] And:
All mantra recitations and austerities, even practiced over long periods, the Knower of Suchness said are pointless, when done with a mind turned elsewhere.[569]

d.div: [182] sde dge_106_bka'/ mdo sde/ ca_'phags pa dgongs pa nges par 'grel ba/ le'u/ 3_shog_9_ba2
