a. Going for refuge and generating the awakening mind

mdun gyi pad sdong 'dab bzhi'i bla ma dang / sangs rgyas chos dang dge 'dun srung ma la/ / mi rtag sdug bsngal dran pas skyabs su mchi/ / bdag dang 'gro rgyud byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ / zhes skyabs 'gro dang /
drin can ma rnams srid zhi'i rgya mtsho las/ bsgral phyir byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed nas/ / mdo sngags chos kyi snying po don gsum du/ / bsdus pa'i gdams pa nyams su blang bar bgyi/ / zhes sems bskyed lan gsum re bya/

1 To my gurus, who are on a lotus tree in front of me, and to the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and protectors, with thoughts of impermanence and suffering, I go for refuge. Pray bless my mindstream and those of all beings. In this way go for refuge; then generate the awakening mind:
2 To free my kind mothers from samsara’s ocean, I shall generate the awakening mind and put into practice the instruction that distills the essence of the sutra and tantra teachings into three points. Recite the verses on refuge and awakening mind three times.
[tshogs zhing ]
b. Visualization of the merit field and seven-limb worship

spyi bor shel dkar byang chub mchod rten gyi/ / bum nang pad zlar bla ma spyan ras gzigs/ / kha sarapANi bang rim bzhi yi sgor/ / sangs rgyas stong ni rigs lnga'i rnam par bzhugs/ /
rang snying pad dmar 'dab stong lte ba ru/ / kha sarapA Ni 'dab mar a dkar stong / / bla ma lha yi gsang gsum 'od zer gyis/ / ye shes spyan drangs skyabs kun ngo bor gyur/ /
bla ma lha la phyag 'tshal mchod tshogs 'bul/ / sdig ltung kun bshags dge la rjes yi rang / / chos 'khor bskor phyir rgyun du bzhugs su gsol/ / 'dis mtshon dge ba byang chub chen por bsngo/ / spro na maN+Dal yang 'bul/

3 At my crown inside the vase[1269] of a white crystal stupa, on a lotus and a moon disc, sits Guru Avalokiteśvara; he is Khasarpāṇi surrounded by a retinue on four levels. The thousand buddhas are present as lords of the five families.
4 My heart is a thousand-petaled red lotus; at its hub is Khasarpāṇi and on the petals a thousand white ah syllables. Light rays emitting from the guru deity’s three secrets invite the gnosis beings, making him the embodiment of all refuge.
5 To you, guru deity, I prostrate and make offerings of all kinds, I confess all my negative karma and rejoice in virtue, I appeal to turn the wheel of Dharma and to constantly remain, and I dedicate all my virtues, exemplified by acts such as these. If you wish, you could make a mandala offering as well.

d.div: [1269] This refers to the bulbous vase-like dome of a Tibetan stupa, which sits above a platform composed of a square block with four ascending steps.

f.d: [tshe 'di'i nyams len ]
c. Practices pertaining to this life

bla ma sangs rgyas tshad med thugs rje can/ / bdag dang mkha' mnyam 'gro ba ma lus pa'i/ / sgrib gnyis byang zhing tshogs gnyis rab rdzogs te/ / myur du sangs rgyas thob par mdzad du gsol/ / lan gsum/

d.div: 6 O gurus and buddhas, possessors of limitless compassion, pray help me and beings equal to the reaches of space purify the two obscurations and perfect the two accumulations, so that we may soon attain buddhahood. (3x)
de ltar gsol bas bla ma sangs rgyas las/ / bdud rtsi dkar po'i rgyun babs spyi bor zhugs/ / snying ga'i yi dam a dang bcas la thim/ / de las byung ba'i bdud rtsis sgrib gnyis sbyangs/ /
dag pa gnyis ldan thugs rje chen por gyur/ / spyi bo'i bla ma snying ga'i yi dam dang / / sangs rgyas stong yang a yig stong la thim/ / mchod rten mkha' la 'ja' ltar yal bar gyur/ /
yi dam thugs kar zla lter hrIHyig mtha'i/ / yi ge drug pa'i 'od zer spro bsdu yis/ / snod bcud skyon sbyangs rgyal ba'i thugs rje bskul/ / kun 'dus 'khyer so gsum dang ldan par gyur/ /

7 Having been appealed thusly, the gurus and the buddhas emit streams of white nectar, which enter my crown and absorb into the deity and the ah syllable at my heart; nectars flowing from this purify the two obscurations. [574]

8 With these two purities, I become the Great Compassionate One,[1270] the guru at my crown dissolves into the deity, the thousand buddhas dissolve into the thousand ah syllables, and like the vanishing of a rainbow, the stupa dissolves into space.

9 At the heart of the deity, on a moon disc and around letter hrīḥ, are the six syllables, from which light radiates and retracts; this purifies the world and its denizens and invokes the conquerors’ compassion. May I be blessed with the three embodiments and the three perspectives.[1271]
[1270] Great Compassionate One (thugs rje chen po, mahākaruṇika) should be understood as an epithet of Avalokiteśvara, specifically in his manifestation as a thousand-arm deity.

[1271] As explained in the author’s own commentary below (p. 731), the three embodiments (kun ’dus gsum) are (1) Khasarpāṇi, who embodies all meditation deities, (2) the guru in the form of Amitābha, who embodies all gurus, and (3) the six-syllable mantra, which embodies all mantras. The three perspectives (’khyer so gsum) are (1) viewing whatever you see as the body of Avalokiteśvara, (2) viewing whatever you hear as the sound of the six-syllable mantra, and (3) viewing whatever thoughts arise, good or bad, as the exalted mind of Guru Great Compassion (Avalokiteśvara), endowed with the essence of emptiness and compassion.

f.d: oM ma Ni pad+me hUM/ zhes bzla/
Om maṇi padme hūṃ (Repeat this mantra).

thugs ka'i 'od kyis snod bcud rang gi lus/ / pad+ma a yig lha sngags sa bon bsdus/ / rang sems la sogs chos kun bden grub kyi/ / skye med rigs pas btsal nas mnyam par gzhag / tshe 'di'i nyams len no//

10 The lights from his heart draw forth the world, its inhabitants, my body, the lotus, the ah syllable, the mantra, and the seed syllable. Through reasoning that seeks the nature of my mind and all phenomena, their lack of arising as truly existent, I rest in meditative equipoise. These, then, are the practices pertaining to this life.
['chi kha'i nyams len ]
d. Practices pertaining to the time of death

rang sems yi dam phyir thon bem rig phral/ / rlung me sgyed bu la gnas ka pA lar/ / phung po rnying pa sbyangs rtogs sbar bya te/ / bdud rtsis srid zhi'i mgron la mchod sbyin bya/ /
mi rtag sgyu ma stong nyid dran byas la/ / lus dang longs spyod gnyen gyi 'brel thag gcad/ / rang gi lus dbus dbu ma'i snying nang du/ / rang sems kha sar pA Ni mtshon gang tsam/ /
steng phyogs dga' ldan yid dga' chos 'dzin du/ / byams mgon gser mdog bzang po'i bzhugs stangs can/ / 'dren par gsol ba btab pas thugs ka nas/ / 'od ser sbubs byung rang gi spyi bor zug /
'du shes gsum ldan lcags kyus ral pa la/ / btab drangs rje btsun thugs dang dbyer med 'dres/ sbyong dus phab nas nyod kyis tshangs bug 'gegs/ / 'chi dus mdun gyi pad+mor skye ba len/ / 'chi kha'i nyams len no//

11 My mind as the deity comes out, separating my body and mind; and inside a skull cup set on a tripod atop fire and wind mandalas, my old body is purified, transformed, and multiplied, and its nectar is offered to the guests of both samsara and nirvana.
12 Recalling impermanence, illusion, and emptiness, I sever the ties with my body, wealth, and loved ones, and inside my body, at the heart inside the central channel, appears a Khasarpāṇi the size of a thumbnail.
13 Maitreya, gold in color and seated in the bhadra posture, resides above in Tuṣita, in Yiga Chözin [courtyard].[1272] As I appeal to this savior, from his heart emerges a hollow light beam that pierces my crown.
14 With the three thoughts,[1273] I am pulled from my topknot by a hook and become fused inseparably with Maitreya’s mind; during training I return, and my crown aperture is sealed. After death, may I be reborn like a new lotus flower in his presence. This then is the practice pertaining to the time of death.

d.div: [1272] On Yiga Chözin, see above page 391.
[1273] On the three thoughts, see below page 737.

f.d: [bar do'i nyams len]
e. Practices pertaining to the intermediate state

'chi kha'i yul snang bar dor mos pa sogs/ / rlung 'dun smon pas bar do ngos zin nas/ / snod snang dag zhing bcud snang yi dam lha/ / kun kyang bden med sgyu ma lta bur blta/ /
stong nyid snying rjes chags sdang nyer bkag ste/ / dag snang dang bcas bsam bzhin skye ba len/ / lta sgom spyod pa'i gnad dang ldan pa yi/ / grub chen mi tra'i gdams pa 'khrul med yin/ / bar do'i nyams len no//

15 Imagining the perceptions at dying as those of the intermediate state, through wind, intention, and aspiration, I will recognize the bardo [as bardo], and I will view the world as a pure land, beings as deities, and all as devoid of true existence and illusion-like.
16 Preventing attachment and aversion with emptiness and compassion, I will with pure perception take birth through my own will. Endowed with the key points of view, meditation, and action, this is the flawless instruction of the great siddha Mitrayogi. This then is the practice pertaining to the intermediate state.
[bsngo smon ]
f. Concluding prayer and dedication

d.div: 'dis mtshon dge bas tshe rabs thams cad du/ / bla ma phyag na pad+mos rjes bzung ste/ / 'di phyi bar do'i nyams len mthar phyin nas/ / bstan 'gro kun gyi dpal du bdag gyur cig /

17 Through the virtue of deeds such as these, may I be cared for in all lives by Guru Padmapāṇi, [575] and by perfecting the practices of this life, death, and the bardo, may I become a glory to the teaching and all beings.

f.d:
smras pa/
tshul 'di rnam dpyod spyan yangs slob ma'i ngor/ / ban gzugs d+harmab+ha dras yi ger bris/ / dge bas mdo rgyud snying po'i gdams pa 'di/ / mi nyams phyogs brgyar yun du rgyus gyur ci/ /

Thus I say:
18 This was written for disciples with the open eyes of intellect by Dharmabhadra, who takes the form of a monk. Through this virtue, may this instruction, the essence of sutras and tantras, never degenerate but flourish always in a hundred directions.
sarba dzag gtaM// //
Sarva jagagataṃ.
@#/ /snying po don gsum gyi zin bris grub chen zhal lung gsal ba'i me long zhes bya ba bzhugs so/ /

d.b: 15. A Mirror Reflecting the Mahāsiddha’s Sacred Words:

b.i: Notes on the Three Essential Points

f.d: dngul chu d+ha rma b+ha dra/
Ngulchu Dharmabhadra

d.div: @#/ /brgyad khri bzhi stong ma 'dres snying po'i bcud/ / don tshan gsum du bsdus pa'i bsam 'phel dbang / / bshad dang sgrub pa'i rgyal mtshan rtser bkod nas/ / 'doms mdzad drin can bla mar gus phyag 'tshal/ /

Respectfully I bow to the kind gurus, who teach and place atop the banner of exposition and practice this wish-granting gem condensing into three points the unadulterated vital essence of all the eighty-four thousand teachings.

f.d: de la 'dir grub pa'i dbang phyug chen po mi tra dz+wa ki la lhag pa'i lha 'phags mchog thugs rje chen pos dngos su gnang ba'i snying po don gsum du grags ba'i gdams pa 'di nyid 'chad pa la rtsa tshig las/

Here, to expound the instruction famed as the “Three Essential Points,” which was directly granted to the great siddha Mitrayogi by his meditation deity, the supreme ārya Great Compassion, these are the root verses:[1274]

d.div: [1274] This commentary is based on two sets of verses — Mitrayogi’s root lines below and Ngulchu’s own verses translated in the previous chapter. To differentiate the two, I italicize the first and bold the second.

f.d: thugs rje chen po la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
I bow to great compassion.

d.div: tshe 'dir rgyun gyi yi dam bsgom/ / 'chi khar 'pho ba'i man ngag bsgom/ / bar dor bsre ba bsgom bya ste/ / rgyun du bsgoms pa kun gyi gnad/ /

In this life, cultivate constantly your meditation deity, at time of death, practice the instruction of transference, and in the intermediate state, practice the mixings. The key point is to practice them constantly.
mi rtag sdug bsngal dran byas nas/ / snying rje chen po rab bskyed de/ / spyi bor bla ma snying gar lha/ / rang sems skye med bsgom par bya/ /

div.b: Recalling impermanence and suffering, thoroughly generate great compassion, visualize the guru at your crown and the deity at your heart, and meditate on your mind as devoid of arising.

d.div: [1275] This verse is found in a text in the Tengyur entitled Heart Yoga (Yogasāra, Toh 2855 Tengyur, rgyud, ngu, 196a) by one Śrī Jagatamitrānanda, most probably the same person as the Mitrayogi identified here as the source of this special instruction. In that Tengyur text, however, the last line reads “and meditate on your mind without distraction.” On the somewhat complex history of the root text attributed to Mitrayogi, see my introduction, page 36.
rang lus mchod sbyin byas nas ni/ / ltos pa thams cad rab spangs te/ / 'od kyi sbu gu'i sbyor pa yis/ / sems ni dga' ldan gnas su 'phang / /
Performing the rite of offering your body and having discarded all dependencies, through the medium of a hollow light beam I’ll send my mind to the Tuṣita realm.
'di nyid bar dor shes byas la/ / phyi nang gsang ba bsgyur byas te/ / stong nyid snying rje'i rnal 'byor gyis/ / mkhas pas nying mtshams sbyar bar bya/ /
Recognizing this as the bardo itself and transforming the outer, inner, and secret through the yoga of emptiness and compassion, the wise connect to the new birth.
gang shar ngos 'dzin lta ba'i gnad/ / de la ma yengs bsgom pa'i gnad/ / dran pa ro snyoms spyod pa'i gnad/ / grub thob chen po'i gdams pa'o/ /

f.d: snying po don gsum gyi gdams pa rdzogs so/[1] /zhes gsungs shing /
Here concludes the instruction on the three essential points.

d.div: [1] grub chen mi tra dzo kis mdzad pa'i snying po don gsum gyi man ngag gi rtsa ba rdo rje'i tshig rkang ma zhes pa'i gzhung 'di gdams ngag mdzod pod tapa'i chos tshan nyer dgu pa'i nang bzhugs/

f.d: 'di la gang shar ngos 'dzin lta ba'i gnad/[2] /ces sogs mjug gi sho lo ka gcig lo tsA bas mdzad pa dang / de yan chad grub chen gyis mdzad par bzhed pa dang / yang rgyun du bsgoms pa kun gyi gnad/ /ces pa yan gyi sho lo ka dang po grub chen gyis mdzad la/ de man chad grub chen gyi gsung la lo tsA bas zin bris mdzad par yang bzhed do/ / ji ltar yang 'di nyid kyi don rgyun du nyams su blang bde ba'i phyir kho bos byas ba'i shog gcig ma dang sbyar te bshad pa la gsum/ mchod par brjod pa/ gzhung don dngos rtsom pa/ mjug gi bya ba'o/ /

So it has been taught. Of these, some maintain that the concluding verse, beginning “Recognizing whatever appears is the key point of view,” [578] was composed by the translator [Trophu Lotsāwa] while up to that was authored by the great siddha himself. Others hold that the first stanza was written by the great siddha and what comes subsequently is drawn from notes by the translator based on the great siddha’s own words. Be that as it may, I will explain the instruction here based on the one-pager[1276] I wrote to facilitate its practice on a regular basis. This has three parts: the salutation, the actual body of the composition, and the concluding activities.

d.div: [2] snying po don gsum gyi man ngag gi rtsa ba rdo rje'i tshig rkang / grub chen mi tra dzo ki/ gdams ngag mdzod pod/ ta_chos tshan nyer dgu ba/ shog_2_na3
[1276] This “one-pager” (shog gcig ma) is Ngulchu’s own verse text. In the format of long Tibetan xylograph, it fits on a single folio.

f.d: dang po [mchod par brjod pa/]ni/
1. The first, the salutation,

thugs rje chen po la phyag 'tshal lo/ /zhes pa ste/ 'di la nges don gyi sangs rgyas thams cad kyi thugs rje'i snying rje chen po la phyag 'tshal ba dang / de nyid bzhin lag gi rnam par shar ba ni 'phags pa spyan ras gzigs sam 'jig rten dbang phyug yin la/ shog gcig mar na mo gu ru lo ke shwa rA ya/ zhes na mo phyag 'tshal ba/ gu ru bla ma/ mtshams sbyor phral bas lo ka 'jig rten/ I shwa ra dbang phyug /a ya la ste bla ma 'jig rten dbang phyug la phyag 'tshal lo/ /zhes pa ste don 'dra'o/ /

is as follows: “I bow to great compassion.” Here homage is being paid to the great compassion that is the embodiment of the definitive compassion of all the buddhas. Such great compassion appears in a form with face and arms as Ārya Avalokiteśvara, or Lokeśvara. In the one-pager it reads “Namo Guru Lokeśvarāya.” Namo means “to bow down to,” and guru is “teacher.” When the words are separated, loka means “the world,” īśvara means “the lord,” and aya means “to.” Thus the phrase means: I bow to the teacher called Lord of the World.” The meaning [of the two salutations] remains the same.
gnyis pa gzhung don dngos rtsom pa
2. The second, the actual body of the composition,
['di ]la gsum/ mdor bstan pa/ rgyas par bshad pa/ don bsdu ba'o/ /
has three parts: a brief overview, an extensive explanation, and a concluding summary.
dang po [mdor bstan pa/]ni/
2.1. A brief overview

tshe 'dir rgyun gyi yi dam bsgom/ / zhes pa nas
kun gyi gnad/ ces gsungs te/ gang zag dbang po rab tshe 'dir rgyun gyi yi dam bsgom pa dang / 'bring 'chi khar 'pho ba'i man ngag bsgom pa dang / tha ma bar dor bsre ba'i man ngag bsgom pa ni skabs don yin la/ 'chi kha dang bar do gnyis kyi nyams len kyang da lta nas rgyun du bsgom dgos pa ni nyams len kun gyi gnad yin no/ / zhes pa'i don yin no//

The root text says:
In this life, cultivate constantly your meditation deity, at time of death, practice the instruction of transference, and in the intermediate state, practice the mixings. The key point is to practice them constantly.[1277]
The essential point is this: the person of highest acumen should constantly cultivate the meditation deity in this very life, those of medium acumen should practice the transference instruction at the point of death, and those of the least acumen should practice the mixings during the intermediate state. This said, the practices pertaining to the time of death and the intermediate state should be practiced all the time. And this is the key point of all of your meditative practice.

d.div: [1277] In the original, although only the first line is cited followed by the phrase “up to,” given the brevity of the root text, I have inserted the verses from the root text in their entirety.

f.d: gnyis pa rgyas par bshad pa
2.2. The extensive explanation
['di ]la gsum/ tshe 'di'i nyams len gyi snying po yi dam bsgom pa/ 'chi kha'i nyams len gyi snying po 'pho ba bsgom pa/ bar do'i nyams len gyi snying po bsre ba bsgom pa'o/ /

This is threefold: (1) cultivating the meditation deity, the essence of the practice for this life, (2) transference meditation, the essence of the practice for the time of death, and (3) the mixings, the essence of the practice for the intermediate state.
[tshe 'di'i nyams len gyi snying po yi dam bsgom pa/]
2.2.1. Cultivating the meditation deity, the essence of the practice for this life
dang po la bzhi/ rkyen bskul ma gdab ste sgrubs su 'gro ba/ rgyu byung chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed pa/ thabs bla ma yi dam la gsol ba gdab pa/ ngo bor rang sems skye med du bsgom pa'o/ /

The first has four parts: (1) invocation and going for refuge, the condition, (2) generating the awakening mind, the cause, [579] (3) supplicating the gurus and meditation deities, the method, and (4) meditating on your own mind as devoid of arising, the actual reality.
[rkyen bskul ma gdab ste sgrubs su 'gro ba ]
2.2.1.1. Invocation and going for refuge, the condition

dang po ni/ shog gcig ma las 'dir snying po don gsum mdor bsdus nyams su len tshul ni gnas gtsang mar zhes bas gnas khang byi dor bya ba/ rten zhes pas mchog gsum gyi rten spyi dang khyad par spyan ras gzigs kha sar paNi'i sku brnyan sogs dang / mchod pa bsham/ zhes bas chu gnyis nyer spyod dang bcas pa gang bzang bkod pa mdzes par bsham pa dang / legs par 'khod ces pas bde ba'i stan la lus gnad bdun nam brgyad ldan gyis 'khod pa ston no/ /

With respect to the first, the one-pager explains in a condensed form the way to engage in the practice of the three essential points in the following manner. “In the clean place” explains the need to clean your place of practice; “lay out representations” explains that you should lay out, in general, the representations of the Three Jewels and, more particularly, that of Khasarpāṇi, such as his icon; “the offerings” explains that you should prepare offerings such as the two waters and other articles of everyday enjoyment of as good a quality as possible and arrange them in a beautiful way; to “be seated well” is to sit on a comfortable cushion in the sevenfold or eightfold posture.

de nas skyabs su 'gro ba la/ mi rtag sdug bsngal dran byas nas/ /zhes pa'i don/
mdun gyi pang sdong 'dab bzhi'i zla ba'i gdan/ / zhes pa nas/
bdag dang 'gro rgyud byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ zhes pa'i bar te/

Next, to go for refuge, the meaning of “Recalling impermanence and suffering” is presented in the lines:
To my gurus, who are on a lotus tree in front of me, and to the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and protectors, with thoughts of impermanence and suffering, I go for refuge. Pray bless my mindstream and those of all beings.

mi rtag pa dran pas skyes bu chung ngu'i lam dang / sdug bsngal dran pas skyes bu 'bring gi lam la bsngo bgrang gtong ba'i lugs bsam pa/ lam gyi gtso bo rnam gsum ltar tshe 'di'i snang shas ldog pa dang / phyi ma'i snang shas ldog pa'i thabs tshul bsam par bya ste/
rnyed dka' rig na gyi nar sdod thabs med/ / don chen bsam na don med 'da' ba phangs/ / 'chi ba dran na phyi mar 'gro grab byed/ / las 'bras bsam na bag med gnas las ldog[3] / ces gsungs pa ltar dal 'byor gyi rten 'di shin tu rnyed dka' zhing don che la 'jig par sla bas ring du mi gnas par 'chi zhing shi ba'i 'og tu bde 'gro dang ngan 'gro gang rung du skye ba las 'os med pas ngan song gsum lta ci smos/ bde 'gro'i gnas su'ang sdug bsngal 'ba' zhig las med cing sdug bsngal de ni las rgyu 'bras las 'byung la/ 'khor ba dang ngan song gi sdug bsngal myong ba'i rgyu las ngan pa bsags pa ni bgrangs las 'das shing / da dung 'bad rtsol la ma ltos par gsog pas na 'bras bu sdug bsngal myong ba las 'os med/ des sdug bsngal 'di las skyob pa'i nus pa bla ma dkon mchog gsum las gzhan med pas bla ma dkon mchog la skyabs su song ste skyabs gnas zhu dgos par dug snyam du bsam/

“Recalling impermanence” relates to the path of the lesser capacity, while “recalling suffering” relates to the path of the intermediate capacity. Here you recall them by mentally reviewing them. Contemplate, as presented in the Three Principal Elements of the Path, the way you turn away from preoccupations with this life and preoccupations with the next life. [Jé Tsongkhapa says]:
If we know how hard it is to find, we will not remain idle. If we see its great value, we will not waste our time. If we contemplate death, we will prepare for our next life. If we contemplate karma, we will renounce heedless acts.[1278] As this states, you should contemplate in the following way. This human existence with leisure and opportunity is extremely hard to find and is invaluable. It is also easily destroyed, for this life cannot last long and the reality of death is ever present. In the aftermath of death too, I have no choice but to be reborn in either the fortunate or the unfortunate realms. And let alone the lower realms, even rebirth in the fortunate realms is nothing but suffering. Suffering comes from karma, the causal law, and as for my accumulation of negative karma, the cause of samsara and birth in the lower realms, it is incalculable. Even now I am continually gathering them without any effort. So I have no choice but to experience their fruit, suffering. Only my guru and the Three Jewels can save me from such suffering. So I must go for refuge to the Three Jewels with the thought that I will seek them as objects of my refuge.

d.div: [3] rje tsong kha pa'i gsung 'bum/ kha_gsung thor bu/ shog_179_na6
[1278] “A Reply to Namkha Palsang’s Letter,” Miscellaneous Writings, 265.

f.d: de la thog mar skyabs yul gsal 'debs tshul ni/ rang nyid gnas pa'i sa phyogs thams cad dag pa'i zhing khams gser gyi sa gzhi la baiDUraya'i mig mang ris dang ldan pa'i rang gi mdun du 'o ma'i rgya mtsho chen po'i dbus nas pad+ma'i sdong po thon pa'i rtse mo 'dab ma bzhi pa rgya che zhing khyon yangs pa lte ba'i dbus pad+ma dkar po dang zla ba'i gdan la rtsa ba'i bla ma thugs rje chen po khasarapANi/ de'i mtha' skor lte ba'i steng du mdun nas brtsams te g.yas skor du 'phags pa spyan ras gzigs nas rtsa ba'i bla ma'i bar gyi brgyud pa'i bla ma rnams dang / mdun gyi 'dab ma'i steng du thub dbang rdo rje 'chang la rgyud sde bzhi'i yi dam dang sangs rgyas stong la sogs pa'i longs sprul gyi sangs rgyas rnams kyis bskor ba/ g.yas kyi 'dab mar chos khri phun tshogs la lung gi chos dkon mchog rnams baiDUraya'i shog bu la gser gyi yi ge rang sgra sgrog cing 'od zer 'phro bas sems can gyi don mdzad pa/ rgyab kyi 'dab mar 'phags pa spyan ras gzigs phyag bzhi pa'am phyag gnyis pa gang rung gis mtshon pa'i byang sems rang rgyal nyan thos te theg pa gsum gyi dge 'dun rnams dang / g.yon gyi 'dab mar dpa' bo mkha' gro dang ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa la sogs pa'i chos skyong srung ma dang bcas pa'i skyabs yul rnams zhal rang la phyogs shing dgyes pa'i tshul gyis bzhugs pa gsal legs par btab/

Set up your field of refuge as follows. Imagine where you are [580] is a pure realm where the earth is gold and adorned with patterns of strings of lapis lazuli. In front of you is a great sea of milk, and in its center is a large lotus tree whose tip has four large petals that create an opening. At the center of this is a white lotus flower and a moon disc on which sits your kind root guru, the great compassionate Khasarpāṇi. Around him on the hub of the lotus flower are the lineage gurus, starting from Ārya Avalokiteśvara at his front and continuing clockwise up to your own root guru. On the front petal is the sovereign sage Vajradhara, who is surrounded by the deities of the four classes of tantra as well as saṃbhogakāya and nirmāṇakāya buddhas like the thousand buddhas [of the Fortunate Eon]. On the petal to the right [of Khasarpāṇi], on an excellent throne, is the scriptural Dharma Jewel in the form of texts written on gold leaves with lapis ink, resounding the words of the scriptures, radiating light, and performing the welfare of sentient beings. On the rear petal are the sangha members of the three vehicles — bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteśvara, in either his one-face four-arm form or his one-face two-arm form, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas. On the left petal are ḍākas, ḍākinīs, and Dharma protectors like Six-Arm Mahākāla. Visualize that all the members of your refuge field face you and reside with joy.

rang gi g.yas su tshe 'di'i pha/ g.yon du ma/ mdun du dgra 'dre byur gsum/ rgyab tu rigs drug bar do dang bcas pa'i sems can thams cad smra shes don go ba mi'i rnam pa can sa chen po'i khyon thams cad smug shig ge gang bar bsam la/ rang gzhan thams cad 'chi ba mi rtag pa dang 'khor ba spyi dang bye brag gi sdug bsngal dran nas 'jigs shing skrag pas dkon mchog la re ltos 'cha' ba dang bcas pa'i skyabs 'gro'i rgyu gsal btab ste shugs drag pos skyabs su mchi ba ste 'gro'o// bdag dang 'gro ba sems can thams cad kyi sems kyi rgyud rigs 'dra snga ba mi dge ba'i rang bzhin can 'di byams snying rje byang chub kyi sems dang / yang dag pa'i lta ba skye ba la sogs pa'i dag par sgyur cig ces pa ni byin gyis rlab tu gsol zhes pa'i don no/ / de ltar gdung shugs drag pos skyabs su song bas skyabs yul rnams las bdud rtsi dkar po'i rgyun byung nas rang gzhan thams cad la thim pas lus ngag yid gsum gyi sdig sgrib bag chags dang bcas pa sbyangs nas lus longs sku spyan ras gzigs dang / sems ye shes chos skur gyur nas sems can gzhan rnams rang rang gi dag zhing la 'ur 'ding gis 'phur te gshegs/ skyabs yul rnams mtha' nas rim gyis bsdus te gtso bo la thim/ de yang rang gi smin mtshams su thim pas dkon mchog gsum gyi byin rlabs thob par bsam mo//

Imagine on your right is your father of this life, on your left your mother, in front are your enemies, demons, and harmful spirits, and behind you, in a large mass, are all the sentient beings of the six realms, including those in the intermediate state, all of them in human form and able to speak and understand the meaning of words. Then imagine that you and all other beings, by contemplating the impermanence of death and the sufferings of samsara, both general and specific, experience terror, and from such fear you place your trust and hope in the Three Jewels. In this way, establish the conditions for refuge and fervently go for refuge. Supplicating that the mindstreams of me and all sentient beings, whose mindstreams have until now been saturated with nonvirtue, may become purified through the arising of loving kindness, compassion, the awakening mind, and the perfect view is the meaning of requesting blessings. Imagine that, as result of such fervent appeals and of going for refuge, white nectar streams from the fields of refuge [581] and dissolves into all of you. Through this all the negative karma of your body, speech, and mind and all your obscurations and their imprints are purified. Imagine that all your bodies transform into the saṃbhogakāya Avalokiteśvara, and all your minds transform into gnosis dharmakāya. Imagine that all the other sentient beings en masse return as if flying to their respective pure lands. The members of the refuge field are gradually absorbed, from the edges to the center, merging eventually into the principal figure. He too dissolves into the point between your eyebrows, and you imagine that you have received the blessing of the Three Jewels.
gnyis pa rgyu byung chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed pa ni/
2.2.1.2. Generating the awakening mind, the cause

snying rje chen po rab bskyed de/ /zhes pa'i don/
drin can ma rnams srid zhi'i rgya mtsho las/ / zhes pa nas/
bsdus pa'i gdams pa nyams su blang bar bgyi/ / zhes pa'i bar te/

This is presented by the line “Thoroughly generate great compassion,” which is explained in the following:
To free my kind mothers from samsara’s ocean, I shall generate the awakening mind and put into practice the instruction that distills the essence of the sutra and tantra teachings into three points.

snying rje chen po ni lus can rnams kyi srog gi dbang po dang 'dra bar sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad snying rje chen po 'di yod na yod dang med na med yin pa ni/ 'jug pa las/
gang phyir brtse nyid rgyal ba'i lo thog phun tshogs 'di'i/ / sa bon dang ni spel la chu 'dra yun ring du/ / longs spyod gnas la smin pa lta bu 'dod gyur ba/ / de phyir bdag gis thog mar snying rje bstod par bgyi/[4] / zhes gsungs pa ltar/

Just as the life faculty is fundamental for living beings, great compassion is fundamental to all attributes of the buddha: when it is present all other attributes are present, and when it is absent none of the attributes are present. Entering the Middle Way says:
As compassion alone is accepted to be the seed of the perfect harvest of buddhahood, the water that nourishes it, and the fruit that is long a source of enjoyment, I will praise compassion at the start of all.[1279]

d.div: [4] sde dge_3861_bstan/ dbu ma/ 'a_slob dpon zla ba grags pa/ dbu ma la 'jug pa/ sems bskyed/ 1_sh+loka_2_shog_201_ba2
[1279] Candrakīrti, Madhyamakāvatāra, 1.2, Toh 3861 Tengyur, dbu ma, ’a, 201a2.

f.d: dper na 'jig rten gyi lo thog phun sum tshogs pa 'byung ba la dang por bskyed pa la gal che ba sa bon dang / bar du gong 'phel du 'gyur ba la gal che ba chu lud dang / tha mar longs spyod pa la gal che ba 'bras bu smin pa zhig dgos pa ltar/ 'dir yang thog mar gal che ba byang chub kyi sems skye ba ni/ brtse ba snying rje chen po la rag las shing / bar du gal che ba sems bskyed mi nyams shing gong 'phel du 'gyur ba dang / tha mar gal che ba nyer zhi'i dbyings la mi gnas par sems can gyi don mdzad pa'ang snying rje chen po la rag las pa'o/ /

In the mundane example of seeking an excellent crop, first the seed is important for producing the crop; in the middle, moisture is important to nurture and enhance the growth; and at the end, for a good harvest, a good ripening of the crop is foremost. In the same way, first engendering the awakening mind relies foremost on compassion; then in the middle, compassion ensures that the awakening mind does not degenerate but is further enhanced; and compassion is vital at the end because it is thanks to compassion that we do not linger in the peace of nirvana but pursue the welfare of the sentient beings.

de lta bu'i brtse ba snying rje chen po de yang 'khor ba dang ngan song gi sdug bsngal la rang nyid lhag par 'jigs nas 'khor ba'i gnas ni me 'obs ltar mthong bas yid 'byung zhing rang nyid kyi sdug bsngal las rjes su dpags nas ma rgan sems can thams cad kyang de lta bu'i sdug bsngal gyi rang bzhin las ma 'das la/ sems can thams cad kyi thog ma med pa nas drin gyis bskyangs pa la bgrang las 'das shing ma 'ongs pa na'ang sbyong ba dang / der ma zad sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob pa yang sems can la rag las pas na sems can thams cad gces shing phangs la yid du 'ong ba'i rnam par shes nas drin can gyi ma sems can thams cad zab mo stong pa nyid kyis dug mtsho dang 'dra ba'i srid pa 'khor ba dang / snying rje chen pos 'o ma'i mtsho dang 'dra ba'i zhi ba myang 'das kyi rgya mtsho chen po las bdag nyid gcig pus bsgral bar bya'o snyam du lhag bsam bskyed nas/ de yang da lta bdag la de lta bu'i nus pa mi 'dug pas sems can rnams srid zhi'i 'jigs pa las bsgral ba'i phyir bdag gis rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang rin po che ci nas kyang thob par bya snyam du smon pa byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed/ de lta bu'i sangs rgyas de yang rgyu med pa dang mi mthun pa'i rgyu las mi 'byung bas na mdo dang sngags kyi chos thams cad kyi snying po don gsum du hril gyis bsdus pa'i gdams pa zab mo snying po don gsum du grags pa 'di nyid nyams su blang bar bgyi'o snyam du dam bca' zhing brjod pa ni 'jug pa sems bskyed yin no//

The way you give birth to such great compassion is by developing a disenchantment with samsara that sees the entirety of samsara as a burning fire and feels terror at the suffering of samsara and the lower realms. You then infer from your own situation that all these old mother sentient beings are also subject to such a terrifying suffering fate. Contemplate as well the incalculable kindness you have received from all sentient beings since beginningless time and how, in the future, they will continue to extend such kindness. Furthermore, even attaining buddhahood [582] depends on sentient beings. In this way, recognize how all sentient beings are dear to you and deserve your concern. Then develop the thought “I alone, through [the wisdom of] profound emptiness, will free all beings from this poisonous ocean of samsara and, through great compassion, will lead them to the peace of nirvana’s great ocean that is like a sea of soothing milk.” In this way, generate the altruistic revolve. Then contemplate, “Yet at present, I do not have the capacity to accomplish this. So to free sentient beings from the dangers of samsara as well as nirvana, I must somehow attain the precious state of full enlightenment.” In this way, generate the aspiring awakening mind. Then generate the thought “Now such buddhahood does not come about without causes and conditions, so I will engage in the practice of this profound instruction renowned as the Three Essential Points, which comprehensively condenses the essence of all the teachings of sutra and tantra into three points.” To make such a promise constitutes generating the engaging awakening mind.
gsum pa thabs bla ma yi dam la gsol ba gdab pa ni/
2.2.1.3. Supplicating the gurus and meditation deities, the method

spyi bor bla ma snying gar lha/ /zhes pa'i don/
spyi bor shel dkar byang chub mchod rten gyi/ zhes pa nas/
oM ma Ni pad+me hUM/ zhes pa'i bar te/

This is presented by the line “Visualize the guru at your crown and the deity at your heart,” which is explained in the following:
O gurus and buddhas, possessors of limitless compassion, pray help me and beings equal to the reaches of space purify the two obscurations and perfect the two accumulations so that we may soon attain buddhahood. Having been appealed thusly, the gurus and the buddhas emit streams of white nectar, which enter my crown and absorb into the deity and the ah syllable at my heart; nectars flowing from this purify the two obscurations. With these two purities, I become the Great Compassionate One, the guru at my crown dissolves into the deity, the thousand buddhas dissolve into the thousand ah syllables, and like the vanishing of a rainbow, the stupa dissolves into space. At the heart of the deity, on a moon disc and around letter hrīḥ, are the six syllables, from which light radiates and retracts; this purifies the world and its denizens and invokes the conquerors’ compassion. May I be blessed with the three embodiments and the three perspectives.
Om maṇi padme hūṃ.

rang nyid tha mal ba'i spyi bor rgyu shel dkar dri ma med pa las grub pa'i byang chub mchod rten kha dog dkar po 'od zer dpag tu med pa 'phro bas 'dzin/ them skas gsum/ gdong chen/ pad chung / ba gam/ dge bcu/ bang rim bzhi/ bum gdan/ bum pa/ bre gdan/ bre/ gdugs 'degs/ chos 'khor bcu gsum/ thugs rje mdo gzung / gdugs/ char khebs/ zla nyi/ tog dang bcas pa'i mtshan nyid yongs su rdzogs pa/ bum pa'i nang du pad+ma dkar po 'dab ma brgyad pa'i lte bar zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du ngo bor rang gi drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma yin pa la rnam pa spyan ras gzigs kha sar pANi sku mdog dkar po zhal gcig phyag gnyis g.yas mchog sbyin dang g.yon thugs kar chos 'chad kyi phyag rgya mdzad pa'i mtheb srin gyis pad+ma dkar po'i yu ba 'dzin pa'i 'dab ma snyan g.yon ba'i thad du kha phye ba 'dzin pa/ zhabs gnyis mnyam pa'i stabs kyis bzhengs pa dar gyi na bza' dang rin po che'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ bang rim bzhi po spyir sgo stong phrag gcig yod pa'i sgo rer sangs rgyas re bzhugs pa'o/ /

While remaining in your ordinary form yourself, visualize at your crown a bodhi stupa made of unblemished white crystal radiating lights immeasurably bright. It has all the following features complete: base, three steps, square platform, small lotus, top of the platform, ten virtues, four steps, base of the vase, the vase, base of the canopy, canopy, platform for the parasol, thirteen rings, scripture chamber, parasol, rain cover, moon, sun, and crowning jewel. Inside the vase, at the center of an eight-petaled lotus and on a moon disc, is your kind root guru in the form of Avalokiteśvara Khasarpāṇi. White in color, he has one face and two arms. His right hand is in the gesture of granting wishes, while his left at his heart is in the gesture of teaching. Between his left thumb and index finger, he holds the stem of a white lotus whose petals are open at the level of his left ear. He is in a standing position, with both his legs straight, and he is adorned in silk garments and precious ornaments. On the four steps are a thousand small doors, [583] and at each entrance is one of the thousand buddhas.

de yang bang rim 'og ma'i phyogs rer cha chung nyer bzhi re/ de'i steng mar nyer gnyis re/ de'i steng mar nyi shu re/ de'i steng mar bco brgyad re yod pa la rgyal ba lnga pa chen po'i lugs la sangs rgyas rnams rigs bzhi'i rnam par bzhed pa ltar na bang rim 'og ma gsum gyi cha chung re'i sum cha'i sar sangs rgyas re bzhugs pas phyogs rer bang rim 'og ma la don gnyis re/ de'i steng mar re drug re/ de'i steng mar drug cu re bzhugs shing / steng ma'i phyogs rer nga gnyis re bzhugs pa'i tshangs thig gi g.yas g.yon du cha chung gi sum cha gnyis re'i sar sangs rgyas sku bong che ba phyogs rer gnyis re bsdoms pas brgyad dang de phyin sum cha re'i sar sangs rgyas re bzhugs pa shar nas brtsams te rnam snang / rin 'byung / 'od dpag med/ don grub ste rigs bzhi'i rnam par bzhugs shing / slar snying ga'i a yig la bsdu ba'i tshe dbus kyi pad 'dab brgyad la a yig che ba re bsgom pa la sangs rgyas che ba re bstims pas legs par snang la/

The heights of the four steps are, from bottom to top respectively, twenty-four micro-units,[1280] twenty-two, twenty, and eighteen. If, as in the Fifth Dalai Lama’s tradition, the buddhas are visualized in the form of the lords of the buddha families, then imagine a buddha resides in the space of two-thirds of a micro-unit, which would mean there would be seventy-two buddhas on each of the four faces of the lowest step, sixty on each face on the next step, another sixty on each face of the next step, and fifty-two on each of the four faces of the last step. On either side of the center line in each of the four directions, in the space of two-thirds a micro-unit, is a buddha slighter larger in size — making eight such buddhas [on each level]. All these buddhas are in the form of the lords of the families, with Vairocana in the east, Ratnasambhava in the south, Amitābha in the west, and Amoghasiddhi in the north. When you dissolve all of them into the ah syllable at your heart, do so by visualizing eight large ah syllables on the eight petals of the lotus and the buddhas dissolving into them. This system seems excellent.

d.div: [1280] Four micro-units (cha chung) equal one “door size” (sgo tshad ), which is the length of full-stretched arms of the principal deity of the mandala, which is in turn equivalent to the height of the deity’s body. These two units — cha chung and sgo tshad — are the two key units of measurement in the drawing and construction of a mandala.

f.d: 'on kyang paN chen chos kyi rgyal mtshan gyis sangs rgyas stong rigs lnga'i rnam par gsungs pa'i dgongs pa ni/[5] bang rim bzhi'i phyogs bzhir mas rim bzhin don gnyis re/ drug cu re drug re/ drug cu re gnyis re/ lnga bcu re/zhes sdom tshig ltar bzhugs pa la bang rim 'og ma gsum gyi shar phyogs pa nyis brgya sku mdog dkar po byang chub mchog gi phyag rgya can/ lho phyogs pa nyis brgya ser po mchog sbyin mnyam gzhag can/ nub phyogs pa nyis brgya dmar po mnyam gzhag can/ byang phyogs pa nyis brgya ljang khu skyabs sbyin mnyam gzhag can/ bang rim steng mi'i phyogs bzhi ga bsdoms pa'i nyis brgya sngon po sa gnon mnyam gzhag can gyi rigs lnga'i rnam par bzhugs pa paN chen thams cad mkhyen pa'i dgongs bzhed mthar thug yin pa phyis brtags pa na/[6] gdugs dkar gyi dbus zhal nyis brgya dkar po/ g.yas zhal nyis brgya ser po/ rgyab zhal nyis brgya dmar po/ g.yon zhal nyis brgya ljang khu/ steng zhal nyis brgya sngon po zhes pa dang yang mthun pas shin tu ngo mtshar bar go bas shog gcig mar sangs rgyas stong ni rigs lnga'i rnam par bzhugs zhes bsgyur yod gsung / thams cad kyang chos gos rnam gsum dang ldan pa sprul sku'i rnam pa can zhal nang du gzigs pa'o//

That said, Panchen Chökyi Gyaltsen says to view the thousand buddhas as the lords of the buddha families in the following manner.[1281] On the steps, on each of the four faces from bottom to top respectively, are seventy-two buddhas, then sixty-four, sixty-two, and fifty. Of these, all two hundred buddhas on the three lower steps of the east are white and display the gesture of supreme enlightenment. All two hundred in the south are yellow and display the gestures of granting wishes and meditative equipoise. All two hundred in the west are red and display the gesture of meditative equipoise. And all two hundred in the north are green and display the gesture of granting refuge. All the buddhas in the four directions on the top step, two hundred in total, are blue and display the gestures of touching the earth and meditative equipoise. When, upon investigation, I understood this to be Panchen’s mature understanding, I recognized that it is strikingly commensurate with the system of visualizing, in the context of the goddess Sitātapatrā (White Umbrella), her central two hundred faces as white, her two hundred right faces as yellow, her two hundred rear faces as red, her two hundred left faces as green, and her two hundred faces on the top as blue. Impressed by this understanding, in the one-pager, I have rendered this as “The thousand buddhas are present as lords of the five families,” said the master.[1282] [584] All the buddhas are in nirmāṇakāya form, wearing the three robes and turning their face inward.

d.div: [5] paN chen blo bzang chos kyi rgyal mtshan gyi gsung 'bum/ nga _snying po don gsum gyi khrid 'phags pa spyan ras gzigs la brten pa shin tu legs pa/ shog_2_na3
[6] ma dper phyis rtags pa ni zhes byung yang yig nor du snang bas phyis brtags pa na zhes bcos yod/
[1281] Panchen Losang Chökyi Gyaltsen, Excellent Guide to the Three Essential Points, 417.
[1282] Here, Jedrung Tsering, the scribe of this text and a senior disciple of Ngulchu, is reporting his guru’s words.

f.d:
rang tha mal pa'i lus stong sang gi nang du rang gi snying pad+ma dmar po 'dab ma stong ldan steng 'og tu pad rim dgu brtsigs kyi 'og ma las steng ma rim bzhin grangs je nyung dang / dpang je mthor song ba'i snying zugs can te/
mtsho bug gzugs dang mtsho ri gzugs/ / mtsho dbang gzugs dang mtsho me gzugs/ / mtsho zla gzugs dang mtsho bug dang / / mtsho ri mtsho dbang klu ste stong / / zhes pa ltar/ bang rim 'og mar 'dab ma brgya dang go bzhi/ de'i steng mar brgya don bzhi/ de'i steng mar brgya nga bzhi/ de'i steng mar brgya so bzhi/ de'i steng mar brgya bcu bzhi/ de'i steng mar go bzhi/ de'i steng mar don bzhi/ de'i steng mar nga bzhi/ de'i steng mar 'dab ma brgyad do/ /

With yourself in your ordinary appearance, visualize that inside your body, imagined as an empty shell, your heart is shaped like a lotus with thousand petals on nine levels, with progressively fewer but larger petals from bottom to top. As stated in the lines:
In shapes of swirling waves and of rising swells, shapes of peaking seas and flickering seas, shapes of cresting seas and swirling waves, and shapes of rising swells and peaking seas — numbering a thousand.[1283] Thus on the lowest level are 194 petals, on the next level are 174, on the next 154, the next 134, the next 114, the next 94, the next 74, the next 54, and on top are 8 petals.

d.div: [1283] Source not located.

f.d: 'dab ma brgyad pa'i lte bar zla ba'i gdan la rang gi rlung sems shin tu phra ba'i ngo bo spyan ras gzigs kha sar pANi mtshon gang tsam dang / 'dab ma rnams kyi steng du a thung dkar po lang stabs kha nang du bstan te thams cad kyang snang la rang bzhin med pa me long gi gzugs brnyan ltar bsam par bya ste/ gzhi la pad+ma khams dmar po/ as khams dkar po/ kha sar pANis rlung dang de'i thugs ka'i hrIHsa sems mtshon pa yin gsungs/

At the center of this eight-petaled lotus, on a moon disc, is your subtle wind-mind in the form of Avalokiteśvara Khasarpāṇi about the size of a thumbnail, while on each petal is a short a in standing position facing inward. Generate these like reflections in a mirror, appearing yet devoid of intrinsic existence. On the ground, the lotus represents the red element, ah the white element, Khasarpāṇi the winds, the syllable hrīḥ at his heart your mind. Thus the master said.

bla ma zhes pas bum nang du bzhugs pa dang lha zhes pas sangs rgyas dang snying ga'i yi dam la go dgos shing / de rnams kyi spyi bor sku'i gsang ba oM yig dkar po/ mgrin par gsung gi gsang ba AHyig dmar po/ thugs kar thugs kyi gsang ba hrIHdkar po hUM sngon pos mtshan pa/ hUM yig las 'od zer dmar po lcags kyu lta bu dpag tu med pa 'phros pas rang bzhin gyi gnas nas rgyal ba sras dang bcas pa spyan drangs te re re la yang ye shes pa cha tshang ba re re thim par bsam zhing / spro na chos 'khor bcu gsum gyi khongs su brgyud pa'i bla ma rnams mtho brtsegs su bzhugs par bsam mo//

“The gurus” refers to the ones residing inside the vase [of the stupa], “the deity” indicates the buddha and the meditation deity at your heart. On their body, at their crown is a white oṃ, the secret of the exalted body; at their throat is a red āḥ, the secret of the exalted speech; at their heart is a blue hrīḥ marked by a blue hūṃ. Countless beams of red light shaped like hooks radiate, inviting the buddhas and bodhisattvas from their natural abodes, and you imagine that gnosis beings enter into each and every one [of the figures visualized thus far]. If you wish to elaborate, you could visualize the lineage gurus on the thirteen rings [of the stupa].

de nas yan lag bdun pa 'bul ba la 'bul yul ni spyi bor bzhugs pa rnams yin pas de rnams la dmigs te lus ngag yid gsum gyis phyag 'tshal ba yan lag dang po dang / dngos bshams yid sprul phyi nang gsang ba de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa 'bul ba gnyis pa dang / rang bzhin gyi sdig pa dang bcas 'gal gyi ltung ba bshags pa gsum pa dang / rang gzhan skye 'phags kyi dge ba la rjes su yi rang ba bzhi pa dang / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar bskul ba lnga pa dang / dus rgyun du ste bskal ba'i bar du mya ngan las mi 'da' bar gsol ba gdab pa drug pa ste phyi ma 'di gnyis la gsol ba btab pa bzhin zhal gyis bzhes par bsam pa rten 'brel gyi gnad do/ / da lam nyams su blangs pa'i dge ba 'di mtshon byed du byas te rang gzhan dus gsum gyi dge ba thams cad sems can gyi don du bla na med pa'i byang chub thob pa'i rgyur gyur cig snyam du bsngo ba ni yan lag bdun pa'o//

Next is offering the seven limbs. The fields to which you are offering are those residing at your crown. So focusing on and paying homage to them with your body, speech, and mind is the first limb. The second limb is making offerings, those actually laid out and those imagined, as well as the outer, inner, secret, and suchness offerings. [585] Confessing and purifying the negative karma of naturally reprehensible acts and of the downfalls from transgressing your precepts is the third limb. Rejoicing in the virtues of self and others, as well as those of ordinary and ārya beings, is the fourth limb. Appealing [to the teachers] to turn the wheel of Dharma is the fifth limb. Supplicating them to not enter nirvana and to remain for eons is the sixth limb. For these preceding two limbs, crucially, for the sake of auspiciousness, imagine that the figures in the refuge fields grant their acceptance. For the seventh limb, dedicate the merits such as your present practice with the thought “I dedicate all virtues, my own and others’, to the attainment of unexcelled enlightenment for the benefit of all sentient beings.”

de nas gsol ba 'debs pa'i rten du maN+Dal nyer gsum ma dmigs pa brtan pos phul la thal mo sbyar te/
rtsa brgyud kyi bla ma dang / sgo stong la bzhugs pa'i sangs rgyas snying rje chen po tshad med pa mnga' ba'i thugs rje can rnams kyis bdag dang nam mkha'i khyon dang mnyam pa'i 'gro ba sems can ma lus pa'i nyon mongs pa dang shes bya'i sgrib pa gnyis bag chags dang bcas pa byang zhing / bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs gnyis rab tu rdzogs te dus ring po min par snyigs dus kyi tshe thung gcig lta bu'i dus shin tu myur bar yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par mdzad du gsol/ zhes gdung shugs drag pos lan gsum la sogs par gsol ba gdab par bya'o/ /

Then to the object of your supplication, with single-pointed focus, make a twenty-part mandala offering. With your palms folded, make the following supplication:
O root and lineage gurus and the buddhas residing in the thousand doors, all of you endowed with limitless great compassion: Help me and all sentient beings equal to the extent of space that our two obscurations — afflictive obscuration and knowledge obscuration — may be purified along with their imprints. Likewise, may we, having perfected the two collections of wisdom and merit in the not too distant future — in fact, within this short human life of the degenerate age — attain the state of perfect buddhahood. Make such a supplication fervently three times or more.

de ltar gsol ba btab pa la brten nas rtsa brgyud kyi bla ma dang sangs rgyas rnams kyi sku'i cha las bdud rtsi dkar po 'od zer 'phro ba dang bcas pa'i rgyun babs/ rang gi spyi bo'i tshangs bug nas zhugs te snying ga'i yi dam a yig dang bcas pa la thim/ de rnams la rang gi byed spyod ngan pa'i nyams grib 'phog pa thams cad sbyangs/ gzi brjid dang nus pa mthu can du gyur nas de rnams las bdud rtsi dkar po 'od zer 'phro ba dang bcas pa'i rgyun byung bas rang gi sgo gsum gyi sgrib gnyis bag chags dang bcas pa sbyangs te 'og sgo dang ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas phyir thon te gar song cha med du dag par bsam pa ni sdig sgrib sbyong ba rdor sems bsgom bzlas kyi gnad tshang ba'i man ngag go/

By virtue of supplicating in this way, streams of white nectar glowing with light descend from the bodies of the root and lineage gurus and the buddhas, enter your crown aperture, and absorb into the meditation deity together with the ah at your heart. Imagine that any pollution you may have in relation to them because of your wrong deeds is cleansed away and that they become potent in their transformative power and capacity. The streams of luminous white nectar flowing from them purifies the nonvirtue of your three doors and of the two obscurations along with their imprints and exits through your lower openings and through all your pores. Imagine [your impurities] disperse and vanish with no trace. This is a pith instruction on the practice of purifying your negative karma and obscurations containing the essential points of Vajrasattva meditation and recitation.

de nas rang gi lus ni sku dag pa sgyu ma'i sku dang / sems ni thugs dag pa don dam 'od gsal te dag pa gnyis ldan thugs rje chen po rgyal ba rgya mtsho'am gsang bsgrub ces kyang bya ba'i yab yum gyi skur gyur pa'i mos pa bya'o/ / de nas brgyud pa'i bla ma sngar bsgoms yod na rtsa brgyud kyi bla ma rnams snying ga'i yi dam la thim zhing / sangs rgyas stong yang pad+ma'i steng gi a yig stong la thim/ mchod rten nam mkha' la 'ja' yal ba ltar mi dmigs par gyur par bsam mo//

Next, imagine that you have become the Great Compassionate Jinasāgara, known also as Secret Attainment Avalokiteśvara, lord and consort, endowed with the two purities — your body’s pure illusory body and your mind’s pure ultimate clear light. [586] If you had earlier visualized the lineage gurus, at this point dissolve the root and lineage gurus into the meditation deity at your heart, and the thousand buddhas into the ah syllables on the thousand lotus petals. Imagine that the stupa also becomes no more, as if vanishing into the sky.

de nas snying gar lha bsgom pa'i man ngag gtso bo ni/ rang rgyal ba rgya mtshor gsal ba'i snying gar bla ma dang yi dam dbyer med pa kha sar pA_Ni'i thugs kar zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng hrIHyig dkar po hUM sngon pos mtshan pa'i mthar oM ma Ni pad+me hUM zhes pa'i yi ge drug pa'i sngags kyi 'phreng ba'i kha dog dkar pos g.yas skor du bskor ba la dmigs te bzlas pa ci 'grub bya zhing / de'i tshe dmigs pa ni sa bon sngags 'phreng dang bcas pa las 'od zer mu mtha' med pa spros te snod kyi 'jig rten thams cad la reg pa tsam gyis nyes skyon thams cad sbyangs te dag pa'i zhing khams bde ba can lta bur gyur/ yang 'od zer gyi sne la 'phags pa spyan ras gzigs kyi sku dpag med spros pa bcud kyi sems can thams cad la khyab ste sems can re re'i spyi bor spyan ras gzigs re re bzhugs pa las bdud rtsi'i rgyun babs pas/ dmyal ba/ yi dwags/ dud 'gro/ mi/ lha min/ lha sogs ba'i rigs drug bar do dang bcas pa so so'i sgrib gnyis rgyu bcas sbyangs te thugs rje chen po'i go 'phang la bkod par bsam pa dang / yang 'od zer dpag tu med pa'i sne mor chu gnyis nyer spyod rol mo 'dod yon/ rgyal srid sna bdun/ bkra shis rtags rdzas la sogs pa'i mchod rdzas mtha' yas pa spros te phyogs bcu'i zhing rab 'byams na bzhugs pa'i rgyal ba sras bcas thams cad la mchod pa phul bas thugs rje bskul te rab tu dgyes shing sku gsung thugs kyi byin rlabs nus mthu thams cad thugs ka'i sngags 'phreng sa bon dang bcas pa la thim pas yi dam kun 'dus kyi ngo bo snying ga'i kha sar pANi/ bla ma kun 'dus kyi ngo bo de'i rigs bdag bla ma 'od dpag med/ gzungs sngags kun 'dus kyi ngo bo thugs ka'i yi ge drug pa ste kun 'dus gsum dang / rang gi mig la gang snang thams cad thugs rje chen po'i sku/ rna bar sgra gang grag yi ge drug pa'i sgra/ sems la bzang ngan gyi rtog pa gang shar bla ma thugs rje chen po'i thugs stong nyid snying rje'i snying po can du mos pa ni 'khyer so gsum yin pas de dag dang ldan par bsam mo//

Next, as for the main instruction on how to visualize the meditation deity at your heart, visualize yourself as Avalokiteśvara Jinasāgara and visualize at your heart Khasarpāṇi, who is the indivisible nature of your guru and meditation deity. At his heart on a moon disc is a white hrīḥ marked by a blue hūṃ, which is encircled clockwise by the letters of the six syllables Oṃ maṇi padme hūṃ, all white in color. Focused on this mantra, repeat it as many times as you can. As you recite the mantra, visualize that incalculable light beams radiate from it and that the worlds they touch are purified of all of their stains and faults on contact, turning them into Sukhāvatī pure lands. Again, imagine, at the tips of these beams of light are incalculable Avalokiteśvara bodies touching all sentient beings. Imagine at the crown of each sentient being sits an Avalokiteśvara from whom descends streams of nectar. Imagine that this purifies the two obscurations and their causes for beings in all six realms — hell beings, hungry ghosts, animals, humans, demigods, and gods — and places them in the state of the Great Compassionate One. Again, imagine, at the tips of all these incalculable beams of light are limitless offerings — water for drinking and washing, articles of everyday enjoyment, music, objects of the five senses, the seven royal emblems, and the eight auspicious symbols — which are offered to the buddhas and bodhisattvas residing in the myriad worlds of all ten directions. This invokes their compassion, and the blessing and power of their body, speech, and mind dissolve into the mantra and the syllable at the center of your heart. This gives rise to three embodiments — Khasarpāṇi at your heart, the embodiment of all meditation deities; Guru Amitābha, the lord of buddha families who is the embodiment of all gurus; and the six-syllable mantra, the embodiment of all mantras. You also become endowed with the three perspectives — viewing whatever appears to your eyes as the body of the Great Compassionate One; whatever sound is heard by your ears as the sound of six-syllable mantra; and [587] whatever thoughts arise, good or bad, as the exalted mind of Guru Compassionate One, emptiness whose essence is compassion.
bzhi pa rang sems ngo bo skye med du bsgom pa ni/
2.2.1.4. Meditating on your own mind as devoid of arising, the actual reality

rang sems skye med bsgom par bya/ /zhes pa'i don/
thugs ka'i 'od kyis snod bcud rang gi lus/ /zhes ba nas/
skye med rigs pas btsal nas mnyam par bzhag /ces pa'i bar te/

This is presented in the line “and meditate on your mind as devoid of arising.” The meaning of this is explained in the following:
The lights from his heart draw forth the world, its inhabitants, my body, the lotus, the ah syllable, the mantra, and the seed syllable. Through reasoning that seeks the nature of my mind and all phenomena, their lack of arising as truly existent, I rest in meditative equipoise.

de yang gsangasnga gas bla med kyi rdzogs rim pa'i lugs bzhin rang nyid rgyal bu rgyan char gsal ba'i lus nang gi dbus drang por rtsa dbu ma khyad chos gsum ldan gyi nang gi snying gar yi dam gsal btab ste ma 'ongs pa na rang nyid 'chi ba'i tshe 'byung ba thim rim gyi rtags 'char ba dang mthun par rjes gzhig gi sdud rim sogs phyi nang gi thabs mkhas la brten na rang sems lhan cig skyes pa'i ye shes myur du skye bas na rang sems hUM yig la zhugs pa bzhin byas te/ hUM las 'od zer dpag tu med pa phyogs bcur 'phros pa snod bcud thams cad la phog pas snod rnams bcud la thims shing / bcud rnams rang nyid rgyal ba mtshor gsal ba la thim par bsam la/ de'i tshe sa chu la thim pa'i rtags smig sgyu lta bu'i snang ba shar ba'i mos pa byed/ rang snying ga'i pad+ma la thim pa'i tshe chu me la thim pa'i rtags du ba lta bu'i snang ba dang / pad+ma a yig la thim pa'i tshe me rlung la thim pa'i rtags mkha' snang me khyer lta bu'i snang ba dang / pad+ma dang a yig rnams yi dam la thim pa'i tshe rlung rnam shes la thim pa'i rtags mar me 'bar ba lta bu'i snang ba dang / yi dam thugs ka'i zla ba la thim pa'i tshe snang ba dkar lam pa/ de sngags 'phreng la thim ba'i tshe mched pa dmar lam pa/ de hrIHyig la thim pa'i tshe nyer thob nag lam pa/ de yang mi dmigs par gyur pa'i tshe thams cad stong pa 'od gsal shar ba'i mos pa bya zhing /

Here, as in the tradition of highest yoga tantra, visualize yourself in the form of a royal prince adorned with ornaments. Inside your body, visualize the central channel stands erect, endowed with its three attributes.[1284] Inside this, at the level of the heart, visualize the meditation deity. Then, akin to the signs that will occur at the time of your death indicating the dissolution of the elements, apply the skillful outer and inner means, such as the process of subsequent dismantling. If you do this, your mind could soon arise as innate wisdom. So imagine your mind has entered the syllable hūṃ, and this hūṃ emits countless beams of light to the ten directions, touching the worlds and their inhabitants. Then imagine the worlds dissolve into the denizens, and the denizens dissolve into yourself in the form of Jinasāgara. At this point, imagine that the mirage-like sign appears, indicative of the earth dissolving into the water element. Next, as you dissolve into the lotus at your heart, imagine that the smoke-like sign appears, indicative of the water dissolving into the fire element. Next, as the lotus dissolves into the letter ah, imagine that the sign like fireflies appears, indicative of the fire dissolving into the wind element. Next, as the letter ah dissolves into the meditation deity, imagine that the sign like a glowing oil lamp appears, indicative of the dissolution of wind into the consciousness. Next, as the meditation deity dissolves into the moon disc at his heart, imagine the white appearance arises; when the moon disc dissolves into the mantra circle, the red increase arises; when it dissolves into the letter hrīḥ, the darkish near attainment arises; and when even this dissolves and becomes imperceptible, imagine that the all-empty clear light dawns.

d.div: [1284] The three attributes are, as identified by the author on page 736, (1) bright and translucent, (2) reddish and gleaming, and (3) straight and standing upright.

f.d: de'i tshe rang gi sems la sogs pa gzugs nas rnam mkhyen bar gyi chos thams cad ming dang brda tsam gyis phar btags nas bzhag pa tsam ma gtogs yul so so'i steng nas rang bzhin gyi bden par grub pa rdul phran tsam yang med de/ bdag las ma yin gzhan las min/ /gnyis las ma yin rgyu med min/[7] /zhes gsungs pa ltar/ rang las rang skye na/ skye ba thug med dang / skye ba don med du 'gyur/ gzhan las skye na me lce las mun pa dang / rdo las myu gu skye bar yang 'gyur/ rang gzhan gnyis ka las skye na ka bum gnyis las ka bum gnyis yin pa skye/ rgyu med pa las skye na nam mkha' las pad+ma skye bar 'gyur ba bcas/ mtha' bzhi skye 'gog gi rigs pa sogs kyis btsal te/ rang 'dogs byed kyi rtog pa la ma bltos par yod par 'dzin pa ltar ma rnyed pas de lta bu med par nges pa na nges shes de nyid kyi steng du bying rgod dang bral bar mnyam par bzhag par bya'o//

At this point, searching via reasoning, such as with the negation of arising from the four possibilities as presented in the lines “Not from itself or from others. . . ,”[1285] establish that everything, including my own mind — from the body aggregate up to omniscience — is nothing but constructs posited by labels and terms, and that not even the tiniest atom exists objectively as truly existent on the part of the things themselves. [588] For if things were to arise from themselves, their arising would be endless and pointless. If, on the other hand, they were to arise from others, darkness could arise from flames and sprouts could arise from pebbles. If things were to arise from both self and others, pillars and vases could arise from things that are both pillars and vases. And if things were to arise from no cause, flowers could arise from the sky. When, after searching in this way, you find that things do not exist as conceived by the mind — that is, as not dependent on their designating thoughts — and you ascertain their nonexistence, rest your mind in equipoise in this very ascertainment, free of laxity and mental excitation.

d.div: [7] sde dge_3824_bstan/ dbu ma/ tsa_slob dpon klu sgrub/ dbu ma rtsa ba shes rab/ rab byed/ 1_sh+loka_3_shog_1_na3
[1285] That is, in the first stanza of Nāgārjuna’s Fundamental Verses (Mūlamadhyamakakārikā), Toh 3824 Tengyur, dbu ma, tsa, 1a3.

f.d: gnyis pa 'chi kha'i nyams len gyi snying po 'pho ba bsgom pa
2.2.2. Transference meditation, the essence of the practice for the time of death
['di ]la bzhi/ sgyu lus tshogs su 'bul ba/ yid kyi 'bral thag bcad pa/ thar pa'i lam chen dbye ba/ rnam shes gyen du 'phang ba'o/ /
This has four parts: offering your body of illusion as a feast, cutting the rope of mind’s attachment, opening the great way to liberation, and shooting your consciousness upward.
[sgyu lus tshogs su 'bul ba ]
2.2.2.1. Offering your body of illusion as a feast

dang po ni/ rang lus mchod sbyin byas nas ni/ /zhes pa'i don/
rang sems yi dam phyir thon bem rig phral/ /zhes pa nas/
bdud rtsis srid zhi'i mgron la mchod sbyin bya/ /zhes pa'i bar te/

The first is presented in the line “Performing the rite of offering your body,” which is explained in the following:
My mind as the deity comes out, separating my body and mind, and inside a skull cup set on a tripod atop fire and wind mandalas, my old body is purified, transformed, and multiplied, and its nectar is offered to the guests of both samsara and nirvana.

de yang gong du rjes gzhig gi sdud rim gyi mthar thams cad stong pa 'od gsal bsgom pa de mthar phyin pa na rdzogs rim pa'i rim pa bzhi pa'i dpe'i 'od gsal 'char zhing / 'od gsal de las ldang ba na phung po rnying pa las go sa logs su ma dag pa'i sgyu lus su ldang la/ de la sgyu lus phyi ldang dang nang ldang gnyis yod pa las 'od gsal las skad cig dang por phung po rnying pa'i snying gar yi dam gyi skur ldang nas skad cig gnyis par phyir thon pa nang ldang yin pas 'dir yang de dang mthun par mnyam gzhag las ldang ba'i skad cig dang por snying gar rang sems yi dam kha sar pANi mtshon gang tsam du ldang la skad cig gnyis par phyir thon te phung po rnying pa la bltas pas che zhing tsho la dkar zhing snum pa zhig tu gyur par bsam la/ de'i mdun du yaM las rlung dkyil sngon po gzhu'i dbyibs can gyi steng du raM las me dkyil dmar po gru gsum pa'i khar mi mgo'i sgyed pu ri rab tsam pa gsum grub par bsam la/ rang sems yi dam gyis phung po rnying pa'i thod pa bkogs te sgyed bu'i steng du bskyon pa rgya stong gsum dang mnyam par gyur pa'i nang du phung po rnying pa bcug ste dum bur gtubs/ me sbar bas zhu zhing khol ba las 'od zer 'phros te phyogs bcu'i rgyal ba sras bcas thams cad kyi thugs kyi byin rlabs thams cad 'od zer sngon po'i rnam par bkug nas thod pa'i nang du thim pas skyon thams cad sbyangs/ gsung gi byin rlabs thams cad 'od zer dmar po'i rnam par thim pas bdud rtsi'i rang bzhin du rtogs par byas/ sku'i byin rlabs thams cad 'od zer dkar po'i rnam par thim pas ji tsam longs spyad kyang mi zad pa'i mang por sbar zhing spel te 'chi ba med pa tshe'i bdud rtsi/ na ba med pa sman gyi bdud rtsi/ zag pa med pa ye shes kyi bdud rtsir gyur par bsam mo//

Earlier, at the end of the subsequent dismantling, you meditated on the clear light, and when it was completed, the illustrative clear light of the fourth stage dawned. When you arise from such clear light, you arise as an impure illusory body — a body that occupies a spatial locus separate from your old body. In general, there are two ways in which an illusory body arises: arising without and arising within. If, in the first instant of clear light, you arise as the meditation deity inside your old body at your heart and then appear outside, this is arising within. Consonant with this, the moment you rise from your meditative equipoise, you arise at your heart in the form of Avalokiteśvara Khasarpāṇi about the size of a thumbnail. Then, the second instant, as you exit your old body and observe it, imagine seeing it as huge, animated, attractive, and gleaming. Visualize in front of it, arising from a yaṃ syllable, a blue bow-shaped wind mandala. Atop this, arising from raṃ, is a triangular fire mandala, and on this is a tripod made of three human heads, each the size of Mount Meru. Imagine that your mind, as the meditation deity, severs the skull off your old body and places it atop the tripod. Inside this skull cup, which is as vast as the billionfold worlds, your body is placed and cut into pieces. [589] Then the fire is lit, and you imagine that [the pieces of your old body] melt and boil and beams of light radiate from this. They draw forth, in the form of blue light rays, the blessings of the heart of all the buddhas and bodhisattvas of the ten directions, which dissolve into the skull cup, purifying all faults. All the blessings of their speech in the form of red light rays dissolve into the skull cup, transforming the content into nectar. All the blessings of their mind in the form of blue light rays dissolve into the skull cup, enhancing the content such that, no matter how much is consumed, it is never exhausted. Imagine that the contents are transformed into longevity nectar of immortality, medicinal nectar of absence of illness, and gnosis nectar of absence of contamination.

de nas rang gi mdun du seng khri pad zla'i gdan la bla ma kha sar pANi/ de'i dbu'i thad du rtsa brgyud kyi bla ma/ thugs ka'i thad du yi dam sangs rgyas/ lte ba'i thad na rim pa bzhin byang sems/ rang rgyal/ nyan thos/ dpa' bo mkha' gro/ chos srung dang bcas pa'i zhi ba'i mgron dang / 'og gi sa gzhir srid pa'i mgron sems can thams cad smug shig ge yod par bsam la/ rang sems yi dam gyi thugs ka nas ka pA la thogs pa'i mkha' 'gro ma dpag tu med pa spros pas bdud rtsi nas lum lum bcus te yar mgron rnams la mchod pa dang / mar mgron rnams la sbyin pa btang bas mgron thams cad dgyes shing tshims nas/ zag med kyi bde stong khyad par can gsar du 'khrungs/ mar mgron rnams kyi sdig sgrib byang nas thugs rje chen por gyur te rang rang gi dag zhing du gshegs/ bdud rtsi'i gzegs ma snod kyi 'jig rten la 'thor bas dag pa'i zhing khams su gyur par bsam mo/ /

Then visualize Guru Khasarpāṇi in front of you on a lotus and a moon disc atop a lion throne. At the level of his head are your root and lineage gurus, at the level of his heart are the meditation deities and buddhas, and at the level of his navel, in their respective order, are the bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, heroes and ḍākinīs, and Dharma protectors. They are your guests from the class of nirvana. On the ground below, imagine your samsaric guests, all sentient beings fully present, a teeming multitude. Then imagine that from the heart of the meditation deity, which is your own mind, countless ḍākinīs emanate holding skull cups, which they use to scoop up nectar as an offering to the exalted guests and as gifts to the unexalted guests [sentient beings]. Imagine that every guest is sated and that an extraordinary level of uncontaminated [gnosis of] bliss and emptiness arises in them. With the negative karma and obscurations of the unexalted guests purified, imagine they all transform into the Great Compassionate Avalokiteśvara and depart to their pure lands. Nectar sprinkles around the universe, transforming it into pure land.

de nas rlung me'i dkyil 'khor sogs bzhugs khri la thim/ yar mgron rnams kyang rim bzhin bsdus te bla ma la thim/ de yang rang la thim pas byin gyis brlabs par bsam zhing mchod bya mchod byed mchod yul thams cad rang bzhin med pa'i don dran par byas la 'khor gsum mi dmigs pa'i rgyas 'debs bya'o//

Next, the element mandalas — wind, fire, and so forth — dissolve into the throne, the exalted guests dissolve one by one into the guru, and he in turn dissolves into you and thus blesses you. Bring to mind how the object to whom you are making the offering, the person who is doing the offering, and what is being offered all lack intrinsic existence, and in this way, seal all three spheres [of the act of offering] as imperceptible.
gnyis pa yid kyi 'brel thag bcad pa ni/
2.2.2.2. Cutting the rope of mind’s attachment

ltos pa thams cad rab spangs te/ /zhes pa'i don/
mi rtag sgyu ma stong nyid dran byas la/ / lus dang longs spyod gnyen gyi 'brel thag bcad/ / ces pa ste/

This is presented in the line “and having discarded all dependencies,” which is explained in the following:
Recalling impermanence, illusion, and emptiness, I sever the ties with my body, wealth, and loved ones,

'chi ba mi rtag pa dran nas lus 'di la chags kyang rang dbang med par 'dor dgos tshul bsams nas lus kyi 'brel thag bcad/ longs spyod rnams la chags kyang rdzas sngags kyis bslad pa'i sgyu ma'i rta glang dang 'dra ste/ ser snas gsog du ma la 'bad kyang gson pa'i tshe yang longs spyod pa'i cha med na 'chi tshe rdul phran tsam yang 'khyer dbang ga la yod/ da lta chags zhen drag pos sdig sdug gtam ngan khyad du bsad nas bsags pa'i 'bras bu sdug bsngal ni lus dang grib ma bzhin mi 'bral bar nges par myong dgos na snying po med pa'i sgro btags kyi longs spyod la chags pas ci bya snyam du longs spyod kyi 'brel thag bcad/ gnyen bshes rnams la chags kyang yid du 'ong bar sgro btags tsam las ngo bos grub pa rdul tsam yang med pas yid brtan mi rung ste/ da lta gnyen du bzungs kyang tshe rabs mang por dgra'i gtso bor gyur nas 'thab cing bsad pa grangs las 'das te dgra gnyen du 'gyur ba dang / gnyen dgrar 'gyur bas nges pa ci yang med/ mthar gcig gis gcig bor te mthong thos med par 'gyur ba gdon mi za bas 'di la chags pas ci bya snyam du gnyen gyi 'brel thag bcad par bya zhing mdor bsdun mi rtag pa sogs re res kyang lus longs spyod gnyen bshes thams cad kyi 'brel thag bcad par bya ste/ de ma chod na bya nam mkhar 'phur ba la rkang pa rdo la btags pa dang 'dra bas gnad che'o//

Recalling death and impermanence, contemplate how, despite your attachment to your body, you will have to discard it with no say on your part, [590] and then cut the rope tying [your mind] to the body. Though you may feel attached to your material resources, they are like the illusory horses and elephants conjured from magical substances and incantations. Thus you may pursue numerous strategies to accumulate wealth, but you do not even have much of a chance to enjoy it when you are living. And if this is true, what power do you have to bring even an atom’s worth of your wealth with you when you die? Indeed, the negative consequences from accumulating your wealth through strong attachment and clinging, braving even disrepute — these you will definitely have to experience, for they are inseparable from you, like a body and its shadow. So contemplate, “What is the point of being attached to meaningless wealth, whose import is a conceptual fiction?” When it comes to your attachment to family and friends, their appeal is also constructed by your mind, for not even an atom exists essentially, in its own right. Thus it’s illogical to believe in their certainty. You hold them to be friends at present, but they have been your arch enemies in numerous lives, and the number of times they have attacked and even killed you is incalculable. An enemy can turn into a friend, and a friend can become an enemy. There is no certainty whatsoever. In any case, everyone will forsake everyone in the end, scattering, never to see or hear one other again. This is inevitable. So contemplate, “What is the point of being attached?” and cut the rope tying [your mind] to all your family and friends. If you do not cut your ties, you will be like the bird trying to fly whose foot is tethered to a rock. This point is critical.
gsum pa thar pa'i lam chen dbye ba ni/
2.2.2.3. Opening the great way to liberation

'od kyi sbu gu'i sbyor pa yis/ /zhes pa'i don/
rang gi lus dbus dbu ma'i snying nang du/ /zhes pa nas/
'od zer sbubs byung rang gi spyi bor zug /ces pa ste/

This is presented in the line “through the medium of a hollow light beam,” which is explained in the following:
And inside my body, at the heart inside the central channel, appears a Khasarpāṇi the size of a thumbnail.
Maitreya, gold in color and seated in the bhadra posture, resides above in Tuṣita, in Yiga Chözin [courtyard]. As I appeal to this savior, from his heart emerges a hollow light beam that pierces my crown.

rang gi lus nang gi dbus drang por rtsa dbu ma phyi sngo dang dmar khyad chos gsum ldan te gsal la dwangs pa/ dmar la snum pa/ drang la 'drongs pa sba lcag 'bring po tsam mar sne sbrul 'jug ltar bug pa med pa lte 'og sor bzhi tsam nas je sbom du song ba'i yar sna spyi bo'i tshangs bug dang mnyam pa bu ga har re yod pa'i snying ga'i thad kyi dbu ma'i nang du rang gi shin tu phra ba'i rlung sems kyi ngo bo kha sar pANi mtshon gang tsam zhig gsal gdab/ 'di nas byang phyogs su ri rab kyi thad steng phyogs kyi nam mkhar lha'i gnas dga' ldan zhes bya ba na rje btsun byams pa mgon po'i bzhugs gnas rgyal mtshan mthon po zhes bya ba'i mdun sar rje btsun chos gsung ba'i gnas yid dga' chos 'dzin bya bar rje btsun byams pa mgon po sku gser gyi mdog can zhal gcig phyag gnyis chos 'khor gyi phyag rgya can skal ldan gyi gdul bya mtha' yas pa la chos gsung bzhin pa/ zhal rang cag la phyogs pa'i tshul gyis bzhugs pa la bdag dga' ldan gyi zhing khams der drang du gsol zhes 'dun pa drag po yid la bsam pas gsol ba btab pa na/ rje btsun gyi thugs ka nas 'od kha dog ser ba sbubs can zhig nar gyis byung ba rang gi tshang bug la thal gyis zug par bsam mo//

Visualize that inside your body, toward the center, is the central channel, blue outside, red inside, and endowed with the three attributes: it is (1) bright and translucent, (2) reddish and gleaming, and (3) straight and standing upright. It’s about the size of a medium bamboo stick, and its lower part is closed like a snake tail. The channel starts to broaden about four finger-widths below your navel; its upper opening is flush with your crown aperture and wide open. Inside your central channel, at your heart, visualize a Khasarpāṇi the size of a thumbnail; he is the nature of your very subtle wind-mind. Then imagine that to the north, in the space above Mount Meru in the heavenly realm of Tuṣita, is Maitreya’s residence, known as the Towering Banner. At this site is the place where Maitreya teaches, called Yiga Chözin (Joyous Mind, Upholding Dharma). [591] Imagine that Maitreya is present there, with his golden body and one face, his two hands in the gesture of turning the wheel of Dharma, and he is teaching his countless disciples. His face turned toward you, supplicate, “Pray bring me to the pure land of Tuṣita.” As you make this appeal forcefully with fervent yearning, imagine that a hollow beam of yellow light emerges from Maitreya’s heart and visibly pierces your crown.
bzhi pa rnam shes gyen du 'phang ba ni/
2.2.2.4. Shooting your consciousness upward

sems ni dga' ldan gnas su 'phang / /zhes pa'i don/
'du shes gsum ldan lcags kyus ral pa la/ /zhes pa nas/
'chi dus mdun gyi pad+mor skye ba len/ /zhes pa'i bar te/

This is presented in the line “I’ll send my mind to the Tuṣita realm,” which is explained in the following:
With the three thoughts, I am pulled from my topknot by a hook and become fused inseparably with Maitreya’s mind; during training I return, and my crown aperture is sealed. After death, may I be reborn like a new lotus flower in his presence.
