de nas rang sems yi dam gyis dbu ma'i nang nas yar bltas pas rje btsun gyi thugs ka gser gyi maN+Dal phyis pa lta bu lug gis [8] mthong bas 'od ser po sbubs can de la lam gyi 'du shes dang / rang nyid lam de la 'gro ba'i 'du shes dang / song nas byams mgon gyi thugs dang rang sems dbyer med bsre ba'i 'du shes gsum dang ldan zhing / slar yang rje btsun gyi thugs ka nas 'od zer dmar po rtse la lcags kyu'i dbyibs can zhig sbu gu'i nang nas mar nar gyis byung ba rang sems yi dam gyi ral pa'i thor tshugs la lcags kyu btab ste drangs par bsams la/ hig ces brjod pas rje btsun gyi thugs dang dbyer med du 'dres te bde stong gi ngang du cung zad bzhag /da lta sbyong dus thugs ka nas thon pa rang gi snying gar phab la yang sngar bzhin spor ba sogs thun rer bdun nam nyer gcig sogs byas te thun grol ba na snying gar phab rjes rje btsun gyi thugs ka nas 'od ser po de dbu ma'i nang gang zhing / khyad par tshangs bug 'od ser po dga' 'khyil lta bus legs par bkag pas tshe 'phel bar bsam mo/ /

As your mind, in the form of meditation deity, looks upward through the central channel, it sees clearly Maitreya’s heart, resplendent like a gold mandala base wiped until shining. You develop three recognitions: (1) the hollow yellow beam as the path, (2) yourself traveling on that path, and (3) having traveled, your mind inseparably fused with Maitreya’s heart. Once again, imagine that a red light shaped like a hook extends from Maitreya’s heart through the hollow [yellow] beam and grabs your mind as meditation deity’s topknot, pulling the deity upward. As you shout hik! you imagine that it becomes fused inseparably with Maitreya’s heart. Then rest for a little while in bliss and emptiness. While training in this, you should imagine bringing your mind as meditation deity back from Maitreya’s heart, down to your own heart, and then shoot it back again. You can repeat this process seven or up to twenty-one times during a session. When concluding the session, bring it back to your own heart. Then imagine your central channel is filled with the yellow light from Maitreya’s heart, and your crown aperture is sealed by a disc of light formed by swirling lines, enhancing your longevity.

d.div: [8] lug gis mthong zhes pa 'di phal cher yig nor tu snang na'ang rang sor bzhag

f.d: 'chi ba'i dus su 'od kyi sbu gu yang rje btsun gyi thugs kar thim par bsam la bde stong la mnyam par 'jog pa chos sku'i 'pho ba dang / slar thugs ka nas kha sar pANi'i rnam par thon pa rje btsun gyi mdun ngos su pad+ma'i sdong po 'dab ma stong ldan gyi lte bar thim pas 'dab ma kha zum par bsam pa longs sku'i 'pho ba dang / rje btsun gyi thugs ka nas 'od zer 'phros pas pad+ma kha phye ste lha'i bu rnam dpyod dang ldan pa zhig tu skyes te rje btsun gyi zhal mthong zhing chos thos par bsam pa ni sprul sku'i 'pho ba'o//

At the time of death, imagine that even the hollow beam dissolves back into Maitreya’s heart, and rest in equipoise on bliss and emptiness. This is the dharmakāya aspect of transference. Again, imagine from Maitreya’s heart emerges a Khasarpāṇi, who dissolves into the hub of a thousand-petal lotus in front of Maitreya, making the lotus fold all its petals. This is the saṃbhogakāya aspect of transference. Again, beams of light emerge from Maitreya’s heart, opening the petals of the lotus. Imagine you are reborn inside in the form of a heavenly child with a discerning intellect [592] who can see Maitreya and hear his Dharma teachings. This is the nirmāṇakāya aspect of transference.
gsum pa bar do'i nyams len gyi snying po bsre ba bsgom pa ni/
2.2.3. The mixings, essence of the practice for the intermediate state

'di nyid bar dor shes byas la/ / zhes pa nas/
mkhas pas nying mtshams sbyar bar bya/ / zhes pa'i bar gyi don/

This is presented in the lines:
Recognizing this as the bardo itself and transforming the outer, inner, and secret through the yoga of emptiness and compassion, the wise connect to the new birth.
These lines are explained in the following:

'chi kha'i yul snang bar dor mos pa sogs/ /zhes pa nas/
dag snang dang bcas bsam bzhin skye ba len/ /zhes pa'i bar te/

d.div: Imagining the perceptions at dying as those of the intermediate state, through wind, intention, and aspiration, I will recognize the bardo [as bardo], and I will view the world as a pure land, beings as deities, and all as devoid of true existence and illusion-like.
Preventing attachment and aversion with emptiness and compassion, I will with pure perception take birth through my own will.

f.d: 'di la 'khrid yig rnams su mi gsal yang bar do'i bsre skor nyams su len pa la da lta nas rmi lam 'dzin pa ni bar do'i tshad 'dzin yin pas rmi lam zin na bar do ngos zin nas bsre skor nyams su len nus par 'gyur gyis ngos ma zin bar bsre skor mi 'byung bas na dang por rmi lam zin pa'i thabs ni/ nyin bar gyi snang ba thams cad rmi lam yin snyam du yang yang dran par bya zhing / nub re bzhin nyal khar rmi lam zin par bla ma dkon mchog la gsol 'debs shugs drag dang / gnyid du 'gro khar rmi lam byung na ngos zin pa zhig bya snyam du 'dun pa gtong ba dang / mgrin par pad+ma dmar po'i lte bar oM gyi mthar a nu t+tAr zhes pa'i sngags 'phreng mdun nas g.yas bskor du bkod pa la sems gtad de nyal ba sogs kyi thabs byas la/ gnyid chos sku dang bsre ba/ rmi lam longs sku dang bsre ba/ sad pa sprul sku dang bsre ba rnams kyang nyams su blang bar bya'o/ /

Although it is not explicitly mentioned in the guide texts, to practice the mixings associated with the intermediate state (bardo), one way to measure your present capacity to recognize the bardo as the bardo is to recognize your dreams as dreams. For if you can recognize dreams as dreams [through practicing lucid dreaming], you will be able to recognize the bardo as the bardo and do the mixings. Without such a recognition, no such rounds of mixing can take place. So here is the method to recognize dreams as dreams. On going to bed, make fervent supplications to your gurus and the Three Jewels to be able to recognize dreams as dreams. Just as you are on the threshold of sleep, set an intention to recognize your dreams as dreams. You could also try visualizing, on the hub of a red lotus at your throat, an oṃ syllable encircled by the letters of the mantra anuttara, the letters starting at the front and going clockwise. Rest your mind on this mantra and go to sleep. In this way, you could practice mixing the sleeping state with dharmakāya, the dreaming state with saṃbhogakāya, and the waking state with nirmāṇakāya.

dngos gzhi bar do'i nyams len ni/ spyir da lta'i snang ba dang khyad par 'chi kha'i yul snang thams cad bar do yin snyam pa dang / gzhan yang rlung stobs dang bar do la bar dor ngos zin par bya'o snyam pa 'dun pa'i stobs dang / bar do ngos zin par shog cig/ ces smon lam dang gsol 'debs shugs drag bya zhing / de'i mthus bar do shar ba na bar dor ngos zin pa 'byung la/ de byung ba na snod kyi 'jig rten thams cad dag pa'i zhing khams yin snyam du bsgom pa ni phyi bsgyur ba dang / bcud kyi sems can thams cad yi dam thugs rje chen po yin snyam du bsgom pa nang bsgyur ba dang de kun kyang ming dang rtog pas btags pa tsam las bden par grub pa rdul tsam yang med snyam du lta ba'i rtsis zin ni gsang ba bsgyur ba yin no/ /

The actual practice of the intermediate state is the following. Whatever appearances you have in general, and whatever appearances you experience at death in particular, view them as part of the intermediate state. Furthermore, fervently pray and supplicate that, through the power of wind yoga or through the power of your intention to recognize the bardo as the bardo, you may be able to recognize the intermediate state. By virtue of these, the bardo can be recognized as the bardo. When this occurs, transformation of the outer occurs when you meditate on the entire world as a perfect buddha realm; transformation of the inner occurs when you meditate on all sentient beings, the denizens, as the meditation deity Great Compassionate One; and transformation of the secret occurs when you contemplate that all of these are mere conceptual designations, with not even an atom possessing true existence.

de lta bu'i bsre skor nyams su len nus nas rang nyid dag pa'i zhing khams gang mos su 'pho ba'am/ yang na lam gyi lhag ma rnams nyams su len pa'i rten khyad par can snyigs dus kyi tshe thung gcig la sangs rgyas sgrub nus pa 'dzam bu gling pa'i mi mngal skyes khams drug ldan du skye ba len na pha ma nyal po byed pa mthong ba dang rten pho lus su skye na pha la sdang zhing ma la chags pa dang / mo lus su skye na ma la sdang zhing pha la chags par gsungs bas de'i tshe rang bzhin med pa'i stong nyid dran la chags pa bkag/ snying rje chen po bskyed de zhe sdang dgag dgos shing / spyir snying rje la spyi don dang sbas don dang mthar thug gi snying rje gsum yod la/

When you can practice such rounds of mixing [593], you will be able to either transport yourself to your desired pure land or take rebirth in a bodily existence conducive to continuing on your path, such as a human existence of this degenerate age that allows you to attain buddhahood in a single lifetime. If you are about to take birth as a human being and gain a body composed of six elements, it is said that as you witness your future parents in copulation, if you are to take birth as a male, you will experience anger toward your father and attachment toward your mother. If, in contrast, you are to take birth as a female, you will experience anger toward your mother and attachment toward your father. At that point, then, you need to prevent the arising of attachment by recalling the emptiness of intrinsic existence and prevent the arising of anger by generating compassion.

spyi don snying rje ni snying rje spyi tsam dang / sbas don gyi snying rje ni sems dben dpe'i 'od gsal dang / mthar thug gi snying rje ni don gyi 'od gsal yin pas 'dir spyi don gyi snying rjes zhe sdang dgag dgos la/ de tsam du ma zad pha spyan ras gzigs rgyal ba rgya mtsho sku mdog dkar po dang / ma gsang ba ye shes sku mdog dmar mor bsam pa sogs dag pa'i snang ba dang bcas pas sems can gyi don bya bar 'dod pa'i 'dun pas bsam bzhin du skye ba blang bar bya'o//

Generally speaking, there are three distinct levels of meaning of the word compassion — the general meaning, the hidden meaning, and the ultimate meaning. Compassion at the level of general meaning refers to what we normally understand by it; at the level of hidden meaning compassion refers to the illustrative clear light of mind isolation; and at the level of ultimate meaning compassion refers to the actual clear light. Here, you prevent the arising of anger through compassion as understood in terms of the level of general meaning. Also you take rebirth through the perception of pure appearances, such as that of white Avalokiteśvara Jinasāgara and his red consort Guhyajñānā, and with the intention to bring about sentient beings’ welfare.
gsum pa don bsdu ba ni/
2.3. Concluding summary

gang shar ngos 'dzin lta ba'i gnad/ / ces pa nas/
grub thob chen po'i gdams pa'o/ / zhes pa'i bar gyi don/
lta sgom spyod pa'i gnad dang ldan pa yi/ / grub chen mi tra'i gdams pa 'khrul med yin/ / zhes pa ste/

d.div: Endowed with the key points of view, meditation, and action, this is the flawless instruction of the great siddha Mitrayogi.

f.d: mnyam gzhag gi skabs su gong gi nyams len thams cad la lta bas rtsis zin par bya ba dang / blo ngor gang shar thams cad bden grub tu 'dzin pa'i dgag bya ngos zin par byas nas bden 'dzin 'gog pa lta ba'i gnad/ bden med kyi nges shes byung ba na bying rgod dang bral bar skyong ba'i 'dris su 'jug pa sgom pa'i gnad/ rjes thob sgyu ma lta bu'i nyams len gyi skabs su stong nyid kyi nges shes chung du song ba na bden med kyi nges shes dran par byas te chos thams cad gnas tshul stong pa nyid kyi ngang du ro snyoms par lta ba ni spyod pa'i gnad yin pas/ lta sgom spyod pa'i nyams len gyi gnad 'gag dang ldan pa 'di ni grub pa che 'bring chung gsum brnyes pa'i skyes bu dam pa mi tra dz+wa ki zhes bya ba'i gdams pa dam pa bar ma chad rgyud pa las [9] brgyud pa'i 'khrul pa med pa yin no//

This is the key point of the view: ensure that all your practices during meditative equipoise are held fast by the glue of the view [of emptiness] and negate the true existence of whatever appears to your mind by recognizing the object of negation. This is the key point of meditation: when ascertainment of the absence of true existence arises, cultivate familiarity with it, maintaining it free of mental laxity and excitation. And this is the key point of action: during post-equipoise, when the force of your ascertainment of emptiness weakens, recall your ascertainment of the absence of true existence and view all phenomena as the equal taste of emptiness. This [teaching] endowed with the key points of view, meditation, and action is an unmistaken instruction of Mitrayogi — a sublime master who has attained the small, medium, and great siddhis — transmitted through an uninterrupted lineage of excellent beings. [594]

d.div: [9] ma dper dam pa bar ma brgyud pa las brgyud pa'i zhes byung yang dam pa bar ma chad pa las brgyud pa'i zhes yin nges pas de bzhin du bcos/

f.d: gsum pa mjug gi bya ba
3. The third, concluding activities,
['di ]la gnyis/ dge ba bsngo ba dang / rtsom pa mthar phyin pa'i bya ba'o/ /
is twofold: dedicating the virtue and successfully completing the composition.
[dge ba bsngo ba ]
3.1. [dedicating the virtue]

dang po ni/
'dis mtshon dge bas tshe rabs thams cad du/ / zhes pa nas/
bstan 'gro mgon gyi dpal du bdag gyur cig / ces pa'i bar ro//

The first is presented in the following:
Through the virtue of deeds such as these, may I be cared for in all lives by Guru Padmapāṇi, and by perfecting the practices of this life, death, and the bardo, may I become a glory to the teaching and all beings.
gnyis pa rtsom pa mthar phyin pa'i bya ba ni/
3.2. The second, successfully completing the composition,

tshul 'di rnam dpyod spyan yangs slob ma'i ngor/ / zhes pa nas/
mi nyams phyogs brgyar yun du rgyus gyur cig /sarba dza ga taM/ zhes pa'i bar te go sla'o zhes gsungs/

is presented in the following:
This was written for disciples with the open eyes of intellect by Dharmabhadra, who takes the form of a monk. Through this virtue, may this instruction, the essence of sutras and tantras, never degenerate but flourish always in a hundred directions.
The meaning of these lines is easy to understand, the teacher said.[1286]

d.div: [1286] Given that this text was compiled on the basis of notes taken at a live teaching of Ngulchu Dharmabhadra, “the teacher” here refers to this master.

f.d:
smras pa/
mi mjed zhing gi ston pa zas gtsang sras/ / bskal bzang rnam 'dren khrod nas byon pa bzhin/ / deng dus 'gro mgon d+harma b+ha dra'i zhabs/ / rgyal kun mkhyen brtse'i klong nas byon pa nges/ /
gang gi thugs rje tshad med dbyar rnga'i sgras/ / zab dang rgya che'i chu 'dzin nyer bskul nas/ / snying po'i mchog gyur gdams pa'i char phabs pa/ / thar 'dod myu gu'i gsos gyur 'di rmad byung / /
de phyir rgyun 'khyer mdor bsdus grub chen gyi/ / zhal lung gsal bar byed pa'i me long 'di/ / rang dang skal mnyam gzhan la'ang phan 'dod blos/ / bkod pas 'gro kun 'phags pas rjes 'dzin shog /

Thus I say:
Son of Śuddhodana, Teacher of this hard-to-tame realm, just as you emerged from among the saviors of the fortunate eons, O Dharmabhadra, the lord of today’s beings, it is certain that you emerged from the sphere of buddhas’ wisdom and compassion.
The monsoon thunder of your boundless compassion has stirred up the clouds of profound and vast teachings, causing the rainfall of this instruction of the utmost essence to nourish the shoots of aspirants’ liberation — a great wonder.
Therefore this mirror reflecting the sacred words of the great siddha in the format of a daily practice I have inscribed with the thought that it may help myself and others. May all beings be sustained by Ārya Avalokiteśvara.
Colophon

ces snying po don gsum gyi zin bris grub chen zhal lung gsal ba'i me long zhes bya ba 'di yang / bdag cag rnams la bka' drin mtshungs pa med cing mkhas shing grub pa'i go 'phang brnyes pa rje btsun dngul chu pa chen po d+ha_rma b+ha dra zhes mkhas mang rgyu skar gyi dbus na nyi zla dang mtshungs pa'i bdag nyid chen pos me phag hor zla dgu pa'i dkar phyogs kyi rgyal ba gsum pa'i nyin skal ldan gyi gdul bya mang por lugs 'di'i rtsa tshig 'dzin chos dang 'brel ba'i zab 'khrid stsal ba'i skabs su/ mgon po gang gi bka' 'bangs kyi char gtogs rje drung tshe ring ming can gyis rang nyid dran pa gso ba dang / blo dman gzhan la'ang phan pa'i bsam pas brjed byang zin bris su bgyis pa dza yan+tu// //

These notes on the Three Essential Points, entitled A Mirror Reflecting the Mahāsiddha’s Sacred Words, were compiled from the profound guidance on the root text of this instruction as well as on the recitation verse by the most revered Dharmabhadra, the great Ngulchupa, who has attained the status of high learning and meditative realization and who stands out from among the assembly of great learned ones like the sun or moon among the heavenly constellations. The master gave this teaching to a large group of disciples on the third day of the third month (April 29, 1827) and during the waxing moon of the ninth month of the fire-pig year (October 23, 1827), and I, bearing the name Jedrung Tsering, who is counted among the community of his disciples, compiled these notes to help refresh my own memory and thinking it might benefit others whose knowledge is less advanced.
